item.title: Winners and Losers From AI Agents
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Winners and Losers From AI Agents
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
Winners and Losers From AI Agents
Key Takeaways
An estimated $30 trillion in consumer spending could be digitized through agentic AI offerings across multiple industries.
As AI agents increasingly influence purchasing decisions, operational efficiency, pricing and digital capabilities may become more important than traditional advantages such as brand recognition.
AI agents could make it easier for consumers to compare products and services, intensifying competition in industries such as insurance, auto retail and ticket resale.
By simplifying discovery, booking and transactions, AI agents could increase the use of software for such industries as transportation, local services and insurance.
Established retailers with trusted customer relationships, competitive prices and reliable delivery networks may be better positioned to withstand disruption.
The recent launch of powerful consumer AI agents has reignited debate over how artificial intelligence could disrupt industries ranging from retail and insurance to transportation and live entertainment.
Unlike traditional AI tools that primarily answer questions, these agents can browse websites, complete forms, compare prices, make purchases and even help negotiate bills.
Morgan Stanley Research estimates that roughly $30 trillion in consumer spending could be digitized through AI agents across online advertising, e-commerce, travel, food delivery, ridesharing, logistics, wearables and other sectors.
The extent of the disruption will depend on how quickly consumers adopt AI agents and how effectively companies make money from agent-driven activity and transactions.
“We continue to believe leading tech platforms with broad-based reach and unique data sets are in advantaged positions to create unique consumer agentic offerings that drive utility and garner scaled adoption,” says Brian Nowak, head of U.S. Internet Research at Morgan Stanley.
For investors, the implications vary widely by industry. While AI agents could increase demand for certain services and make transaction more efficient, they could also intensify price competition, weaken traditional advantages in winning customers and shift advertising revenue toward new platforms.

item.title: AI Investing After the Midterms Dip
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
AI Investing After the Midterms Dip
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
AI Investing After the Midterms Dip
Key Takeaways
The selloff in AI-related stocks after the U.S. midterms appeared overdone, and markets have since recovered some of the losses; and further volatility could create potential buying opportunities.
Some data center projects scheduled for 2028 could move to 2029, potentially supporting a smoother rebalance between supply and demand across the supply chain.
Morgan Stanley Research maintains its forecasts for hyperscaler capital spending of $1.6 trillion in 2028 and $1.8 trillion in 2029.
Financing could become more selective, with increasing importance given to tenant quality, access to power and contractual protections.
The main investment opportunities after the selloff include the hyperscalers, select data center supply chain companies, software enablers and AI adopters.
Equity markets, particularly technology stocks, fell sharply in the days after the U.S. midterm elections. Democrats’ sizable advantage in both the House and Senate, alongside gains in several governors’ races, raised investor questions about the outlook for data center construction, the technology investment cycle and global equities. Markets have since recovered some of the losses from that initial post-election selloff.
However, Morgan Stanley Research believes the selloff was an overreaction. Should there be further volatility, investors can look for opportunities among AI enablers, infrastructure providers and companies adopting the technology.
The election results are more likely to delay some data center projects from 2028 to 2029 than derail the broader capital investment cycle. This has potential to elongate the AI spending cycle, which could bring a smoother rebalancing of supply and demand across the data center supply chain, an improved credit outlook and higher lease rates for computing capacity.
More than 20 Morgan Stanley Research teams globally assessed how the new U.S. political landscape could affect data center development, policy and equity investment opportunities across the U.S., Asia and Europe.
1. Data Center Buildout Delayed, Not Derailed
Newly elected governors are unlikely to disrupt projects already under construction, leaving the outlook for 2027 projects unchanged. However, some data centers scheduled for completion in Texas and Ohio in 2028 could be delayed until 2029 as incoming governors work with legislators to establish new requirements for developers.
Morgan Stanley Research has shifted 20% of its projected 2028 data center capacity to 2029, while maintaining a positive view of the overall buildout. Globally, the revised forecast implies growth in data center capacity of 9% in 2028 and 20% in 2029.
Potential U.S. delays could also create attractive opportunities for data center development outside the country.
2. AI Capital Spending Forecast Stays on Track
Hyperscalers—the major technology companies providing cloud computing, storage and networking services—are likely to continue spending and building as much capacity as possible to develop and scale new products for billions of users. The reason is simple: AI investment continues to offer an estimated return on invested capital of more than 30%.
Morgan Stanley Research maintains its forecasts for hyperscaler capital spending of $1.6 trillion in 2028 and $1.8 trillion in 2029.
These companies are also likely to shift some development to states with more favorable policies toward data centers, including Tennessee and Louisiana.
3. Financing Remains Available But Selective
With capital spending forecasts unchanged, AI-related debt issuance is likely to remain high in 2027, led by the hyperscalers.
However, financing for new construction and specialized AI cloud providers, known as neoclouds, could face greater scrutiny. Tenant quality, a credible path to securing power and contractual protections will likely become increasingly important.
W
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Wall Street is cooling on Jensen Huang's Nvidia
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Wall Street is cooling on Jensen Huang's Nvidia
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
Wall Street is cooling on Jensen Huang's Nvidia — but history says don't give up on the stock just yet
Breaking up with Nvidia (NVDA) is hard to do. After the stock dropped 25%, two of Wall Street's biggest banks pulled it from their top-pick lists, and neither could bring itself to say "sell" — yet.
Morgan Stanley's version was the most polite: It's not you, it's our stop-loss policy. The bank removes any top pick that falls more than 25% from where it was named, and Nvidia had slid a bit more since getting the title on Oct. 2. Only a day earlier, Bank of America cut Nvidia, Micron (MU) and Lam Research (LRCX) from its US 1 List of best ideas. Both banks still rate Nvidia a Buy.
Others were less gentle. Baird cut the stock to Neutral on Wednesday and slashed its price target to $200 from $500, citing rising odds of a CEO change. Aletheia Capital downgraded Nvidia to Hold on Monday. Mizuho, Citi, and Wells Fargo trimmed their price targets in the days after reports tied CEO Jensen Huang to a suspected Chinese spy.
Still, nobody is packing Nvidia's things into a box. Of 82 analysts who rate the stock, 77 call it a Buy, according to Bloomberg data.
The average price target sits about 87% above where the stock closed Tuesday. That's the widest gap between the two measures in two years of monthly readings, because the stock fell and the targets mostly stayed put.
Wall Street's reluctance to get bearish on Nvidia has history on its side, mostly.
Nvidia has closed 25% below a record 13 times since its 1999 IPO. A year later, it was higher in nine of them, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
The exceptions were brutal. After drops in 2001, 2002, and 2007, the stock lost more than half its value again over the next 12 months. It's also a small sample, and half of it comes from the dot-com boom and bust, when Nvidia was a fraction of today's $4 trillion giant.
Even Bank of America's own strategist isn't giving up on the bigger AI story. "It's paramount for the US to remain number one in terms of tech primacy. And that's where I see almost a put on the ... tech story," Savita Subramanian, BofA's head of US equity and quantitative strategy, told Yahoo Finance on Tuesday — though she didn't discuss the list change itself.
Analysts have been right lately. Every average target set from November 2024 through November 2025 was reached within a year, according to Yahoo Finance analysis of Bloomberg data.
And Nvidia is no longer priced for perfection. It trades at about 11 times next fiscal year's expected earnings, per Yahoo Finance calculations, versus about 18 times for the S&P 500 (^GSPC), according to FactSet.
Every one of the 69 price targets sits above Tuesday's close, even the lone Sell, Seaport's $180.
The bigger question is who runs the company
As of Wednesday morning, Polymarket traders saw a better than 1 in 4 chance that Nvidia would announce Huang's exit by the end of March.
Venture capitalist Vinod Khosla approves of the board's first move. "Starting with an independent investigation is exactly the right thing to do," he said on Yahoo Finance's "Deirdre Bosa Live" on Tuesday.
Dan Niles of Niles Investment Management, who told Yahoo Finance on Monday that he has known Huang for 30 years, isn't worried about the personal side: "Would you want a drunkard and a womanizer leading you in World War II? Answer is absolutely. That was Winston Churchill."
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Follow Jared Blikre on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com.

item.title: Utah-Based Startup Raises 500 Million for Modular AI Data Center
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Utah-Based Startup Raises 500 Million for Modular AI Data Center
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
Utah-Based Startup Raises $500 Million for Modular AI Data Center
(Bloomberg) -- Torus, an energy-storage startup, said it raised $500 million in funding to help launch a new shipping container-sized product that combines batteries with artificial-intelligence computing.
The Series C round was led by Magnetar with participation from investors including Iconiq Capital, Origin Ventures and Trinity Capital, Salt Lake City-based Torus said in a statement. The funds will support manufacturing of the company's new product, called Foundry. Hydra Host, an AI infrastructure company, is among the customers, Torus said.
Torus founder and Chief Executive Officer Nate Walkingshaw said in an interview that the computing containers can be installed at businesses or factories where grids have excess power capacity. That can help avoid expensive infrastructure upgrades that put pressure on utility bills. The units, which specialize in AI inference tasks, range in size from one to 20 megawatts and can be installed within four months, he said.
The product launch comes as data-center developers in the US race to find enough power to run energy-intensive AI applications. Developers seeking to build sprawling campuses that can draw as much electricity as a city face the prospect of greater scrutiny and longer timelines in states, including Texas and Ohio, where Democrats who campaigned for tighter restrictions on data centers won governors' races in last week's midterm elections.
Torus has been selling modular battery systems that help businesses and factories manage their energy use and reduce power bills. The shifting political landscape provides an opening for companies that can offer computing power without jacking up electricity bills or adding to local noise or pollution, Walkingshaw said.
"The Foundry product is our version of a distributed data-center approach to move the chips to the power that's already there," he said.

item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
How cuts to what Medicare pays doctors could hit retirees
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
How cuts to what Medicare pays doctors could hit retirees
One of the big selling points of traditional Medicare is there are no restrictions on which doctors you can see for your care.
Medicare Advantage plans, the alternative to traditional Medicare offered through private companies, on the other hand, often have a limited network of providers that are ever-changing.
But newly announced cuts to the rates Medicare pays doctors could pose a problem for patients no matter which program they're in.
Last week, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) announced cuts to Medicare payments to physicians for 2027. In 2027, Medicare will trim 2.3% off the baseline rate used to calculate payments to doctors.
"Any cut to primary care payments puts practices at risk, worsens physician shortages, and could make it harder for Medicare patients to see their doctor when they need to," Kisha Davis, president of the American Academy of Family Physicians, told Yahoo Finance.
Under the changes, when an office visit and minor procedure occur on the same day, CMS will reduce payment by 20% for the lower-cost service. The most expensive service, for example, a surgical procedure, would be paid at 100% and all other procedures on the same day would be paid at 80%.
Physicians are not required to participate in Medicare, though the majority of them do.
Medicare payments to physicians are already lower, on average, than payments from private insurers and are not automatically indexed to keep pace with inflation in medical practice costs, according to KFF.
Medicare physician payments fell 33% from 2001 to 2025 when adjusted for inflation, even as practice expenses keep climbing, according to an analysis by the American Medical Association.
The Medicare Economic Index (MEI), which tracks practice cost inflation, jumped 60% during that same period, according to the AMA.
"Imagine going 20 years without a raise while the cost of running your practice, keeping your staff and buying equipment keeps rising," Davis said. "For some practices, a further cut could mean closing their doors, and for patients, longer waits for appointments and fewer options for care close to home."
The impact doesn't stop at Medicare, she added. Tricare, state Medicaid agencies, and many other insurers base their payments on the Medicare physician fee schedule.
"Medicare should reward clinicians for keeping people healthy," HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. said in a statement. "We are putting prevention and primary care at the center of Medicare, closing payment loopholes, and cracking down on waste … changing what Medicare pays for to change what our health system delivers."
For now, seniors don't need to panic that their doctor is suddenly going to cancel appointments because of the scaled-back payment schedule. But the payment squeeze does have potential ramifications for some patients if their favorite physician chooses to limit the number of Medicare patients they accept. It's impossible to predict that at this stage.

item.title: Blackstone Aims to Raise $3 Billion for Real Estate Secondaries
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Blackstone Aims to Raise $3 Billion for Real Estate Secondaries
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
Blackstone Aims to Raise $3 Billion for Real Estate Secondaries
(Bloomberg) -- Blackstone Inc. is pitching a fund that will snap up stakes in other asset managers' real estate vehicles, expecting to raise at least $3 billion amid a prolonged need for liquidity in the sector.
Strategic Partners, the firm's secondary business, raised $2.6 billion for a prior iteration of the fund in 2023, with executives citing a growing demand for cash among both money managers and their investors, known as limited partners.
The latest fund aims to acquire interests in core real estate funds from asset managers and their clients, at a discount to the net asset value, according to people familiar with the matter. It will look to invest primarily in funds with data center, rental housing and industrial assets, the people said, requesting not to be identified because the fundraising isn't public.
A representative for Blackstone declined to comment.
The US real estate market has been hammered in recent years, with the Covid-19 pandemic hitting offices particularly hard. The Federal Reserve's rate increases starting in 2022 further curbed deals, and Blackstone's own real estate division is still recovering from the brutal stretch.
Slower fundraising and a deal lull have fueled a boom on secondaries for real estate and other private assets. Real estate secondaries deals led by fund managers rose to $14.5 billion last year, up 60% from a year earlier, according to a report from Ares Management Corp. The report projected volumes to double over the next several years.
Continuation vehicles, which move existing assets into a new fund and raise fresh cash, have become increasingly popular among fund managers. In real estate, private-asset firms have increasingly used these funds to hold onto trophy assets in sectors such as logistics, data centers and senior housing, according to a report from Jefferies Financial Group Inc.

item.title: Anthropic's new Claude product drop just sent a message to these 3 tech stocks
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Anthropic's new Claude product drop just sent a message to these 3 tech stocks
2026-11-12
Por Texto propio
Anthropic's new Claude product drop just sent a message to these 3 tech stocks
On the eve of its much-hyped IPO, Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) is sending its latest message to the software space: We want a large piece of your business… in part to justify our exorbitant valuation.
Coinciding with its roadshow launch, Anthropic released several new features late Tuesday, including Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta. It also pushed Claude Dashboards to general availability as Claude Data. The tools are available on all paid plans and extend Anthropic's efforts to bring more functionality directly within Claude.
The unveiling sent Microsoft (MSFT) shares down 2.2% amid fears of a true new rival to the tech giant's Office franchise.
"There is no question given Anthropic's unprecedented growth, deep technical expertise and substantial financial resources this new product offering bears watching," Stifel analyst Brad Reback wrote to clients. "That said, we do NOT expect these products to have any meaningful impact on M365 growth rates for the foreseeable future based on deep enterprise integration, security/governance and MSFT's complete commitment to ensuring customer IP sovereignty."
Anthropic's release could impact three other tech stocks more quickly than Microsoft, KeyBanc analyst Jackson Ader pointed out. They include Monday.com (MNDY), Asana (ASAN), and Zoom (ZM). All three stocks traded lower on Tuesday amid Anthropic news.
Here's how Ader is thinking through it.
Claude Whiteboards overlaps with Monday.com, Asana, and Zoom.
"Teams can talk through a complex plan, and Claude turns it into a board with deliverables, timelines, assignments, and more for each member of the team," Ader said. "It also competes more directly with Zoom Whiteboard, whose AI capabilities generate diagrams, organize sticky notes, and turn board content into summaries and action items. Where Claude Whiteboards differs from MNDY and ASAN is what happens after the plan is made. The board Claude makes is saved as an artifact. It is not a system of record with the automation, workload views, reporting, and admin controls the work management platforms have. Since a plan has to be run somewhere, MNDY and ASAN will retain their moat for where work gets tracked and executed. A Claude Whiteboard is more of a snapshot, capturing the plan when it's made, but does not stay current on its own as the work moves forward."
Claude Meetings overlaps with AI Notetaker from Monday.com, AI Meetings from Asana, and Zoom's MyNotes and ZoomMate.
"Claude Meetings, which has been marked as 'coming soon' by Anthropic, lets a user add Claude to a call to take notes on the conversation as well as update documents and take actions on behalf of the user regarding items that came up on the call," Ader wrote. "Monday recently launched 'AI Notetaker' and Asana launched 'AI Meetings' where their tools perform similar tasks as Claude Meetings. Join a call, transcribe the conversation, and take action deliverables exiting the meeting. For Zoom, the overlap spans My Notes for transcription, summaries and next steps, built-in Meeting Summary for shared meeting recaps, and ZoomMate for creating deliverables and executing follow-up workflows across connected apps. My Notes already works across Zoom, third-party platforms, and in-person conversations without a meeting bot, so the competitive overlap is in capturing meeting context and turning it into completed work, rather than replacing Zoom's underlying video platform."

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang crisis hits a struggling chip comeback stuck below a giant wall: Chart of the Day
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Nvidia’s Huang crisis hits a struggling chip comeback stuck below a giant wall: Chart of the Day
2026-11-12
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidias-boardroom-bombshell-hits-a-fragile-chip-rally-chart-of-the-day-110000355.html
Chip stocks spent four sessions clawing out of last week's AI rout. Nvidia's boardroom crisis just pulled the rug out from under them.
The comeback was fragile to begin with. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks had won back less than a third of the market value it lost from early October to last week's low, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) was still stuck below its 200-day moving average despite a rally of about 17% off that low.
Then came Nvidia (NVDA). The stock tumbled after the bell Wednesday following reports that its board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, falling below a floor near $164 that had held twice in the past 14 months.
The scandal-plagued chipmaker had already shed about $190 billion in market value since last week's low, even as TSMC (TSM), Broadcom (AVGO) and AMD (AMD) each added roughly a quarter of a trillion dollars. At its overnight low, Nvidia's loss swelled to more than $600 billion, putting the stock at its lowest level since July 2025.
The rest of the market had been in better shape. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) clawed back about $2.5 trillion in market value over the same stretch, nearly 60% of what it lost in its monthlong slide from a record, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
Software had lagged, too. Microsoft (MSFT) has slipped since last week's low, and the iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF (IGV) has managed only about 3%.
Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, called it "not a relief rally but a belief rally that everything is still going to be okay" on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang on Wednesday.
The broader market has bought in. The equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP), which gives the smallest member the same weight as Nvidia, is a whisker from its record. Apple (AAPL) closed at a record Wednesday.
Bespoke Investment Group noted that the S&P 500 itself is still oversold, even though most of its sectors are overbought. The index is being held back by its heavyweights.
Tech's old floors are now its ceilings
Rebounds from a washout tend to stall where the selling first got serious, at old floors that have turned into ceilings.
For chip stocks, that wall sits near 11,100 to 11,200 on the chip index. That area held as a floor from May into October before it cracked, and it's roughly halfway back from the October high. First, though, the index has to get back above its 200-day average, which it fell short of Wednesday.
The Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) jumped back above its 200-day level. Its line in the sand is 29,000, where the halfway mark of its slide meets its mid-October lows and early November highs. Traders who bought on the way down and got trapped may be happy to sell there just to break even.

item.itunes:summary:
Nvidia’s Huang crisis hits a struggling chip comeback stuck below a giant wall: Chart of the Day
2026-11-12
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidias-boardroom-bombshell-hits-a-fragile-chip-rally-chart-of-the-day-110000355.html
Chip stocks spent four sessions clawing out of last week's AI rout. Nvidia's boardroom crisis just pulled the rug out from under them.
The comeback was fragile to begin with. A Yahoo Finance basket of 62 chip stocks had won back less than a third of the market value it lost from early October to last week's low, and the PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) was still stuck below its 200-day moving average despite a rally of about 17% off that low.
Then came Nvidia (NVDA). The stock tumbled after the bell Wednesday following reports that its board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, falling below a floor near $164 that had held twice in the past 14 months.
The scandal-plagued chipmaker had already shed about $190 billion in market value since last week's low, even as TSMC (TSM), Broadcom (AVGO) and AMD (AMD) each added roughly a quarter of a trillion dollars. At its overnight low, Nvidia's loss swelled to more than $600 billion, putting the stock at its lowest level since July 2025.
The rest of the market had been in better shape. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) clawed back about $2.5 trillion in market value over the same stretch, nearly 60% of what it lost in its monthlong slide from a record, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
Software had lagged, too. Microsoft (MSFT) has slipped since last week's low, and the iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF (IGV) has managed only about 3%.
Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, called it "not a relief rally but a belief rally that everything is still going to be okay" on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang on Wednesday.
The broader market has bought in. The equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP), which gives the smallest member the same weight as Nvidia, is a whisker from its record. Apple (AAPL) closed at a record Wednesday.
Bespoke Investment Group noted that the S&P 500 itself is still oversold, even though most of its sectors are overbought. The index is being held back by its heavyweights.
Tech's old floors are now its ceilings
Rebounds from a washout tend to stall where the selling first got serious, at old floors that have turned into ceilings.
For chip stocks, that wall sits near 11,100 to 11,200 on the chip index. That area held as a floor from May into October before it cracked, and it's roughly halfway back from the October high. First, though, the index has to get back above its 200-day average, which it fell short of Wednesday.
The Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) jumped back above its 200-day level. Its line in the sand is 29,000, where the halfway mark of its slide meets its mid-October lows and early November highs. Traders who bought on the way down and got trapped may be happy to sell there just to break even.

item.title: Jensen Huang espionage controversy will cast a long shadow over Nvidia, veteran tech strategist warns
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Jensen Huang espionage controversy will cast a long shadow over Nvidia, veteran tech strategist warns
2026-11-12
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jensen-huang-espionage-controversy-will-cast-a-long-shadow-over-nvidia-veteran-tech-strategist-warns-173844118.html
Jensen Huang espionage controversy will cast a long shadow over Nvidia, veteran tech strategist warns
The rough road for Nvidia (NVDA) and CEO Jensen Huang is only just beginning, even if we are only a few days into intense news coverage of the debacle, veteran tech strategist Ted Mortonson warned.
"Talking to institutional clients, Jensen is the face of the company, and whenever you mention espionage as an ex-military person, that's a whole other dynamic," Baird strategist Ted Mortonson said on Sozzi Unleashed. "So that opens up massive investigation opportunities, not only for the Republicans and Democrats, but also the FBI. And it's going to go on for a long time. So there's going to be this cloud over the company, even though they are two to three years ahead of their competition both on software and silicon."
Mortonson's colleagues downgraded their rating on Nvidia to Neutral today. Analyst Tristan Gerra's note was titled, "Icarus' Rise and Fall; Company Will be Fine."
Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees. Nvidia shares are down about 9.6% since the situation became public.
Nvidia's board of directors launched an independent investigation into reports that the woman Huang had an affair with was allegedly a spy for the Chinese government. The board said it hired powerful law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the investigation. Former acting US Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon Kim will run point on the investigation.
Mortonson said clients are rotating into Nvidia rival AMD (AMD), whose stock is up 13% over the past five days.
The endgame for Nvidia could involve more than just Huang leaving as CEO, Mortonson said.
"It could be restrictions of some markets even, you know, tighter controls from the Department of Commerce," he said. "Singapore has always been this country of entry into China underneath the table, so to speak. … I think the export controls get cleaned up. And historically Nvidia had about 20% of their revenue coming from China. I think that's shut off, definitely in the near term and maybe the long term."

item.title: 'Icarus' rise and fall': Analyst downgrades Nvidia stock amid Jensen Huang woes, highlights risks
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
'Icarus' rise and fall': Analyst downgrades Nvidia stock amid Jensen Huang woes, highlights risks
2026-11-12
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/icarus-rise-and-fall-analyst-downgrades-nvidia-stock-amid-jensen-huang-woes-highlights-risks-131204555.html
Let Wall Street analyst downgrades begin on the once-untouchable Nvidia (NVDA) stock in the wake of CEO Jensen Huang's high-profile affair.
Baird analyst Tristan Gerra cut his rating on Nvidia to Neutral on Wednesday in a note titled, "Icarus' Rise and Fall; Company Will be Fine."
"Downgrading to Neutral until uncertainties regarding U.S. government action likely resulting from the upcoming congressional hearing are lifted, U.S. government investigations reach their conclusions, revenue impact from risk channel near-term adjustments along with potential charges is quantified, and uncertainties around CEO tenure clear," Gerra wrote.
Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees. Shares are down about 12% since the situation became public.
Nvidia's board of directors launched an independent investigation into reports that the woman Huang had an affair with was allegedly a spy for the Chinese government.
The board said it hired powerful law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the investigation. Former acting US Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon Kim will run point on the investigation.
Gerra highlighted several near-term risks to Nvidia's stock, including a new ban on H200 exports to China.
"We believe low-level shipping is taking place into Asia-based warehouses with some inventories awaiting China demand. We estimate this could translate into a $5 billion write-down, Gerra said, adding: "Export control limitations notably addressing the Southeast Asia data center loopholes, along with DOJ potential action against Megaspeed and resulting preemptive or enforced actions from other data center operators located in the region with potential China demand exposure. Historically China-related GPU demand has been higher than Street expectations and often unquantified."

item.title: CoreWeave stock pops — but its debt problem hasn't gone anywhere
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
CoreWeave stock pops — but its debt problem hasn't gone anywhere
2026-11-12
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/coreweave-stock-pops--but-its-debt-problem-hasnt-gone-anywhere-164359122.html
Investors may want to temper their CoreWeave (CRWV) enthusiasm, which is on full display Wednesday.
This is far from a perfect business, and don't lose sight of that.
CoreWeave stock popped 24% in morning trading as the company came out swinging against the bears that have shredded the stock more than 40% inside of a month.
The company beat on third quarter sales estimates. Its loss was better than expected. It raised the bottom end of full-year revenue guidance by $1 billion.
Less than 30 minutes into the earnings call, CEO Michael Intrator even attempted to take the bears head-on again.
"Looking ahead, we will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to," Intrator said. "Consistent with our historical approach, we expect to finance the majority of the remaining CapEx needed to deliver our backlog through delayed draw term loans matched to specific customer contracts. Through 2027, more than 75% of committed CapEx is tied to investment-grade and enterprise customers, with the remainder tied to the world's leading AI labs and AI-native companies. The pricing of these facilities reflects the underlying customer commitments and our proven ability to deliver. They can finance anywhere from 70%-100% of the associated CapEx,"
But all of this doesn't sweep this important issue under the rug regarding CoreWeave: It has a lot of debt and an insane amount of associated interest expense!
For the nine months ended Sept. 30, CoreWeave's interest expense tallied $2 billion — up sharply from $841 million a year earlier. The excessive interest expense easily toppled the $14 million in operating income CoreWeave generated in the same period.
In the third quarter alone, CoreWeave racked up $846 million in interest expense.
The company's non-current recourse debt ballooned to $32.4 billion from $14.6 billion a year earlier.
In short, CoreWeave needs a lot to go right over the next 12 months to support a balance sheet that's throwing off this high level of interest expense.
"CoreWeave delivered about the best quarter we could have asked for," Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei said. "They're continuing to mature as a company, executing better with every print, and managing the narrative more competently than they ever have. Stats were good-to-great, funding concerns were addressed, the strategic moves make sense, and, much as we were after 2Q earnings, we're left grappling with our Underperform. We want to be believers, especially with the stock off 65% from its May high. If we were sitting in Intrator's chair, we'd make many of the same calls, and we congratulate the CRWV team on the trajectory. But we just can't get over our long-term fundamental concerns about this business model."
CoreWeave's business was — and is — reliant on customers, and markets have confidence in the model working as designed. Expect said confidence to continue to be tested.

item.title: Nvidia stock rebounds, chip stocks surge as CoreWeave earnings boost AI trade
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia stock rebounds, chip stocks surge as CoreWeave earnings boost AI trade
2026-11-12
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-stock-rebounds-chip-stocks-surge-as-coreweave-earnings-boost-ai-trade-151001136.html
Nvidia (NVDA) stock rebounded on Wednesday as the overall chip sector surged on the heels of CoreWeave's (CRWV) better-than-expected quarterly results.
Nvidia shares rose for the first time since CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, rising roughly 4% after two straight days of declines. A company board investigation, increased scrutiny from lawmakers, and questions over whether restricted semiconductors were diverted to China have weighed on the stock in recent sessions.
Even with the bounce, Nvidia is down about 14% in November and has lost about $700 billion in market value. The rally also came despite a downgrade on the stock from Baird to Neutral.
"Downgrading to Neutral until uncertainties regarding U.S. government action likely resulting from the upcoming congressional hearing are lifted, U.S. government investigations reach their conclusions, revenue impact from risk channel near-term adjustments along with potential charges is quantified, and uncertainties around CEO tenure clear," analyst Tristan Gerra wrote in a note to clients.
The broader semiconductor sector jumped on Wednesday after CoreWeave raised its full-year revenue outlook to $13 billion to $13.3 billion, up from a prior target of $12 billion to $13 billion, citing strong demand for AI compute capacity.
"Demand for compute is growing faster than the capacity to deliver that infrastructure and that is being echoed by the expansion of the margins that we are seeing on each additional contract," CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during the company's earnings call on Tuesday.
Shares of chipmakers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) stock rose over 5%, while Intel (INTC) shares surged.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which manufactures Nvidia chips, jumped 4%. Semiconductor equipment maker ASML (ASML) rose 3%.
Storage maker Sandisk (SNDK) and memory chipmakers Micron Technology (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) all gained over 8%.

item.description:
Wall Street thinks the Fed made a 'mistake' — and now more hikes are coming

item.title: Nvidia stock is pricing in 2 major risks as CEO Jensen Huang's affair fallout plays out
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Nvidia stock is pricing in 2 major risks as CEO Jensen Huang's affair fallout plays out
2026-11-12
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/nvidia-stock-is-pricing-in-2-major-risks-as-ceo-jensen-huangs-affair-fallout-plays-out-190743109.html
Nvidia's (NVDA) loyal investor base is starting to get antsy about the endgame for newly embattled CEO Jensen Huang.
Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees. Nvidia stock is down about 12% since the situation became public.
"At this point, the market is pricing in two major potential headwinds," strategists at the Kobeissi Letter said. "First, the growing possibility that Jensen Huang will be removed as CEO. Second, [the] possibility that sensitive Nvidia technology or information was compromised."
Nvidia's board of directors launched an independent investigation into reports that the woman Huang had an affair with was allegedly a spy for the Chinese government.
The board said it hired powerful law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the investigation. Former acting US Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon Kim will run point on the investigation.
While the stock's decline is startling given the strength of Nvidia's business, the reason the stock hasn't fully collapsed is that the masses generally don't expect Huang to be pushed out of the CEO role. And if he is forced out, Nvidia's business is so important to the AI build-out that it can withstand Huang no longer calling shots.
Call it blind optimism, if you will.
When asked how important Huang is to the next few years of the AI chip darling, Niles Investment Management founder and longtime tech investor Dan Niles told Sozzi Unleashed that he "isn't."
"[Huang's] got a very deep bench, and a historical example is what happened to Apple after Steve Jobs passed away. … Did it collapse?" Niles said. "So Jensen's done a great job of empowering people underneath him. I think one thing that will happen is there will be a successor appointed. The board will force that. And so I think that will occur out of this."
"Are the products in the pipeline, much like when Steve Jobs passed away, that will keep the company going for the next couple of years? Absolutely," Niles added. "But is Jensen very important to the company? Completely. So those are two separate thoughts. But they can both coexist."

item.title: US credit card debt reaches a record $1.3 trillion as inflation rises
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
US credit card debt reaches a record $1.3 trillion as inflation rises
2026-11-12
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/us-credit-card-debt-reaches-a-record-13-trillion-as-inflation-rises-165616476.html
Americans are leaning on credit cards to keep up with higher prices, with October's headline inflation data coming in hotter than expected.
In a new report from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, US credit card balances rose by $22 billion in the third quarter, reaching a record $1.28 trillion dollars in total debt. This increase came as inflation measured by the Consumer Price Index rose by 0.4% in October from the previous month.
Prices for key essentials like groceries increased 0.4% month over month after remaining relatively flat over the past two months. Americans also paid more for gas, fuel, and electricity, up 1%, 2.4%, and 0.9%, respectively, compared to the month before and on top of modest gains in previous months.
The national average credit card interest rate currently stands at 19.71%, per Bankrate, the highest interest rate level since December 2025. That's likely causing Americans to accrue debt faster. Plus, Americans tend to take on more debt around the holidays, with US consumers planning to spend over $1 trillion during the key holiday months this year, according to the National Retail Federation.
Read more: 6 things to do if you can't pay your credit card bill
Americans "continue to spend, despite high gas prices and the lowest sentiment we've ever seen, so it doesn't surprise us that that's going to carry through the holiday season," Ali Furman, PwC US consumer markets industry leader, told Yahoo Finance in September. "It's just a continuation of the trends."
Delinquency rates, or the rate of people with overdue payments, worsened in the third quarter too, increasing by 0.3 percentage points from the previous quarter to 6.87%.
It's not just credit card debt that Americans are finding themselves in; higher rates on mortgage, auto, and student loans are also taking a toll.
Mortgage balances increased by $257 billion last quarter, totaling $13.4 trillion at the end of September. The average price of a home in the US is now near $500,000 after spiking around this time last year, according to St. Louis Fed data.
Read more: This map shows the median home price by state
Auto loan balances jumped by $21 billion in Q3 to $1.73 trillion as new vehicle prices hit a record high of $51,000 in October, according to Kelley Blue Book.
Student loan balances also grew by $5 billion, bringing the total to $1.66 trillion in debt for Americans as tuition continues to climb each month.
Higher interest rates may be here to stay, making it harder for Americans to pay off the debt. Based on the hotter-than-expected October inflation reading, the Fed is expected to raise interest rates at its policy meeting next month.

item.title: Fed’s Waller leans towards 25bp hike next month, says would consider 50 bp if inflation is hot for October
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Fed’s Waller leans towards 25bp hike next month, says would consider 50 bp if inflation is hot for October
2026-11-12
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/feds-waller-leans-toward-quarter-point-rate-hike-in-december-open-to-50-basis-points-090000672.html
Federal Reserve governor Chris Waller said Tuesday that he is leaning toward raising interest rates by a quarter percentage point in December. If October inflation data released Tuesday morning is hot, he's willing to raise rates by 50 basis points next month.
"Inflation is too high … this means that even if, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points at the FOMC's December meeting," Waller said in a speech in London.
But if the October inflation data comes out higher than expected, then stronger action may be needed, Waller said. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said. "Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take."
Read more: How the Fed rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments
The Consumer Price Index is expected to rise 0.3% in October compared to a month earlier, a far slower pace than September's 0.6% gain. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, is seen rising 0.2%, down from 0.3% in the prior month.
Inflation, as measured by the Personal Consumption Expenditures index, the Fed's preferred gauge, came in hotter than expected. Core PCE inflation, excluding food and energy prices, rose 0.3% in September and 3.1% from that time last year.
"Let's just say it: September's inflation data were bad. There was no silver lining," Waller said.
Waller noted concerns about the breadth of price increases and said he'll be watching to see whether elevated inflation across many categories persists, including whether prices for high-tech goods related to the AI build-out continue to rise at the very high rate seen in recent months. Waller is also looking to see whether the run-up in energy prices over the past several months is being passed through to the cost of goods and services directly or indirectly.
Waller noted that the impact of higher prices from AI doesn't appear to be fading anytime soon, based on research by Federal Reserve staff. He pointed out that the index for high-tech products rose in December 2025 and jumped further in January 2026, ahead of an escalation in prices for those goods that eventually showed up in the February producer prices and inflation data.
He also said that the latest manufacturing data pointed to the possibility of further price increases and that there are reasons to expect energy prices will remain high due to higher insurance rates for ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. He also noted that diesel oil production is constrained by limited refining capacity and is expected to remain high even in a more peaceful Middle East, unlike crude oil prices.
Markets are pricing in a better than 80% chance that the Fed hikes by a quarter of a percentage point.

Markets are pricing in a better than 80% chance that the Fed hikes by a quarter of a percentage point.

item.title: Billionaire venture capitalist Vinod Khosla says judge AI by usage, not stock prices
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Billionaire venture capitalist Vinod Khosla says judge AI by usage, not stock prices
2026-11-12
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/billionaire-venture-capitalist-vinod-khosla-says-judge-ai-by-usage-not-stock-prices-190230250.html
Wall Street wants to know whether AI is a bubble. Most of the worry is about who's paying for it.
The companies leading the build-out are spending faster than their businesses bring in cash. Combined free cash flow for Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Meta (META), Microsoft (MSFT), and Oracle (ORCL) fell to about minus $31 billion in the third quarter, according to Goldman Sachs. That's down from positive $37 billion to $62 billion a quarter through 2025.
All that spending is a bet that people will use AI. Vinod Khosla, the billionaire Sun Microsystems co-founder and early OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) backer, says usage is the number to watch, not the stock market's mood swings. "It's not prices, it's actual usage," he said Tuesday on Yahoo Finance's Deirdre Bosa Live. He measures it in tokens — the chunks of text AI models process.
By that measure, the boom is real. Much of Big Tech's cash goes into computing power that AI labs rent to run their chatbots, and those labs' sales are taking off. OpenAI's quarterly revenue jumped nearly 50% to $10 billion.
Khosla has history on his side. "When you look at internet traffic, you can't tell where the bubble was," he said. The share of Americans online kept climbing through the dot-com crash, from about 43% in 2000 to 59% in 2002, even as the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) lost 78%.
The builders paid for the internet, and their customers cashed in
Usage was never the problem. Overbuilding was. Telecoms spent more than $500 billion laying fiber, and with 85% of it sitting unused, the cost of bandwidth fell 90%, according to research by Kai Wu, founder of Sparkline Capital.
Corning (GLW), which made the glass, fell 99% from 2000 to 2002 and didn't top its dot-com high until February, a month after it signed a deal worth up to $6 billion to supply fiber for Meta's AI data centers. The AI rush then more than doubled the stock by late June. The stock has since given back more than half, closing Tuesday near its 2000 peak.
Cheap bandwidth was a gift to whoever came next. Netflix and Meta "came around and started using it," Wu said on Yahoo Finance's Stocks in Translation podcast.
Alphabet, Meta, and Netflix (NFLX), none of which was public when the Nasdaq peaked, have added more than $5 trillion in market value since their first trades. Cisco (CSCO) is worth about $174 billion less than at its 2000 peak, per Yahoo Finance calculations.
The roles have since flipped. "Instead of Global Crossing, we now have Google," Wu said.

item.title: ‘Oversubscribed’ is the IPO world’s velvet rope — why Anthropic’s packed order book tells buyers so little
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
‘Oversubscribed’ is the IPO world’s velvet rope — why Anthropic’s packed order book tells buyers so little
2026-11-12
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropics-ipo-has-a-line-around-the-block-history-says-thats-not-the-signal-to-watch-160920832.html
There's a line outside Anthropic's IPO, and the bankers want everyone to see it. Any nightclub owner knows the crowd outside says more about the door than the party.
Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) offering has drawn multiple times the orders for the shares available, Bloomberg reported Wednesday, led by anchor-size orders. With a private placement, Anthropic and its co-founders are raising as much as about $90 billion at a targeted $1.4 trillion valuation, which would make it the biggest listing ever.
Impressive? Sure. Rare? Not even close.
Read more: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
Who gets past the rope
Most IPOs are heavily oversubscribed, which lets underwriters pick who gets shares, according to University of Florida professor Jay Ritter. Investors know it, so they pad their orders on hot deals, expecting them to be cut back in size. Plenty of that demand is often fast money looking for a quick flip.
That's why the first month of trading can mislead. "For the first 30 days you've got a pop with the IPO, but then after the lockup, that's when the market's actually going to give us the true valuation," Robert Schein, chief investment officer at Blanke Schein Wealth Management, told Yahoo Finance.
The price is the real signal
Still, the order book isn't worthless. It just speaks through the price.
Since 1980, US IPOs priced above their marketed range have gained 50% on day one on average, according to Ritter's data. Deals priced within the range averaged 12%, and those priced below it just 3%. Only about a quarter of deals clear that bar.
Anthropic set its $70-$78 range conservatively, and the Financial Times reported that bankers now expect to price above it, lifting the valuation to $1.5 trillion or more. Pricing is expected Nov. 18, with trading as soon as Nov. 19. When the bouncers start raising the cover charge, the crowd outside is real.
Year 1 is a different story
IPOs from 1980 to 2024 returned about 6% on average in their first year, compared with about 11% for similar-size companies. They trailed in four of their first five years. That's one reason four centuries of hot IPOs have rewarded patience more than speed.

item.title: Bloom Energy surges, helping to erase much of this week’s AI jitters
item.author: Paige Oamek
item.description:
Bloom Energy surges, helping to erase much of this week’s AI jitters
2026-11-12
Por Paige Oamek
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/bloom-energy-stock-surges-as-coreweave-earnings-spur-rally-in-power-stocks-185358201.html
AI power-provider stocks rallied on Wednesday after CoreWeave (CRWV) posted earnings that eased worries about how data center build-outs get funded. Bloom Energy (BE) was one of the biggest winners, jumping about 16% by midday.
The move may not have been a total surprise.
Bloom's third quarter earnings, announced in late October, were a mixed picture. On one hand, the company, which designs, manufactures, and installs solid oxide fuel cells, reported record revenue of $1.24 billion, up 138% from a year earlier, and raised its 2026 revenue guidance for the third time this year, to $4.4 billion to $4.6 billion. It was also added to the S&P 500.
On the other hand, Bloom burned cash. Operating cash flow was negative $27.1 million, and capital expenditures rose to $153.5 million, nearly triple its second quarter capex.
Still, management said the market is broadening.
"The demand for electricity is just going to skyrocket not just because of AI, but because of so many market segments that require electricity in this digital age," Bloom Energy CEO K.R. Sridhar said during an Oct. 22 earnings call. "This is coming from resiliency. It's coming from security."
Some analysts say CoreWeave's earnings report added to that case.
"CoreWeave's pricing comments suggest demand continues to outpace available supply, supporting our view that speed and certainty to power will remain differentiators for the foreseeable future," Evercore analyst Nicholas Amicucci said in a note on Wednesday.
The positive sentiment around AI infrastructure following CoreWeave's earnings also bodes well for Nebius Group (NBIS), a significant Bloom Energy customer, which reports earnings on Thursday. Nebius also rose over 18% by midday on Wednesday.
The move higher on Wednesday also came after Bloom secured a nonbinding agreement with California Resources Corporation earlier this month to explore carbon capture in the state.
Additionally, a few days later, Bloom signed an agreement with Japanese technology firm NTT (9432.T). The company will deploy fuel cells across multiple data center projects worldwide operated by NTT Data Group.
"We are witnessing strong interest in deploying Bloom systems to meet rapidly growing power demand in many international markets," Sridhar hinted during October's earnings call.
Exploring international markets may prove to be fruitful — or even existentially vital. After the midterms, Bloom Energy stock was among the S&P 500's biggest losers. Shares dropped on concerns about data center delays, including Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa's possible moratorium on all data center approvals.

item.title: Alphabet Kicks Off Asia Bond Sale as AI Firms Face Scrutiny
item.author: Janice Huang
item.description:
Alphabet Kicks Off Asia Bond Sale as AI Firms Face Scrutiny
2026-11-12
Por Janice Huang
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/alphabet-kicks-off-asia-bond-011249415.html
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc. began marketing its inaugural Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bond sale, testing investor interest at a time of increasing volatility for companies focused on artificial intelligence.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The Google parent set initial price guidance for its proposed 2-year, 5-year and 10-year Hong Kong dollar bonds at around 4.6%, 5% and 5.5%, respectively, according to a person familiar with the matter. The company is also marketing 2-year, 5-year, 10-year and 30-year Singapore dollar-denominated notes, with guidance around 2.75%, 3.25%, 3.65%, and 4%, the person said.
Proceeds from the offering will be used for general corporate purposes, which may include the repayment of outstanding debt. The bonds could be priced as early as Thursday, the person said.
The deal comes at a challenging moment for technology industry borrowers. Investors have become more cautious toward AI-linked assets after a broad market selloff last week fueled by concerns that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could lead to greater scrutiny of data center development and AI infrastructure spending.
The sector has also been shaken by market turmoil sparked by Nvidia Corp., the leading maker of AI chips, which has been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang.
Alphabet's fundraising effort is part of a broader push by global hyperscalers to tap new debt markets as they seek financing for AI-related projects. The company sold its first Australian dollar bonds in August and has also issued notes in Swiss francs, British pounds, Canadian dollars and Japanese yen this year.
Alphabet and other firms, including Microsoft Corp., Amazon.com Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc., have been borrowing at a record pace while simultaneously committing tens of billions of dollars to build out AI capabilities.
Earlier this month, Alphabet raised €6 billion ($6.7 billion) through a multi-tranche euro bond sale, its second offering in the currency this year. The company paid materially higher borrowing costs than in its inaugural euro deal in May as concerns over the pace of AI spending rose.

Earlier this month, Alphabet raised €6 billion ($6.7 billion) through a multi-tranche euro bond sale, its second offering in the currency this year. The company paid materially higher borrowing costs than in its inaugural euro deal in May as concerns over the pace of AI spending rose.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Huang allegedly involved in a second affair with an Nvidia exec
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Huang allegedly involved in a second affair with an Nvidia exec
2026-11-12
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/nvidia-ceo-huang-allegedly-involved-in-a-second-affair-with-an-nvidia-exec-221824237.html
Embattled Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was allegedly involved in a second extramarital affair.
The company's board is reportedly meeting to determine if it will oust Huang as chief executive, the Wall Street Journal reports. Nvidia stock fell in after-hours trading following the report.
According to The New York Times, Huang, whose relationship with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell.
She joined Nvidia in 2008 and heads up the company's healthcare business.
The Times report says that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate at a hotel during a company conference in March, and that when a bystander took a photo of the interaction, a security guard "sequestered them" and made them an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.
Last month, The Times reported that US intelligence services believed a woman, Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, may have acted as an intelligence asset, sharing information with the ruling party in Beijing.
On Sunday, Huang issued a statement apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees for having an affair, though he didn't name with whom.
In response, Nvidia's board said it is launching an independent investigation into the matter.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board said in a statement Sunday.

item.title: Meta is losing its longtime head of infrastructure
item.author: Lucas Ropek
item.description:
Meta is losing its longtime head of infrastructure
2026-11-12
Por Lucas Ropek
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/meta-losing-longtime-head-infrastructure-201201421.html
A key figure in Meta's growth into a social media and tech industry powerhouse is leaving the company.
It sounds like Janardhan will remain at Meta for a little bit, although he is expected to leave next year. "Santosh will stay on for transition and he is moving into an advisory role on Meta Compute," said a Meta representative.
Janardhan, who originally joined the company in 2009, helped the firm grow into the massive internet presence that it is today. Bloomberg originally reported Janardhan's departure, citing an internal memo that had recently been circulated. It's unclear why Janardhan is stepping down from the role. The memo did not specify the reasons for his departure and Meta didn't immediately respond to a request for clarity on the issue. However, Janardhan's memo apparently cited the need to "pass the baton."
In recent years, the company's investment in infrastructure has exploded, as it seeks to keep up with its competitors in the AI race. Earlier this year, Janardhan was tasked with leading Meta Compute, the company initiative to scale its data center investments and strategy.

item.title: Goldman Sachs calls chip stocks 'oversold.' Here are the names it says to buy.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Goldman Sachs calls chip stocks 'oversold.' Here are the names it says to buy.
2026-11-11
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/goldman-sachs-calls-chip-stocks-oversold-here-are-the-names-it-says-to-buy-165654250.html
Goldman Sachs is sifting through the AI stock rubble in search of bargains.
"We believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said about semiconductor stocks.
Three of his top names to buy: Nvidia (NVDA), Broadcom (AVGO), and AMD (AMD).
"Even in a 'no growth' scenario for 2028 (which we see as relatively unlikely), NVDA/AVGO are trading 12X/13X this baseline — which we believe valuations are compelling at current levels," Schneider wrote in a note. "We find AMD to be very attractive given the growth we believe it can achieve, albeit at a less compelling valuation."
It has been a brutal run for tech stocks in November.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.3% of its market value on Nov. 5 as investors assessed what a blue wave on Election Day would mean for the build-out of AI data centers. The move wiped out $3 trillion in value.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) plunged 1,800 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq (^IXIC) cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).
Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially semiconductor names.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (^SOX) is down 21% in the past month, and 6% in November alone.
"We believe the market has been contending with competing tensions relative to semiconductors: (1) How does the funding gap between current capex and free cash flows for hyperscalers and AI model labs levels get closed? (2) Is there sufficient land/power/shell coming on line to match current Street estimates for Semis?" Schneider explained. "Following the US elections on Nov. 3, the second of these tensions came into greater focus with greater uncertainty around the pace of datacenter builds in states such as Texas."
He added, "[Although] we recognize there may be few catalysts for stocks to move higher before year end, we think risk/reward is compelling for select names at current levels."

item.title: Energy prices matter way more for inflation than they used to: Fed report
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Energy prices matter way more for inflation than they used to: Fed report
2026-11-11
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/energy-prices-matter-way-more-for-inflation-than-they-used-to-fed-report-110000366.html
Since the start of the Iran war, investors have been wrestling with what elevated oil prices mean for the economy.
Trump and his economic advisers advanced the traditional view that price increases from an oil supply shock would be short-lived, rather than a persistent threat to stability.
But many agitated consumers — and economists — saw higher gas prices and more expensive goods as a new, stubborn feature of everyday spending, a consequence of the conflict permeating deeper into the economy.
Read more: How oil price shocks ripple through your wallet, from gas to groceries
A new research note from the Federal Reserve offers a fresh take on the energy price debate. The "transitory" or temporary shocks are adding up to make a meaningful — and unpleasant — difference.
Inflation in the post-pandemic economy sticks around for longer, the report found, and oil shocks more strongly leak into core inflation, presenting a challenge for central bankers. Where in a previous era the Fed might have been correct to "look through" an oil spike as a fleeting event, the new research suggests energy shocks matter a lot more now.
Which makes sense: Between the post-COVID inflation boom, Russia-Ukraine, and Iran/Hormuz, it's been, as many analysts have punned, "one supply shock after another."
"Our estimated model implies that the recent rise in oil prices could significantly raise core inflation in the advanced economies over the next few years were the greater persistence and higher pass-through to continue," the Fed's report said.
Before the pandemic and subsequent crises, central bankers could more easily manage oil-price shocks. Inflation didn't persist as long, so any increases faded quickly. That helps explain the belief that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz (assuming the war would end) wouldn't amount to a dramatic and extended economic event. Oil price increases also tended to stay within headline inflation metrics. That meant gas and energy costs would rise, but those pricing pressures would stay confined and woudn't spread into core inflation.
Those dynamics gave central bankers, political leaders, and consumers protections from geopolitical instability.
A conflict over energy might create an economic ripple that would soon subside. But the post-pandemic data, the Fed's research shows, points to a shift in the inflation process. If it continues, it means the economy is more sensitive to oil price shocks. And higher energy prices could easily bleed into core inflation.
The Fed offered a note of caution, however: This is still a very short period, post-pandemic. This could be the new normal, or it could be a weird anomaly.
"Nevertheless," the report said, "they illustrate an upside risk to inflation should oil prices remain elevated or supply-chain disruptions persist for an extended period."
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: American paychecks are losing to inflation again — here are the most painful categories
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
American paychecks are losing to inflation again — here are the most painful categories
2026-11-11
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/american-paychecks-are-losing-to-inflation-again--here-are-the-most-painful-categories-144702833.html
The gas pump is about the only place Americans are getting relief from inflation. Plane tickets, restaurant meals, and electric bills have all risen faster than the average worker's pay over the past two years.
Pump prices have fallen for six straight weeks. Even so, a gallon of gas still costs about 37% more than it did a year ago.
That's one of the few yearly numbers the government could publish Tuesday. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not collect October 2025 prices during last year's shutdown, so the usual annual inflation rate is missing.
Read more: October inflation breakdown includes cheaper gas, bigger grocery bills
So we estimated it. According to Yahoo Finance's calculations, consumer prices rose about 4% in the year through October, up from 3.7% in September.
Paychecks didn't keep up. Average hourly pay rose about 3%, which leaves pay down nearly 1% after inflation. That's the seventh straight month workers have lost ground, matching May as the worst stretch of the run.
And prices are speeding up. They rose 0.4% in October, while "core" prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3%. Both came in hotter than Wall Street expected.
Over the past three months, core prices climbed at a nearly 4% annual pace, noted Kevin Gordon, head of macro research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research. That's the fastest since April 2024, per Yahoo Finance's calculations.
"For households, the reduced purchasing power from inflation hits twice as hard when your wages aren't keeping up," Elizabeth Renter, lead economist at Life360, said in emailed comments.
The most painful categories
Since October 2024, average hourly pay has increased by about 7%. Here's what outran it.
Airfares jumped more than 20%. Car repairs rose by about 13%, hospital services by about 12%, and electricity by nearly 10%. A meal at a sit-down restaurant costs about 9% more.
Groceries are the exception, up only about 5%.
Take the average of four costs most households can't skip — the "utility, gasoline, grocery, and electricity components" of the index — and they're up 12% from a year ago, Gordon wrote on X.
The war in the Middle East is a major reason, according to RSM chief economist Joe Brusuelas. He pointed to "the passing through of higher energy prices — think diesel prices — to transportation services and food at home." Diesel, the fuel that powers nearly everything else, is still near its record high.
That leaves the Federal Reserve on track to raise interest rates, which would push up borrowing costs on credit cards, car loans, and other debt. Fed governor Chris Waller said Tuesday he's leaning toward a December hike and would consider a half point, double the usual move, if inflation runs hot. Traders on Polymarket see a better-than-90% chance of a hike when the Fed meets on Dec. 8-9.

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/american-paychecks-are-losing-to-inflation-again--here-are-the-most-painful-categories-144702833.html
The gas pump is about the only place Americans are getting relief from inflation. Plane tickets, restaurant meals, and electric bills have all risen faster than the average worker's pay over the past two years.
Pump prices have fallen for six straight weeks. Even so, a gallon of gas still costs about 37% more than it did a year ago.
That's one of the few yearly numbers the government could publish Tuesday. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not collect October 2025 prices during last year's shutdown, so the usual annual inflation rate is missing.
Read more: October inflation breakdown includes cheaper gas, bigger grocery bills
So we estimated it. According to Yahoo Finance's calculations, consumer prices rose about 4% in the year through October, up from 3.7% in September.
Paychecks didn't keep up. Average hourly pay rose about 3%, which leaves pay down nearly 1% after inflation. That's the seventh straight month workers have lost ground, matching May as the worst stretch of the run.
And prices are speeding up. They rose 0.4% in October, while "core" prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3%. Both came in hotter than Wall Street expected.
Over the past three months, core prices climbed at a nearly 4% annual pace, noted Kevin Gordon, head of macro research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research. That's the fastest since April 2024, per Yahoo Finance's calculations.
"For households, the reduced purchasing power from inflation hits twice as hard when your wages aren't keeping up," Elizabeth Renter, lead economist at Life360, said in emailed comments.
The most painful categories
Since October 2024, average hourly pay has increased by about 7%. Here's what outran it.
Airfares jumped more than 20%. Car repairs rose by about 13%, hospital services by about 12%, and electricity by nearly 10%. A meal at a sit-down restaurant costs about 9% more.
Groceries are the exception, up only about 5%.
Take the average of four costs most households can't skip — the "utility, gasoline, grocery, and electricity components" of the index — and they're up 12% from a year ago, Gordon wrote on X.
The war in the Middle East is a major reason, according to RSM chief economist Joe Brusuelas. He pointed to "the passing through of higher energy prices — think diesel prices — to transportation services and food at home." Diesel, the fuel that powers nearly everything else, is still near its record high.
That leaves the Federal Reserve on track to raise interest rates, which would push up borrowing costs on credit cards, car loans, and other debt. Fed governor Chris Waller said Tuesday he's leaning toward a December hike and would consider a half point, double the usual move, if inflation runs hot. Traders on Polymarket see a better-than-90% chance of a hike when the Fed meets on Dec. 8-9.

item.title: Anthropic says a key AI safety alarm has been triggered, days before its IPO
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Anthropic says a key AI safety alarm has been triggered, days before its IPO
2026-11-11
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropic-says-a-key-ai-safety-alarm-has-been-triggered-days-before-its-ipo-171519615.html
A week ago, Anthropic told would-be investors that AI speeding up its own research might "imminently" trigger one of the company's key safety alarms. On Tuesday, in the same filing that set a price range for its record-setting IPO, it said that has now happened.
"We made a determination that we have met this threshold," the company wrote in its amended prospectus. It based the call on "what we expect from future models and our overall rate of progress, rather than on what we have observed from current models."
The safety threshold sits in Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy — the company rulebook for adding tougher safety measures as its AI gets more powerful. This one is triggered when AI is doing enough of Anthropic's research to roughly double how fast its models improve. The policy says that pace would pack two years' worth of AI progress, at its 2018-2024 rate, into a single year. The filing says AI "has already been accelerating our research and development." Crossing the line means more safeguards, not a shutdown.
The fear is AI will improve itself faster than people can check it. In 2023, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei joined other AI leaders in warning that the "risk of extinction from AI" should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.
Anthropic says humans stay in charge. It doesn't expect to safely use Claude "to fully autonomously design and build successive generations of frontier models without meaningful human supervision or understanding," the filing says, and it is weighing policy changes "to keep humans in control."
An outside group sees the same speedup. METR, an independent nonprofit that tests AI systems, estimated last week that Anthropic's models have been improving nearly twice as fast since October 2025.
In a separate review, METR called Anthropic's August argument that it was still below the threshold "overstated" and said it was "plausible" the line was crossed by mid-July.
A $1.4 trillion debut
Anthropic set its price range at $70 to $78 per share on Tuesday as it began its roadshow, the round of investor meetings before pricing. That values it at as much as about $1.4 trillion, counting every share that could exist. Trading could start as soon as Nov. 19, according to reports.
Read more: Everything you need to know ahead of Anthropic's IPO
Some of the market's biggest names are tied up in the IPO. Nvidia (NVDA) and Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) Google are each buying $10 billion of Anthropic stock at the IPO price, part of a $26 billion private placement with AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), Micron (MU), Microsoft (MSFT), and Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM). Amazon (AMZN) and Google already own big stakes.

item.title: Consumers are turning to cheaper brands like it's 2021 as inflation pinches
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Consumers are turning to cheaper brands like it's 2021 as inflation pinches
2026-11-11
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/consumers-are-turning-to-cheaper-brands-like-its-2021-as-inflation-pinches-110000841.html
The verdict is in, or nearly there. After Tuesday's hotter-than-expected inflation numbers, the Fed is most likely going to raise interest rates at its policy meeting next month.
On top of that, investors are now worried about a much more hawkish Fed in 2027.
Pricing pressures were so strong across essentials like food, rent, and medical care that there's renewed chatter the Fed might impose a jumbo hike of 50 basis points.
The expectations have clearly changed.
Higher costs are showing up in other places too. Like in data about how Americans are spending their money. According to a new analysis by the Bank of America Institute, consumers are "trading down" to cheaper brands at the highest levels since the height of the pandemic.
The data reveals that consumers are increasingly value-conscious. People are buying store brands over name brands, going to cheaper retailers instead of department stores, and eating fast food in place of sit-down restaurants.
"While households continue to spend, they are increasingly seeking discounts as concerns about higher prices persist," wrote Taylor Bowley, an economist at the Bank of America Institute. With a ton of deposit accounts, credit cards, and debit cards, the bank is uniquely positioned to track spending across a wide swath of demographics.
The analysis showed consumers appear increasingly focused on value, shifting spending to value-tier merchants at 2021 levels. Millennials — faced with the cost of raising families, high housing, auto, and childcare costs — are leading the shift toward value-oriented shopping, the report found.
That change is most pronounced in apparel and grocery spending, suggesting that the hunt for bargains isn't limited to discretionary purchases but now extends to everyday household spending.
"While consumers can delay apparel purchases, trading down on groceries is notable because it suggests Millennials are looking for savings even in areas where spending is harder to avoid, like food," the report said.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.
