item.title: Top strategist: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair highlights key risk for tech companies
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Top strategist: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair highlights key risk for tech companies
2026-11-11
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/top-strategist-nvidia-ceo-jensen-huangs-affair-highlights-key-risk-for-tech-companies-184212599.html
Add national security risk to the outlook for the S&P 500 (^GSPC), in addition to a potential slowdown of the AI data center build-out.
That risk has been brought to the forefront amid the stunning debacle unfolding at Nvidia (NVDA) and with its high-profile founder and CEO, Jensen Huang.
"I think the news on Nvidia highlights that national security is critically important for these tech companies, and government involvement might even be more aggressive from here than less aggressive," Bank of America head of US equity and quantitative strategy Savita Subramanian said on Sozzi Unleashed.
"So I think it's a really interesting time," Subramanian added. "I think you want to stay along [with] the idea that AI is not the metaverse … It's not just going to end. But the speed of capex might be stretched out a little bit rather than happening over the next two years."
Nvidia's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into reports that a woman CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was allegedly a spy for the Chinese government.
Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees.
Nvidia stock fell 4.27% on Monday as a dark cloud settled over Nvidia and its once-Teflon CEO's future. Shares fell another 6% in afternoon trading on Tuesday.
"We've seen the government involved in semis historically. We saw a 10% stake in Intel from the US Treasury. So we've seen this support mechanism come through," Subramanian said. "I think that it's paramount for the US to remain No. 1 in terms of tech primacy. And that's where I see almost a put on the tech story from here."
"I don't think it ends. I don't think it gets derailed by a blue sweep. I think there's bipartisan support to remain No. 1 when it comes to tech," she added. "But I do think that issues over the last week, the cost of capital rising onerously for these companies that are trying to build out capacity, some of those aspects might be more scrutinized."

item.title: Micron stock is a screaming buy at current valuation levels: Goldman Sachs
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Micron stock is a screaming buy at current valuation levels: Goldman Sachs
2026-11-11
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/micron-stock-is-a-screaming-buy-at-current-valuation-levels-goldman-sachs-172852076.html
Micron's (MU) valuation has reached a level where it's simply too cheap to ignore given its fundamentals, says Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider.
Schneider reiterated his $1,250 price target on the once red-hot AI momentum trade. It assumes about 70% upside from current levels.
"We also believe risk/reward is becoming more attractive for Neutral-rated Micron in light of the high probability of strong free cash flow in the coming quarters," Schneider said.
Micron is currently approaching tangible book value, Schneider noted. When a stock trades below tangible book value, investors value the company at less than the estimated value of its assets after subtracting its liabilities and intangible assets.
In a sense, the market is saying the company's physical and financial assets are worth more than the entire company's stock market value.
That seems to be bordering on an unwarranted disconnect, at least in assessing Schneider's work on the chip player.
Micron's stock is down 17% over the past month amid fears that a blue wave on Election Day could slow the build-out of AI infrastructure. That could have ramifications for orders for Micron's memory chips.
The rout has brought Micron's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio down to an almost laughable 4.2 times, according to Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. Keep in mind Micron is coming off a quarter of strong demand amid memory chip shortages driving up prices.
The Street still expects Micron to grow earnings by at least 17% in its next fiscal year.

item.title: Hot inflation report has Wall Street eyeing whether the Fed could make a jumbo rate hike next month
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Hot inflation report has Wall Street eyeing whether the Fed could make a jumbo rate hike next month
2026-11-11
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/hot-inflation-report-has-wall-street-eyeing-whether-the-fed-could-make-a-jumbo-rate-hike-next-month-164942156.html
A hotter-than-expected October inflation reading showed that inflation remains elevated after soaring in September, solidifying the odds the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month.
It's even raising the specter of a jumbo half-percentage-point hike.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%, marking a slight cooldown from September's 0.6% gain. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2% and unchanged from September.
The Labor Department did not report a 12-month inflation rate for October — the measure of how much prices climbed over the past year — because of last fall's government shutdown. Prices in October 2025 were never measured.
"The stronger-than-expected 0.3% rise in the core CPI in October was similar to September's in that it was very broad-based, rather than driven by any one-off or temporary factors," said Thomas Ryan, economist for Capital Economics. "This should all but confirm a December hike, with the strength of inflationary pressures in the last two months raising the risk that the Fed opts for a larger 50bp move rather than 25bp."
Jason Pride, chief of investment strategy and research at Glenmede, looks at two specific data points to assess whether inflation is returning to target, and both moved the wrong way in October.
Services minus the cost of housing rose 0.5%, the highest reading since May, extending the sticky services dynamic that has been the central obstacle to getting price trends back to 2% all year. Pride said that measure needs to average out near 0.2% before there is a credible case that broad inflation is falling to the Fed's 2% target. Meanwhile, goods prices excluding food, energy, and used cars rose 0.4%, the highest since January.
Given these trends, Pride warned that investors should plan for rates at or above today's level well into next year, with the path beyond December dependent on whether services prices finally turn.
The immediate question is the size of the Fed's next move.
"Will the central bank deliver a 25 basis points or 50 basis points move?" said James McCann, senior economist at Edward Jones, noting that price growth was again stronger than feared.
"We think it is most likely that the Fed will deliver a 25 basis points move, especially with oil prices moving lower in recent days and financial conditions increasingly volatile," he said. "However, the risk of a bigger 50 basis points move cannot be ruled out."
item.content:encoded:
Hot inflation report has Wall Street eyeing whether the Fed could make a jumbo rate hike next month

2026-11-11

Por Jennifer Schonberger

https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/hot-inflation-report-has-wall-street-eyeing-whether-the-fed-could-make-a-jumbo-rate-hike-next-month-164942156.html

A hotter-than-expected October inflation reading showed that inflation remains elevated after soaring in September, solidifying the odds the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month.

It's even raising the specter of a jumbo half-percentage-point hike.

The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, compared with expectations of 0.3%, marking a slight cooldown from September's 0.6% gain. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, compared with expectations of 0.2% and unchanged from September.

The Labor Department did not report a 12-month inflation rate for October — the measure of how much prices climbed over the past year — because of last fall's government shutdown. Prices in October 2025 were never measured.

"The stronger-than-expected 0.3% rise in the core CPI in October was similar to September's in that it was very broad-based, rather than driven by any one-off or temporary factors," said Thomas Ryan, economist for Capital Economics. "This should all but confirm a December hike, with the strength of inflationary pressures in the last two months raising the risk that the Fed opts for a larger 50bp move rather than 25bp."

Jason Pride, chief of investment strategy and research at Glenmede, looks at two specific data points to assess whether inflation is returning to target, and both moved the wrong way in October.

Services minus the cost of housing rose 0.5%, the highest reading since May, extending the sticky services dynamic that has been the central obstacle to getting price trends back to 2% all year. Pride said that measure needs to average out near 0.2% before there is a credible case that broad inflation is falling to the Fed's 2% target. Meanwhile, goods prices excluding food, energy, and used cars rose 0.4%, the highest since January.

Given these trends, Pride warned that investors should plan for rates at or above today's level well into next year, with the path beyond December dependent on whether services prices finally turn.

The immediate question is the size of the Fed's next move.

"Will the central bank deliver a 25 basis points or 50 basis points move?" said James McCann, senior economist at Edward Jones, noting that price growth was again stronger than feared.

"We think it is most likely that the Fed will deliver a 25 basis points move, especially with oil prices moving lower in recent days and financial conditions increasingly volatile," he said. "However, the risk of a bigger 50 basis points move cannot be ruled out."

item.title: 'Not great': October CPI inflation rises 0.4% as food and rent costs spike
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
'Not great': October CPI inflation rises 0.4% as food and rent costs spike
2026-11-11
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/not-great-october-cpi-inflation-data-comes-in-hotter-than-expected-as-food-and-rent-costs-spike-142323507.html
Consumer Price Index data for October showed that inflation remains elevated, as costs rose across a wide range of essential goods and services, including food, rent, and medical care.
The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October from a month earlier, higher than the 0.3% economists were expecting but below September's 0.6% gain, according to Labor Department data released on Tuesday. "Core" inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, coming in ahead of the 0.2% economists were expecting to match September's level.
October's report didn't include annual inflation figures because the Bureau of Labor Statistics was unable to publish full October 2025 data due to the government shutdown last year. But many economists estimate that inflation accelerated on a year-over-year basis.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Housing costs were a major contributor to October's price increases. Owners' equivalent rent, which measures homeownership costs, rose 0.3%, while rents were up 0.2%.
Food costs were up 0.5%, driven by higher meat and dairy prices. Lettuce prices rose 7.3%, and baby food jumped 5.1%.
Transportation costs accelerated 0.8% last month, while medical care items were up 0.5% and medical services rose 0.3%.
"One hopes inflation starts returning to normal, but that's a hope right now, not a reality," economist Justin Wolfers wrote on X.
Rising energy prices weighed heavily on September's report, but October's price increases were less dramatic. Energy costs rose 0.7% last month, down from 5.2% in September.
Read more: October inflation breakdown: Cheaper gas, bigger grocery bills
"CPI for October is not great," Kevin Gordon, head of macro research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research, wrote in a post on X.
"Inflation breadth still looking poor across goods and services," he wrote in another post, referring to the wide variety of categories in which prices are rising.
Tuesday's inflation data is the Federal Reserve's final look at the CPI before it meets Dec. 8-9, although it will get another look at inflation data via its preferred measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index, later this month.
The hot report, coupled with a labor market that's holding up and even showing signs of accelerating, cemented traders' expectations for a rate hike in December. Traders now see a 15.3% chance of a larger 50 basis point move.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: 10-year Treasury yield jumps as hot inflation lifts rate-hike odds: AlphaCheck
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
10-year Treasury yield jumps as hot inflation lifts rate-hike odds: AlphaCheck
2026-11-11
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/10-year-treasury-yield-jumps-as-odds-of-rate-hike-rise-amid-hot-inflation-print-alphacheck-144120699.html
Good morning. Stocks fell on Tuesday as the 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX) jumped to 4.93% after a hotter-than-expected October inflation reading, strengthening expectations for a rate hike next month.
Long-dated bond yields, which serve as a benchmark for borrowing costs, were already rising after Fed governor Chris Waller said, ahead of the inflation report, that he would leave the door open for a 50 basis point increase, depending on inflation. The odds of a December rate hike stood at 89% on Tuesday.
The 30-year Treasury (^TYX) yield touched 5.3% while the 2-year yield jumped 14 basis points to 4.69%. Meanwhile, Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) dropped 3% to near $89 per barrel, while WTI (CL=F) also declined to hover around $84.50 per barrel.
Read more: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
Shares of AI chip heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA) extended declines after President Trump mentioned the FBI was "looking into" CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman believed by US intelligence to be tied to the Chinese government. The rest of the semiconductor sector declined as the Tech (XLK) sector fell amid a broader stock sell-off.
Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Here are some other notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: Take-Two Interactive (TTOW), Hims & Hers (HIMS), and Sea Limited (SE).

item.title: SpaceX, Rocket Lab blast higher as NASA hands out $10 billion in moon base awards
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
SpaceX, Rocket Lab blast higher as NASA hands out $10 billion in moon base awards
2026-11-10
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/spacex-rocket-lab-blast-higher-as-nasa-hands-out-10-billion-in-moon-base-awards-164320855.html
NASA wants a base on the Moon, and Wall Street is suddenly buying the ride there. Space stocks ripped for a second session Monday as SpaceX (SPCX) and seven other companies line up for lunar delivery work worth up to $10 billion.
NASA named the eight winners on Nov. 7 at Kennedy Space Center. Alongside SpaceX and Blue Origin are three smaller public companies, Intuitive Machines (LUNR), Firefly Aerospace (FLY) and Voyager Technologies (VOYG).
For those three, the prize is out of this world. They're worth about $8.5 billion combined, less than the contract's ceiling, though each still has to win missions one by one.
Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) is NASA's way of hiring private companies to fly cargo to the moon. The new 10-year version covers larger landers, and NASA raised the original contract's value to $4.2 billion from $2.6 billion. Intuitive Machines CEO Steve Altemus said the company is "excited to participate in this next evolution of CLPS."
"We are building the Moon Base mission by mission," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the agency's announcement.
Rocket Lab (RKLB) didn't make NASA's list but jumped anyway ahead of its third quarter results after Monday's close. The stock rose about 28% over two sessions, its third-best two-day run in two years, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Space stocks surged off last week's post-election low, rising roughly 20% to 60% since the Nov. 5 close, with Firefly in the lead. SpaceX posted its biggest two-day gain since early October, while the Nasdaq (^IXIC) gained about 4%.
The bounce follows a brutal stretch. An average of nine space stocks more than doubled this year by May 28, two weeks before SpaceX's June 12 debut, then gave it all back. The group is now down for 2026.
SpaceX is a different story. Wall Street prices it less as a lunar trucker than as an AI cloud, competing with neoclouds — companies like CoreWeave (CRWV) that rent out AI computing power — and with hyperscalers, the cloud giants such as Amazon (AMZN) and Microsoft (MSFT).
On Monday, SpaceX added more than $100 billion in market value, more than the roughly $90 billion that 16 other US-listed space stocks are worth combined. NASA's 10-year moon pot is about a tenth of that one-day gain.
Rocket Lab's third quarter revenue jumped 73% from a year earlier to nearly $268 million, topping estimates, and its fourth quarter forecast came in above Wall Street's. Even so, the stock slipped after hours, and Neutron, its bigger rocket, isn't set to debut until 2027.

item.title: AI stocks have 2 major headwinds driving recent volatility
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AI stocks have 2 major headwinds driving recent volatility
2026-11-10
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/ai-stocks-have-2-major-headwinds-driving-recent-volatility-160346646.html
AI stocks rose on Monday, but markets remain on high alert amid fears that a slowdown in data center build-outs will upset the profit boom of the world's biggest companies — all of which are in tech.
Those fears have become amplified in the wake of the "blue wave" that crested on Election Day, which could see newly elected Democratic senators and governors muck up the AI expansion.
Additionally, there appears to be a second, less-obvious driver of the recent painful AI stock rout.
Companies like Apple (AAPL) and Amazon (AMZN) have recently said they are keeping a closer eye on AI token spending. The read-through is that AI tech doesn't have infinite pricing power.
"A significant push back on the pricing of AI by enterprises is growing in a meaningful way," Miller Tabal chief markets strategist Matt Maley wrote in a note. "The new 'usage pricing' policy for enterprises has caused a massive jump in the cost of AI for these enterprises (companies) … and this has caused MANY of them to balk at these increased costs. Many are now using AI routers to direct simple queries to smaller/cheaper models … and keeping the expensive frontier models for more complicated tasks. Others are adopting open-weight and local models … and quite a few are now enforcing budgets and token caps for employees."
This one-two punch led to a historic and painful session for investors on Nov. 5.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) plunged 1,800 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq (^IXIC) cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).
Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially tech names.
Maley added, "There are TWO major developments from the past several weeks which are creating some further significant … and warranted … fears about the ROI for the AI industry. … Yes, a slowdown in the buildout of the data centers will likely pushout the timeframe when many companies will be able to create their full profit potential … but this 'pricing' issue raises some significant questions about just how profitable it will be. In other words, the HUGE profit assumptions that have been imagined by many AI bulls for the profitability of AI are starting to wane."

Companies like Apple (AAPL) and Amazon (AMZN) have recently said they are keeping a closer eye on AI token spending. The read-through is that AI tech doesn't have infinite pricing power.

"A significant push back on the pricing of AI by enterprises is growing in a meaningful way," Miller Tabal chief markets strategist Matt Maley wrote in a note. "The new 'usage pricing' policy for enterprises has caused a massive jump in the cost of AI for these enterprises (companies) … and this has caused MANY of them to balk at these increased costs. Many are now using AI routers to direct simple queries to smaller/cheaper models … and keeping the expensive frontier models for more complicated tasks. Others are adopting open-weight and local models … and quite a few are now enforcing budgets and token caps for employees."

This one-two punch led to a historic and painful session for investors on Nov. 5.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) plunged 1,800 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq (^IXIC) cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).

Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially tech names.

Maley added, "There are TWO major developments from the past several weeks which are creating some further significant … and warranted … fears about the ROI for the AI industry. … Yes, a slowdown in the buildout of the data centers will likely pushout the timeframe when many companies will be able to create their full profit potential … but this 'pricing' issue raises some significant questions about just how profitable it will be. In other words, the HUGE profit assumptions that have been imagined by many AI bulls for the profitability of AI are starting to wane."

item.title: Morgan Stanley buys Vinyl Equity to capture more IPO wealth
item.author: David Hollerith
item.description:
Morgan Stanley buys Vinyl Equity to capture more IPO wealth
2026-11-10
Por David Hollerith
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/morgan-stanley-buys-vinyl-equity-to-capture-more-ipo-wealth-170514799.html
Morgan Stanley (MS) said Monday it has agreed to acquire Vinyl Equity, a company that serves a lesser-known back-office function, as the Wall Street giant looks to deepen its services around taking companies public.
The acquisition would give Morgan Stanley greater control over the transfer of shares from private companies into public markets, a move that bolsters its workplace wealth management business, which administers employee stock plans for millions of workers across corporate America.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.
Morgan Stanley already offers administration services to more than 1,000 private companies, representing nearly 70% of existing unicorns, according to Scott Whatley, head of Morgan Stanley at Work. Those companies will be the initial focus for the newly acquired business.
The potential payoff from those relationships has become increasingly evident in Morgan Stanley's recent earnings.
In its second and third quarters, the bank's IPO-related stock flows accounted for more than half of the $380 billion in net new assets attracted by the bank's wealth management division, according to company executives.
Speaking at a capital markets conference on Monday afternoon, Morgan Stanley wealth management chief Jed Finn said transferring shares from private to public ownership can take as long as two weeks through traditional transfer agents, while Vinyl's technology can complete the process on a next-day settlement timeline.
Finn said corporate clients had sought the capability for years, partly because they wanted to avoid transferring sensitive shareholder information among multiple outside firms.
"We're finding ways to be easier to do business with for our clients," Whatley said, adding that removing third-party transfer agents "will increase the probability" of retaining assets and converting them into fee-based flows.
The acquisition is the latest move by Morgan Stanley to deepen its relationships with private companies and their employees before they go public, following its acquisition of private-share marketplace EquityZen earlier this year. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Forge Global and EquityZen.)
Whatley said bringing share transfers within Morgan Stanley could also help the bank retain more client assets and convert them into fee-generating wealth-management relationships.
The deal could also position Morgan Stanley to capitalize on the emerging market for tokenized securities, which use blockchain technology to record and transfer ownership of financial assets.

item.title: Intel took 25 years to get back to its dot-com peak — and lost it in 6 months: Chart of the Day
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Intel took 25 years to get back to its dot-com peak — and lost it in 6 months: Chart of the Day
2026-11-10
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/intel-took-25-years-to-get-back-to-its-dot-com-peak--and-lost-it-in-6-months-chart-of-the-day-144715722.html
Half off sounds like a deal. On Wall Street, it can be the start of a much bigger sale.
Right now, Intel (INTC), Arm (ARM), Sandisk (SNDK), and CoreWeave (CRWV) are among the AI darlings trading at less than half their 2026 highs, and chip stocks just lost nearly 30% in five weeks.
Chip stocks bounced Friday and roared back Monday. The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) jumped about 7%, its best day since July, and the S&P 500 (^GSPC) rose more than 2%, its biggest gain since April.
Veteran trader Michael Martin isn't biting. "Lower prices mean lower market cap. It doesn't mean better value," said Martin, founder of TraderMindset.com, who works with Wall Street legend Victor "Trader Vic" Sperandeo.
"I keep hearing Gordon Gekko's voice in the back of my mind — 'A fool and their money are lucky to get together in the first place,' " he told Yahoo Finance.
His bigger worry is traders who talk themselves into holding on. "Don't confuse investor language with trader language," he said. "If you're a trader, be a trader."
Intel's long, strange trip
Martin's favorite example is Intel. "A lot of people think like, wow, Intel was 125. I can get it now for half that. It's a bargain," he said. "But at 55 or whatever it is, you can see 40 long before you're gonna see 140."
Intel's own history backs him up. The stock peaked at about $75 in August 2000, was down to half by October, and kept going, bottoming near $13 in 2002.
It didn't close above that dot-com peak again until April 24, 2026. Loyal holders got a victory lap to about $141 in June before the AI selloff dragged the stock back below its old high on Oct. 30. Intel closed Monday at about $59, still up roughly 60% this year.
Intel had plenty of company. Five other dot-com leaders also kept falling after first being cut in half, from another 30% for Microsoft (MSFT) to another 88% for Amazon (AMZN), according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
None of that makes investor language wrong. Amazon now trades at nearly 50 times its 2000 peak.
But that's an investor's clock. Trouble starts when a trade gets judged on one.
How to keep a trade from becoming an accident
Martin, a discretionary trader for four decades, offers guidelines, not rules.
Size it small. If you're just scalping or trading a bounce, think $100 for every $100,000 in an account, or one-tenth of 1%.
Don't take losses home. "If you buy something on Tuesday … if it's showing a loss by Friday, it has to trade."
Know your clock. Younger investors "can buy quality names and hold them forever." Near retirement, "your first order of business here is to play superior defense."

item.title: Nvidia has a 'deep bench' if Jensen Huang steps aside, tech investor says
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Nvidia has a 'deep bench' if Jensen Huang steps aside, tech investor says
2026-11-10
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/nvidia-has-a-deep-bench-if-jensen-huang-steps-aside-tech-investor-says-181907948.html
Nvidia can still crush it in the coming years if embattled CEO Jensen Huang is forced to step away from the company.
When asked how important Huang is to the next few years of the AI chip darling, Niles Investment Management founder and longtime tech investor Dan Niles told Sozzi Unleashed that he "isn't."
"[Huang's] got a very deep bench, and a historical example is what happened to Apple after Steve Jobs passed away. … Did it collapse?" Niles said. "So Jensen's done a great job of empowering people underneath him. I think one thing that will happen is there will be a successor appointed. The board will force that. And so I think that will occur out of this."
"Are the products in the pipeline, much like when Steve Jobs passed away, that will keep the company going for the next couple of years? Absolutely," Niles added. "But is Jensen very important to the company? Completely. So those are two separate thoughts. But they can both coexist."
Read more: Follow live updates and reactions for Nvidia stock
Nvidia's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into reports that a woman CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was allegedly spying on him for the Chinese government.
Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees.
Nvidia stock fell 5% on Monday as a dark cloud settled over Nvidia and its once-Teflon CEO's future.
Niles said this is a "horrible" situation for Huang, someone he has known for 30 years.
"The big question every Nvidia and tech investor is asking this morning … Will Jensen stay on as CEO of Nvidia?" Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives wrote in a note. "The Board investigation will be key and investors are factoring in Jensen will stay on as CEO with a small chance he ultimately is removed or steps aside and the stock is down modestly accordingly. Jensen is the core DNA of Nvidia and its AI success and ambitions are heavily tied to him staying on as CEO."
Ives added, "Jensen is not replaceable ... there is no other person on the management team bench that can step in seamlessly as CEO and that speaks to the key risk now with Nvidia that investors will factor this dynamic to the stock. Jensen has become the global face of the AI Revolution and that now will be front and center for Nvidia how to navigate this very difficult situation looking forward."

item.title: Thanksgiving gas is on track for a record, even after a 6-week slide
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Thanksgiving gas is on track for a record, even after a 6-week slide
2026-11-10
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/thanksgiving-gas-is-on-track-for-a-record-even-after-a-6-week-slide-162015015.html
Gas prices just fell for a sixth straight week. Thanksgiving drivers are still on track to pay more than ever.
Regular gas averaged $4.01 a gallon on Monday, according to AAA. That's down about 10% from its latest peak of nearly $4.48 in late September, based on US Energy Information Administration data.
Wholesale prices have fallen more than twice as fast. Gasoline futures (RB=F) slid about 25% from Sept. 18 through the Nov. 9 close, their lowest finish since March 10, as oil (CL=F) dropped about 23% from its April high.
Pump prices have typically run about $1 a gallon above futures. Based on the Nov. 9 close, that points to about $3.65 a gallon, or roughly 35 more cents of relief, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
"That'll be a 3-handle by mid-next week," market analyst Mike Zaccardi posted on X on Nov. 6, when the average stood at $4.07.
Even that would only tie a record. The highest Thanksgiving-week average in EIA data going back to 1990 is $3.65, set in 2022. The latest weekly reading, for the week of Nov. 2, was $4.15.
Adjusted for inflation, though, this year's $4.50 peak in May comes to about $4.53 in current dollars, far below 2022's $5.71 and 2008's $6.33, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
The slide picked up speed in the week of the Nov. 3 midterms, when pump prices fell 12 cents, the most since June. ING economist James Smith doesn't expect the election to change much.
"Sure, gasoline prices mattered enormously to US voters, and politicians have been surprisingly frank about that," Smith wrote in a Nov. 6 note. "But if diplomacy could not deliver a solution before the elections, why should it suddenly do so now the political clock has reset for two years?"
Diesel is a different story.
The fuel that moves goods by truck and rail hit a record $6.53 a gallon in the week of Sept. 21 and was still about $6.17 on Nov. 9, according to AAA. US stockpiles fell below 100 million barrels in late October, the lowest since 2003, the EIA said.
Those costs are showing up across corporate America. S&P 500 companies mentioned "inflation" or "inflationary" 820 times on October earnings calls, the most since February 2024, Bloomberg reported, as fuel, fertilizer and plastic resin got pricier.
The open question, Chris Versace of TheStreet Pro wrote Monday, is "the length of time to bring supply levels back to normal. That will help dictate how quickly inflation pressures fade, and with it margin relief for companies."
The EIA's next weekly reading is due Monday evening; October Consumer Price Index data follows Tuesday, and the Thanksgiving-week reading comes Nov. 23.
item.content:encoded:
Thanksgiving gas is on track for a record, even after a 6-week slide

2026-11-10

Por Jared Blikre

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/thanksgiving-gas-is-on-track-for-a-record-even-after-a-6-week-slide-162015015.html

Gas prices just fell for a sixth straight week. Thanksgiving drivers are still on track to pay more than ever.

Regular gas averaged $4.01 a gallon on Monday, according to AAA. That's down about 10% from its latest peak of nearly $4.48 in late September, based on US Energy Information Administration data.

Wholesale prices have fallen more than twice as fast. Gasoline futures (RB=F) slid about 25% from Sept. 18 through the Nov. 9 close, their lowest finish since March 10, as oil (CL=F) dropped about 23% from its April high.

Pump prices have typically run about $1 a gallon above futures. Based on the Nov. 9 close, that points to about $3.65 a gallon, or roughly 35 more cents of relief, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

"That'll be a 3-handle by mid-next week," market analyst Mike Zaccardi posted on X on Nov. 6, when the average stood at $4.07.

Even that would only tie a record. The highest Thanksgiving-week average in EIA data going back to 1990 is $3.65, set in 2022. The latest weekly reading, for the week of Nov. 2, was $4.15.

Adjusted for inflation, though, this year's $4.50 peak in May comes to about $4.53 in current dollars, far below 2022's $5.71 and 2008's $6.33, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

The slide picked up speed in the week of the Nov. 3 midterms, when pump prices fell 12 cents, the most since June. ING economist James Smith doesn't expect the election to change much.

"Sure, gasoline prices mattered enormously to US voters, and politicians have been surprisingly frank about that," Smith wrote in a Nov. 6 note. "But if diplomacy could not deliver a solution before the elections, why should it suddenly do so now the political clock has reset for two years?"

Diesel is a different story.

The fuel that moves goods by truck and rail hit a record $6.53 a gallon in the week of Sept. 21 and was still about $6.17 on Nov. 9, according to AAA. US stockpiles fell below 100 million barrels in late October, the lowest since 2003, the EIA said.

Those costs are showing up across corporate America. S&P 500 companies mentioned "inflation" or "inflationary" 820 times on October earnings calls, the most since February 2024, Bloomberg reported, as fuel, fertilizer and plastic resin got pricier.

The open question, Chris Versace of TheStreet Pro wrote Monday, is "the length of time to bring supply levels back to normal. That will help dictate how quickly inflation pressures fade, and with it margin relief for companies."

The EIA's next weekly reading is due Monday evening; October Consumer Price Index data follows Tuesday, and the Thanksgiving-week reading comes Nov. 23.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO dilemma after the AI sell-off: 'Damned if you do, damned if you don't'
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Anthropic's IPO dilemma after the AI sell-off: 'Damned if you do, damned if you don't'
2026-11-10
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/anthropics-ipo-dilemma-after-the-ai-sell-off-damned-if-you-do-damned-if-you-dont-231326634.html
This past week's stock market meltdown could hardly have come at a more critical moment for Anthropic (ANTH.PVT). The sell-off cast a shadow over the frontier artificial intelligence developer's expected pre-Thanksgiving public debut, raising questions about its potential valuation and ability to sustain the next phase of AI growth.
"The only thing that matters the rest of this year is the Anthropic IPO," said Neostellar principal Willy Lee on Yahoo Finance's Market Hang. Lee said investors want to know whether Anthropic can sustain long-term growth and secure a meaningful share of the AI market.
"Those are the two questions that every investor is asking within their investment committee every single day before the IPO," said Lee.
Anthropic recently revealed revenue grew $1,206% to $33.2 billion through the first nine months of the year. The company also noted a staggering aggregate committed spend of $895.4 billion, which it says is primarily related to compute and infrastructure.
But the AI growth story was put to the test this past week as investors weighed a Democratic congressional win against the impact of the AI data center build-out. On Thursday, the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) suffered its worst daily decline since April 2025, with chip stocks leading the declines.
The market turmoil prompted prospective buyers to discuss lowering Anthropic's valuation to a range of $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, with some considering as low as $1.1 trillion, according to Bloomberg. That's far below estimates as high as $2 trillion projected in early October.
Amid increasingly jittery sentiment toward AI stocks, Anthropic faces a difficult decision, particularly if the unwinding of the AI trade continues.
"It would be difficult to go public," Anna Rathbun, founder and CEO of Grenadilla Advisory, told Yahoo Finance's Market Hang.
If Anthropic decides to delay its IPO, investors could interpret the move as a bearish signal for the AI trade, said Kevin Mahn, chief investment officer at Hennion & Walsh.
"If they don't delay, and their IPO fails, or comes in below expectations, that could be perceived as bearish to certain investors," said Mahn. "Damned if you do, damned if you don't."
Investors will also be looking for clues about the health of the AI trade on Nov. 17, when Nvidia (NVDA) reports earnings. With hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta (META) having already reported, along with foundry Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) and chip equipment maker ASML (ASML), expectations are high that Nvidia will once again beat earnings estimates and raise its guidance.
"We got so much confirmation already," said Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum. "I give it a 1% chance that they miss."

item.title: The stock market is doing some of the Fed's dirty work
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
The stock market is doing some of the Fed's dirty work
2026-11-10
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/the-stock-market-is-doing-some-of-the-feds-dirty-work-080000516.html
The odds of a Fed rate hike are creeping upward. A strong jobs report last week cemented the argument further for another raise. And inflation figures coming later today are expected to confirm that pricing pressures remain stubbornly high.
Together, that's a compelling case — elevated pricing pressures call for a hike, while healthy jobs figures provide cover for tamping down the economy.
The odds for a 25 basis point hike at the Fed's December meeting are over 80%, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
But a new analysis from DataTrek co-founder Nicholas Colas suggests that the recent volatility on Wall Street is also doing some heavy lifting for the Fed — potentially removing the need for subsequent hikes next year.
"Stock market volatility and lower equity prices are one definition of 'tighter financial conditions,'" Colas wrote in the note. That means that Fed funds futures see the recent action on Wall Street as reducing the need for the central bank to intervene.
After the expected hike next month, the market forecasts the Fed will stay the course through at least the first quarter of 2027. Chances of the next increase aren't considered likely until April. Overall odds of a more hawkish rate policy have diminished, with the odds for no or one hike in 2027 now at 68%, up from 57% a week prior, Colas said.
One of Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's catchphrases is that "markets are doing some of the Fed's work for it." As Colas noted, that's increasingly coming true.
But recent tech jitters can also make the Fed's job more difficult, adding another layer of uncertainty and reorienting the public's expectations on top of the fact that the market and the Fed respond to each other.
If the tech sell-off takes off again and markets begin to anticipate a troubled growth story, the Fed might jump to action to reassure Wall Street. Right now, a little bit of selling is saving the Fed from some trouble. But a heavier dose of pessimism could be self-reinforcing.
Follow Hamza Shaban on X @hshaban.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's debacle highlights this one glaring issue
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's debacle highlights this one glaring issue
2026-11-10
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huangs-debacle-highlights-this-one-glaring-issue-110147953.html
The Nvidia (NVDA) story has been led by Jensen Huang since the company's founding in 1993, sketched out on a napkin at a Denny's.
Huang's passion for computing chips (first gaming chips, now AI chips) was on display in an endless stream of interviews, in his signing autographs for enthusiastic fans on his world travels, and in his fried chicken dinner with fellow tech titans overseas that went viral.
His star power was evident in the curiosity among the crowds at the annual GTC event about which black leather jacket he would wear on stage to pump up the future of AI.
The market's infatuation with Nvidia has gone hand in hand with its infatuation with Huang and the technology he pioneered, which helped create one of the world's most valuable companies.
Huang is like Nvidia's sun — the center around which the whole show runs.
But a fresh scandal involving the most visible CEO in the world has raised a valid question among investors, perhaps for the first time ever.
What in the world is Nvidia's succession plan? Does one even exist?
"Every high-profile company carries key-person risk, and Nvidia is no exception," FedWatch strategist Ben Emons said. "While Jensen Huang's full cooperation suggests, in my view, that he has little reason to conceal information and likely did not share sensitive data with the alleged spy, the initial cover-up and later disclosures will still likely weigh on investor confidence."
Nvidia's board of directors has launched an independent investigation into reports that a woman CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was allegedly spying on him for the Chinese government.
Huang admitted to the affair on Sunday in an email to employees.
Nvidia shares fell 5% in early trading on Monday as a dark cloud settled over Nvidia and its once-Teflon CEO's future.
Huang has never talked about a succession plan publicly. Nor is anything of the sort disclosed in public filings such as proxy statements or the annual report. The only two people on Nvidia's earnings calls are Huang and longtime CFO Colette Kress.
The top four leaders on Nvidia's investor relations page all hold the title of executive vice president: Colette Kress, Nick Parker, Debora Shoquist, and Tim Teter. Usually at these levels of leadership, someone being groomed as a CEO successor would also carry the president title alongside their formal title, such as CFO or COO.
By all outward indications, Huang has displayed the typical behavior for an ultra-wealthy founder CEO — one that thinks they'll be doing the job forever and won't slow down at all. For these folks, succession planning is usually far down the totem pole.

item.title: Analysts says Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company’s future
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
Analysts says Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company’s future
2026-11-10
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/analysts-say-nvidia-ceo-unlikely-to-be-ousted-over-affair-but-raise-questions-about-companys-future-165238577.html
Analysts say Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company's future
Wall Street analysts are reacting to news of Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy with a mixture of caution and concern about the company's future and what the episode means for the AI industry.
Nvidia stock fell in early trading Monday.
In an email to Nvidia employees, Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized to his family. The company's board has launched an independent investigation into the matter, but noted that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."
The woman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Singapore data center company MegaSpeed, which has been the subject of investigations into whether it smuggled Nvidia chips into China.
One of the company's co-founders, Jensen Huang, is instrumental to the AI boom and closely guides Nvidia's strategy.
Moor Insights & Strategy CEO and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead told Yahoo Finance that he doesn't believe Huang will be pushed out unless the board's investigation turns up anything.
"The issue is that Jensen is the product strategist, the closer with the hyperscalers, and the face of the company in Washington and Beijing. This story puts that last role at risk," Moorehead said.
Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to investors that the board's initial statement reduces the chances that it plans to oust Huang, but said doing so would be a significant negative for the company due to his "hands-on operating style."
But he wrote that the incident could hurt the CEO's credibility.
"Regardless of the outcome of the investigation, however, we necessarily see Jensen losing some of his power/credibility in advocating for AI and Nvidia with US government representatives (whether free trade with foreign entities or how the government regulates AI development)," Bryson wrote.
Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein, meanwhile, wrote in a note following the news that the board investigation will likely overshadow Nvidia's earnings report on Nov. 17.
"A lot of risk associated with Jensen Huang and his status as CEO…cannot be hedged out. He is too important for NVDA and the entire industry. I would assume the investigation finds no serious wrongdoing or anything criminal. Jensen likely remains CEO; nothing changes in the long run," Klein said.
Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon pointed out that the incident will increase scrutiny of Nvidia in Washington.
The headlines are "(at the very best) going to be a heavy distraction, and at the worst provide significant ammunition to both sides of the aisle, from China hawks (of which there are many on Capitol Hill) already displeased with the current US stance toward the country, to incoming Democrats unhappy with the close ties to Trump that Jensen has cultivated over the last few years," he wrote in an investor note.
item.content:encoded:
Analysts says Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company’s future

2026-11-10

Por Daniel Howley

https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/analysts-say-nvidia-ceo-unlikely-to-be-ousted-over-affair-but-raise-questions-about-companys-future-165238577.html

Analysts say Nvidia CEO unlikely to be ousted over affair, but raise questions about company's future

Wall Street analysts are reacting to news of Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy with a mixture of caution and concern about the company's future and what the episode means for the AI industry.

Nvidia stock fell in early trading Monday.

In an email to Nvidia employees, Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized to his family. The company's board has launched an independent investigation into the matter, but noted that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

The woman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Singapore data center company MegaSpeed, which has been the subject of investigations into whether it smuggled Nvidia chips into China.

One of the company's co-founders, Jensen Huang, is instrumental to the AI boom and closely guides Nvidia's strategy.

Moor Insights & Strategy CEO and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead told Yahoo Finance that he doesn't believe Huang will be pushed out unless the board's investigation turns up anything.

"The issue is that Jensen is the product strategist, the closer with the hyperscalers, and the face of the company in Washington and Beijing. This story puts that last role at risk," Moorehead said.

Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to investors that the board's initial statement reduces the chances that it plans to oust Huang, but said doing so would be a significant negative for the company due to his "hands-on operating style."

But he wrote that the incident could hurt the CEO's credibility.

"Regardless of the outcome of the investigation, however, we necessarily see Jensen losing some of his power/credibility in advocating for AI and Nvidia with US government representatives (whether free trade with foreign entities or how the government regulates AI development)," Bryson wrote.

Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein, meanwhile, wrote in a note following the news that the board investigation will likely overshadow Nvidia's earnings report on Nov. 17.

"A lot of risk associated with Jensen Huang and his status as CEO…cannot be hedged out. He is too important for NVDA and the entire industry. I would assume the investigation finds no serious wrongdoing or anything criminal. Jensen likely remains CEO; nothing changes in the long run," Klein said.

Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon pointed out that the incident will increase scrutiny of Nvidia in Washington.

The headlines are "(at the very best) going to be a heavy distraction, and at the worst provide significant ammunition to both sides of the aisle, from China hawks (of which there are many on Capitol Hill) already displeased with the current US stance toward the country, to incoming Democrats unhappy with the close ties to Trump that Jensen has cultivated over the last few years," he wrote in an investor note.

item.title: Why Nvidia's alleged Chinese spy scandal is going to confuse markets — and the government
item.author: Yahoo Finance
item.description:
Why Nvidia's alleged Chinese spy scandal is going to confuse markets — and the government
2026-11-10
Por Yahoo Finance
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/why-nvidias-alleged-chinese-spy-scandal-is-going-to-confuse-markets--and-the-government-110000900.html
Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang is at the center of a massive scandal that's rocking the AI giant's stock.
It's also raising fresh questions about the company's relationship with China — and its stance on selling advanced technology to an economic adversary.
Huang admitted in a Nov. 8 memo to employees to an affair following reports of a relationship with Alice Huang (obviously no relation), whom US intelligence officials believe worked for China's Ministry of State Security. "I was unfaithful to my wife," he wrote. Nvidia's board has initiated an investigation.
Wall Street reaction so far has been negative but not catastrophic, with analysts questioning whether Huang will stay on while acknowledging how central he is to the company and the broader AI revolution. (Here's a suite of reactions.)
A key lesson in key-man risk if we've ever seen one.
But most critically, the Huang Affair has made it impossible to know where Beijing's alleged intelligence scheme ends and Nvidia's genuine policy aims begin. Everything is now in question.
In lobbying for looser export controls with China, was Huang motivated by revenue streams or an illicit romance? Getting entangled in a Chinese spy plot blurs the lines between the company's actual beliefs and what Chinese intelligence officials attempted to accomplish, sowing confusion in markets and the government.
"Regardless of the outcome of the investigation, however, we necessarily see Jensen losing some of his power/credibility in advocating for AI and Nvidia with US government representatives," Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson wrote.
It's hard to know and implausible to argue the difference between Nvidia's financial interests and China's intelligence scheme. Even if the alleged Chinese spy had zero influence on Huang's decision making and extracted zero intelligence from him and his company, Huang's messiness makes Nvidia appear impaired.
But Huang's importance atop the AI mountain makes him a crucial player in the US economy. President Trump and leaders in the tech world have come to his defense. The logic behind it is that Huang is so pivotal to American AI competitiveness that not even his irresponsible actions outweigh his worth and standing as a tech leader.
But Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives said in a note on Monday that the investigation will boost major scrutiny of Nvidia and tip the thorny China chip export issue further toward bipartisanship.
"On the heels of last week's Blue Tidal Wave this will also increase momentum for more regulatory scrutiny in the Beltway especially around China and chip restrictions at a time the AI Arms Race is heating up into its next gear between the US and China," he said.

item.title: Trump is defending Jensen Huang but his fellow Republicans could put him under pressure even before Democrats take over in January
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump is defending Jensen Huang but his fellow Republicans could put him under pressure even before Democrats take over in January
2026-11-10
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/trump-defends-jensen-huang-but-other-republicans-could-turn-up-the-pressure-quickly-144235766.html
President Trump defended Jensen Huang on Sunday night, calling the embattled Nvidia chief "an honorable guy." But members of the president's own party have signaled they could offer more pointed questioning even before the Democrats take power on Capitol Hill in January.
Trump told reporters he thinks Huang should stay on as CEO, adding that he would even be open to having him along for a trip scheduled for next week to Shenzhen, China.
"I think he probably has an excuse for it," Trump said after Huang admitted to an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy. "He's done an amazing job for our country."
Other Republicans have suggested they might be more critical.
Last Thursday, three influential House Republicans requested that Huang voluntarily appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang has now admitted to having an affair.
"It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk," the leaders wrote in a letter asking Huang to appear by next week or provide an alternative date by this Wednesday.
The committee didn't offer immediate comment on Monday morning about whether that would change, but other lawmakers weighed in on the quickly growing scandal. Lawmakers are returning to Washington this week following the election recess.
Outgoing Texas Sen. John Cornyn posted "Congressional oversight investigation needed."
Some members of Trump's team are also reportedly more wary of Huang. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly personally oversaw a classified intelligence memo earlier this year that warned senior officials about potential issues, according to the New York Times.
Nvidia's board of directors has ordered an independent investigation of reports that the executive at a Singapore-based company with whom Huang was having an affair was working for the Chinese government.
In a statement Sunday, the board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised."
China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied any spy plot, calling the accusations "nothing but smears against China."
Yet the quickly growing scandal could change the tenor of Trump's travel to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit on Nov. 18 — whether or not Huang is in attendance.
Hope for the MATCH Act?
The scandal could also boost momentum for action on the Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act, which aims to tighten international export controls on advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

item.title: Fed’s Barkin Says Policy Direction Clear, But Needs Careful Pace
item.author: Enda Curran; Aidan Williams
item.description:
Fed’s Barkin Says Policy Direction Clear, But Needs Careful Pace
2026-11-10
Por Enda Curran; Aidan Williams
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fed-barkin-says-policy-direction-170606304.html
(Bloomberg) -- Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond President Tom Barkin signaled robust demand and stubbornly high inflation mean interest rates will need to go higher, though he cautioned that any hikes will need to be done at a careful pace.
Most Read from Bloomberg
In a speech outlining his overview of the economy, Barkin described corporate profits as remarkable and noted that consumers continue to spend in an economy experiencing a record streak of unemployment at or below 4.5%.
But he cautioned on how long consumer strength can last and highlighted that both businesses and households continue to complain about rising costs, making the path but not the pace clear for policymakers.Rich
"The appropriate direction of monetary policy is relatively straightforward," Barkin said in a speech in South Carolina. "However, risks to the demand outlook remain easy to envision. Because of that, it is wise to move policy with care."
Fed officials held interest rates steady last month, saying the "accumulation of more information" would allow them to determine the best level for policy. The 10-2 decision to stay put followed a unanimous move to lift the benchmark rate in September by a quarter percentage point to a target range of 3.75% to 4%.
Several policymakers speaking since the meeting have touted the need for additional rate hikes, and traders see about an 80% chance of a hike in December.
Data last week showed jobs growth surged in October. and the unemployment rate edged lower. Fed officials will see one more jobs report and a full slate of inflation data — beginning with the consumer price index for October on Tuesday — before they gather again in December.
Barkin described the AI boom as the "elephant in the room" for policymakers. How it plays out will be especially consequential for the economy in the near term, he said.
"If it underdelivers, business investment could pull back, stock prices could follow, and so too could asset-fueled consumer spending," Barkin said. "The risk runs the other way, too. AI could overdeliver and displace more workers than expected, resulting in a pullback in spending. Either scenario would move attention to the maximum employment part of our mandate."

item.title: Nvidia stock sinks 4% as chipmaker investigates CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia stock sinks 4% as chipmaker investigates CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy
2026-11-10
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-stock-sinks-as-chipmaker-investigates-ceo-jensen-huangs-relationship-with-alleged-chinese-spy-130346548.html
Nvidia stock sinks 4% as chipmaker investigates CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with alleged Chinese spy
Nvidia (NVDA) stock trimmed losses to fall 4% on Monday after the chipmaker's board announced it would investigate the relationship between CEO Jensen Huang and a woman whom the intelligence community believes could be a Chinese Spy. The rest of the tech (XLK) sector, however, rallied.
In a Sunday memo to employees, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair, apologizing to his family and staff while pledging full cooperation with an independent board review. Wall Street analysts quickly flagged the heightened 'key-person risk' for the world's leading AI chipmaker.
"Jensen is the core DNA of Nvidia, and its AI success and ambitions are heavily tied to him staying on as CEO. Jensen is not replaceable," Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives wrote on Monday morning.
A look across the semiconductor sector showed the risk damage was largely contained to Nvidia. Shares of rival AMD (AMD) bounced 13% after an upgrade to Buy from Oppenheimer analysts. Broadcom (AVGO) rose 8%, while Intel (INTC) edged up 5%.
Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which manufactures Nvidia chips, rose nearly 4%, while semiconductor equipment maker ASML (ASML) also gained 6%.
Storage maker SanDisk (SNDK) moved up 6%. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) rose more than 6%, while SK Hynix (SKHY) gained 5%.
Other chip-related stocks include processor maker Qualcomm (QCOM) and semicondcutor designer Arm Holdings (ARM), moving up about 3% and 6% respectively.
Meanwhile, Alphabet (GOOGL) shares rose more than 1% on Monday after the tech giant introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs. Alphabet has been accelerating its homegrown AI chip business, introducing four TPU systems in a single year.

"Jensen is the core DNA of Nvidia, and its AI success and ambitions are heavily tied to him staying on as CEO. Jensen is not replaceable," Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives wrote on Monday morning.

A look across the semiconductor sector showed the risk damage was largely contained to Nvidia. Shares of rival AMD (AMD) bounced 13% after an upgrade to Buy from Oppenheimer analysts. Broadcom (AVGO) rose 8%, while Intel (INTC) edged up 5%.

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which manufactures Nvidia chips, rose nearly 4%, while semiconductor equipment maker ASML (ASML) also gained 6%.

Storage maker SanDisk (SNDK) moved up 6%. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) rose more than 6%, while SK Hynix (SKHY) gained 5%.

Other chip-related stocks include processor maker Qualcomm (QCOM) and semicondcutor designer Arm Holdings (ARM), moving up about 3% and 6% respectively.

Meanwhile, Alphabet (GOOGL) shares rose more than 1% on Monday after the tech giant introduced two new tensor processing units, or TPUs. Alphabet has been accelerating its homegrown AI chip business, introducing four TPU systems in a single year.

item.title: Google Escalates Nvidia Rivalry With Specialized Versions of AI Chips
item.author: Dina Bass
item.description:
Google Escalates Nvidia Rivalry With Specialized Versions of AI Chips
2026-11-10
Por Dina Bass
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/google-escalates-nvidia-rivalry-specialized-123000247.html
(Bloomberg) -- Alphabet Inc.'s Google (GOOG) is rolling out a broader array of artificial intelligence chips, aiming to capitalize on its rapid ascent as a challenger to Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) in a market worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The company is introducing two new variations of its tensor processing units, or TPUs, custom-made semiconductors that help develop and run AI software. The latest chips will address the need for confidential computing and help models access a wider range of information when handling queries. More broadly, they're meant to serve an industry that's shifting toward the use of AI agents and confronting security challenges.
The rollout marks an acceleration in product development for Google's chip unit. The business once released a new AI processor every two years. This year, it put out two at the same time. And the latest variations, due to be announced Monday, will add additional flavors to that pair of chips.
The four TPU offerings will optimize different needs, Google chip chief Amin Vahdat said in an interview. "This really follows the thesis that we have here at Google, which is that the future is going to be about specialization, and the upsides for specialization continue to be significant."
Google is staking its claim at a tumultuous time for the AI chip industry. Concerns about a potential slowdown in infrastructure spending have roiled tech stocks, and US midterm elections that swept Democrats into power have raised fresh doubts about data center projects. But the demand for AI processors from Nvidia remains larger than it can satisfy, and that's left room for Google and other contenders to build a sizable business.
The new TPU 8tx and 8i Max variations aren't completely new silicon designs — rather, they're reconfigured to take on tasks that customers have been requesting, Vahdat said.
The 8tx is aimed at handling secure, confidential work for customers like government agencies and companies in regulated industries. The system works with chips from Advanced Micro Devices Inc., part of a collaboration between the two companies.
The 8i Max, meanwhile, is meant to run AI applications that require long-context windows — the amount of data an AI system can consider in a single request. That's necessary for things like drug discovery and math but is also important for coding applications, Vahdat said.
TPUs compete in a market dominated by Nvidia's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Google set out to develop the technology more than a decade ago, alongside Broadcom Inc., which helped with design and coordinating production. The initial idea was to more efficiently handle the search giant's burgeoning computing needs. It then realized the potential of TPUs for doing AI work and has now begun selling them outside of its cloud-computing operation.
Google's new life as a chip seller is proving lucrative. By 2028, TPU sales will top $135 billion, including related software and hardware, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. That's up from an estimated $12 billion this year, and it doesn't include sales from clients using the chips through Google Cloud.
TPUs have netted some high-profile clients, including Apple Inc., Meta Platforms Inc. and Oracle Corp. And offering specialized versions of the chips should help Google make further progress, Vahdat said. The variations will be available next year, he said.
"We could build a single chip that tries to address the whole market, or by building specialized versions of the chips, we actually can deliver much more value," he said.
Even Nvidia, which has historically promoted its GPUs as a product for all AI tasks, is starting to offer more specialized chip systems. That includes offering its own central processi

item.title: Blockbuster October jobs report keeps Fed rate hike in play for December
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Blockbuster October jobs report keeps Fed rate hike in play for December
2026-11-09
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/blockbuster-october-jobs-report-keeps-fed-rate-hike-in-play-for-december-135325070.html
A much stronger-than-expected October jobs report solidified expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December as officials remain focused on higher inflation.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics report released Friday showed that 165,000 jobs were created in October, compared with expectations of around 70,000, and the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, compared with expectations of 4.2%. That's much higher than the average monthly gain of 48,000 over the past 12 months and well above the roughly 30,000 jobs needed to hold employment steady. Over the past three months, payrolls are averaging 137,000. Labor force participation inched up to a hair above expectations at 61.9%.
Job gains in both August and September were revised higher by 84,000. The bulk of jobs added were in the sectors of professional and business services, healthcare, and transportation and warehousing. Manufacturing added 19,000 jobs.
"The policy takeaway on the report is that the Fed will move confidently towards the December rate hike of twenty-five basis points as the economic expansion steams ahead," RMS economist Joe Brusuelas said.
Read more: How jobs, inflation, and the Fed are all related
While job gains are picking up, wage growth remains somewhat muted. Wages grew 3.1% in October, compared with expectations for 2.9%.
Diane Swonk, chief economist for KPMG, noted the dichotomy between wage growth and inflation. While wages have increased, average hourly earnings remain below the overall pace of inflation, even as the economy is adding more paychecks, buoying spending power and demand. Yet she said inflation is acting as a regressive tax, with lower- and middle-income households getting hit harder than affluent households.
"That's a sticking point for the Fed," Swonk told Yahoo Finance.
"If you allow inflation to metastasize, it is like a cancer," she added. "What they're hoping to do is to cool inflation on the margins by going up more incrementally, not in the aggressive way they did in 2022."
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh noted these dynamics following the last policy meeting, in which the Fed held rates steady. He pointed to payroll growth that is noticeably above last year's pace, the four-week moving average of unemployment insurance claims that continues to run at the lowest level in generations, and that "on the employment side of the Fed's dual mandate, conditions are quite positive."
"Yet Americans, of course, are still dealing with inflation that has been running above the Committee's objective for close to 6 years," he said. "It's our responsibility to get inflation down. That's the reason the FOMC's discussion over the last couple of days focused mainly on the price stability side of our remit."

item.title: OpenAI Completes $11 Billion Portion of Funding at $1.25 Trillion Value
item.author: Natasha Mascarenhas; Rebecca Torrence
item.description:
OpenAI Completes $11 Billion Portion of Funding at $1.25 Trillion Value
2026-11-09
Por Natasha Mascarenhas; Rebecca Torrence
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-completes-11-billion-portion-205841010.html
(Bloomberg) -- OpenAI has closed on new funding of roughly $11 billion, the initial part of a round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, according to people familiar with the matter.The funding was wired to the company as of Friday, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public. The remainder of the round, which could increase to as much as $20 billion in total, is expected to be completed in the coming weeks, one person said.The AI developer has been in talks for more than a month to raise a large funding round after delaying its plans for an initial public offering. OpenAI initially set out to raise $30 billion or more at a $1.4 trillion valuation, Bloomberg News has reported, before scaling back its plans amid a public market rout for the AI sector.OpenAI declined to comment. The Wall Street Journal previously reported some details of the funding. The reduced funding goals represent a stark shift for a fundraising juggernaut that helped usher in the current AI boom. The sentiment around AI has also changed dramatically since the round kicked off, due to concerns about the spending spree on physical infrastructure for artificial intelligence and the potential for new roadblocks to data center construction following the US midterm elections.OpenAI raised $122 billion in a March funding round at an $852 billion valuation.

item.title: Wall Street Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
item.author: Ryan Gould
item.description:
Wall Street Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
2026-11-09
Por Ryan Gould
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-street-races-megadeals-countdown-140000480.html
Wall Street Races for Megadeals as Countdown Begins on Trump Era
Ryan Gould
6 min read
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump's return to the White House changed the political calculus around mergers and acquisitions, reviving companies' desire for dream deals that had become difficult to pull off. Now, corporate America is on the clock.
The rout by the Democrats in the midterms is creating a sudden sense of urgency in boardrooms, with executives wondering if they might have one last chance to pull off a transformational transaction while M&A-friendly regulators remain in place under Trump.
Conversations with top advisers suggest the result is already prompting companies to ask whether they should move fast to bring big strategic moves forward. There's a realization that a resurgent Democratic Party could work to frustrate the kind of blockbuster dealmaking that's built up steam during Trump 2.0. and powered record revenue on Wall Street.
Kevin Foley, co-head of investment banking at JPMorgan Chase & Co., one of the world's top advisory firms, said companies should be ready to transact through another complicated operating environment.
"The biggest risk may be assuming that, sooner or later, things go back to normal," New York-based Foley said. "Standing still is always an option, but when industries are changing this fast, it's the wrong one."
Fernando Rivas, a senior Wells Fargo & Co. banker, put it more starkly at an industry conference in Boston on Thursday when he said a "now or never" mentality will return to drive M&A in the near term.
Trump's two terms have accounted for an outsized share of the biggest deals. More than half of all announced transactions worth at least $50 billion and involving a US company over the past two decades have come while he was president, according to analysis of Bloomberg-compiled data.
This year alone has seen landmark combinations in mission-critical sectors like power and technology, such as this month's record-breaking $100 billion-plus takeover of laser maker Lumentum Holdings Inc. by Marvell Technology Inc. Elsewhere, the Department of Justice cleared Paramount Skydance Corp.'s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. without antitrust remedies.
There's a particular urgency to get going with these more complex transactions. Megadeals can take months to negotiate and even longer to clear regulatory reviews around the world. Companies that wait until a 2028 presidential campaign is in full swing to move ahead with such deals risk seeing them become political footballs at the stump.
"If you have a major transaction that is going to take time to put together and get through the process, you really have to start working on it now and probably announce it by the middle of 2027," said Paul Nary, assistant professor of management at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School. "There isn't that much time left."
Balance Shift
A major test case for mega M&A in the new landscape could be the potential combination of Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla Inc., which would be among the biggest and most politically sensitive corporate tie-ups ever attempted and reveal the extent of the billionaire's influence with Trump as the balance of power in Washington begins to shift.
Bloomberg News has reported that Musk, who spent almost $500 million supporting Republican candidates in key midterm races, is pushing to announce a merger of his two largest companies by the first half of 2027. But things have become more complicated; shares in both SpaceX and Tesla have slumped amid concerns that a Democrat-led Congress will probe Musk's business and political dealings and, more broadly, look to slow the artificial intelligence boom he has consistently championed.
While Democrats will not ta
