The rout by the Democrats in the midterms is creating a sudden sense of urgency in boardrooms, with executives wondering if they might have one last chance to pull off a transformational transaction while M&A-friendly regulators remain in place under Trump.

Conversations with top advisers suggest the result is already prompting companies to ask whether they should move fast to bring big strategic moves forward. There's a realization that a resurgent Democratic Party could work to frustrate the kind of blockbuster dealmaking that's built up steam during Trump 2.0. and powered record revenue on Wall Street.

Kevin Foley, co-head of investment banking at JPMorgan Chase & Co., one of the world's top advisory firms, said companies should be ready to transact through another complicated operating environment.

"The biggest risk may be assuming that, sooner or later, things go back to normal," New York-based Foley said. "Standing still is always an option, but when industries are changing this fast, it's the wrong one."

Fernando Rivas, a senior Wells Fargo & Co. banker, put it more starkly at an industry conference in Boston on Thursday when he said a "now or never" mentality will return to drive M&A in the near term.

Trump's two terms have accounted for an outsized share of the biggest deals. More than half of all announced transactions worth at least $50 billion and involving a US company over the past two decades have come while he was president, according to analysis of Bloomberg-compiled data.

This year alone has seen landmark combinations in mission-critical sectors like power and technology, such as this month's record-breaking $100 billion-plus takeover of laser maker Lumentum Holdings Inc. by Marvell Technology Inc. Elsewhere, the Department of Justice cleared Paramount Skydance Corp.'s $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. without antitrust remedies.

There's a particular urgency to get going with these more complex transactions. Megadeals can take months to negotiate and even longer to clear regulatory reviews around the world. Companies that wait until a 2028 presidential campaign is in full swing to move ahead with such deals risk seeing them become political footballs at the stump.

"If you have a major transaction that is going to take time to put together and get through the process, you really have to start working on it now and probably announce it by the middle of 2027," said Paul Nary, assistant professor of management at the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton School. "There isn't that much time left."

Balance Shift

A major test case for mega M&A in the new landscape could be the potential combination of Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla Inc., which would be among the biggest and most politically sensitive corporate tie-ups ever attempted and reveal the extent of the billionaire's influence with Trump as the balance of power in Washington begins to shift.

Bloomberg News has reported that Musk, who spent almost $500 million supporting Republican candidates in key midterm races, is pushing to announce a merger of his two largest companies by the first half of 2027. But things have become more complicated; shares in both SpaceX and Tesla have slumped amid concerns that a Democrat-led Congress will probe Musk's business and political dealings and, more broadly, look to slow the artificial intelligence boom he has consistently championed.

item.title: Elizabeth Warren will take over the Senate Banking Committee next year. Expect hearings.
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Elizabeth Warren will take over the Senate Banking Committee next year. Expect hearings.
2026-11-09
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/elizabeth-warren-will-take-over-the-senate-banking-committee-next-year-expect-hearings-205713342.html
Democratic firebrand Elizabeth Warren, a consumer advocate known for her fierce battles over financial regulations, will take the gavel in January to become chair of the powerful Senate Banking Committee.
According to a source familiar with her plans, the Massachusetts senator intends to use her expanded platform to advance legislation to tackle populist affordability issues with a focus on housing.
The person familiar with her plans says Warren will use the committee's investigative powers to hold hearings and launch investigations into executive branch ethics and corporate practices, aiming to hold President Trump, the administration, Wall Street, and Big Tech accountable for economic decisions she views as having driven up costs for consumers.
Warren is also expected to take steps to shield the Federal Reserve from White House overreach. Any future nominee for the Fed will have to go through her committee. Earlier this year, she rallied Democrats to oppose Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's confirmation before the banking committee, stalling his eventual confirmation.
Wall Street is likely to be another of Warren's targets. Before Republicans regained control of Congress, Democrats would have the chief executives of big banks testify before the Senate Banking and House Financial Services committees once a year. The banking industry can expect a return to that practice.
Stephen Biggar, who covers the financial sector for Argus Research, says hearings will offer more transparency, but won't be accompanied by meaningful rulemaking. Biggar expects increased oversight, potentially more consumer protections, and actions to limit banks' market share size, such as blocking mergers.
He added that there are concerns that the deregulation efforts and lower capital requirements for banks championed by Republicans are now at risk.
James Angel, an associate professor at Georgetown University's McDonough School of Business, said he thinks the hearings will accomplish two things: producing information and sound bites that will get people to pay attention and galvanize public opinion. Second, Angel says they will serve as a deterrent for people in power.
"If people will be held under oath and there's a prospect of perjury, that will deter people from doing 'Trumpier' things," Angel said in an interview.
Angel also noted that any Trump appointee who has to be confirmed by Warren's committee will need to withstand bipartisan scrutiny and thus is more likely to be a moderate.

item.title: Nvidia faces a more hostile Washington
item.author: Ashley Gold
item.description:
Nvidia faces a more hostile Washington
2026-11-09
Por Ashley Gold
https://www.semafor.com/article/11/06/2026/nvidia-faces-a-more-hostile-washington
CEO Jensen Huang’s close relationship with President Trump is unlikely to inoculate the company from an increasingly hostile Washington, as Democrats prepare to take over regulatory committees and key Republicans look to impose stronger high tech export controls.
Plus, three Republican House members recently requested Huang appear in a private briefing on whether he was the target of a Chinese spy. Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo did not directly answer whether Huang would attend the briefing, telling Semafor in a statement: “We’re confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know. We often receive updates from the U.S. government regarding parties and entities of concern and always act accordingly.”
In the lame duck, a must-pass defense bill could include export control measures that would further restrict chip sales to China. (It could pass even more easily next year.) Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., likely the next chair of the Senate Banking Committee, has long wanted Huang to testify before Congress on Nvidia’s tranche of deals with other tech companies, and chip sales to China.
Trump will have to decide if protecting Huang’s interest is more important than working with Congress on this issue as the debate over AI shifts.

item.title: Blackstone Real Estate Seeks Rebound From Shock Exits and Losses
item.author: Preeti Singh; Patrick Clark
item.description:
Blackstone Real Estate Seeks Rebound From Shock Exits and Losses
2026-11-09
Por Preeti Singh; Patrick Clark
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/articles/blackstone-real-estate-seeks-rebound-170001970.html
(Bloomberg) -- Steve Schwarzman was concerned. It had been a rough stretch for Blackstone's real estate division. The market was brutal, and the shooting death of Wesley LePatner at the firm's New York headquarters nearly a year earlier still weighed heavily on the group.
Most Read from Bloomberg
To try to raise morale, Schwarzman invited top leaders from Blackstone's real estate business to his Manhattan apartment for dinner in June. The billionaire founder and his handpicked heir apparent, Jon Gray, wanted to see firsthand how they were holding up.
Over the course of the meal, Schwarzman played both coach and cheerleader. He emphasized how important real estate was to Blackstone's legacy and to its future. He was confident that market conditions were finally improving. Under new leader Nadeem Meghji, the group would lay the groundwork for a $30 billion fundraise later in the year.
Lifting spirits further, staff members delivered periodic updates from the NBA finals game underway at Madison Square Garden: The New York Knicks continued to defy odds and expectations. Anything seemed possible.
But the five months since have only brought more tumult for a group that was once a crown jewel for the $1.4 trillion firm. In September, Meghji, the head of the unit, announced his plans to leave, less than 10 months after the departure of his former co-head Kathleen McCarthy. The real estate market is getting slammed yet again by higher rates, the group's profit is tracking at half its 2022 peak, and the anticipated flagship fundraise has been delayed.
Blackstone's most recent financial results revealed another disappointing quarter for the real estate group. Distributable earnings for the group fell 10% from the same quarter a year earlier, assets were down $30 billion from their peak, and its opportunistic strategies lost 3.2% in three months. Blackstone's private equity division has dethroned real estate as the most profitable business in the firm.
The firm tapped David Levine and Giovanni Cutaia to shore up the unit, all under the watchful eye of Gray, who built the business and remains actively involved. The duo has to persuade investors that they can steady the ship, and they need to close new deals before they can raise more money.
"There are big opportunities that could accelerate deployment, but we'll remain very disciplined investors, as we always have," Levine. "If the transaction environment is slower, we're not going to rush."
The new leaders will seek to revitalize a unit that went from Blackstone's fastest growing segment to its slowest.
"We feel incredibly confident in the people we have at the firm, our succession planning, the continuity we have," Gray said last month in a Bloomberg TV interview. Levine and Cutaia "have stepped right in," he added. "They're very capable and our investors have a lot of confidence."
A Star is Born
While every big buyout firm boasts of its real estate investments, it's hard to overstate its importance to Blackstone. In 1992, Gray joined the firm fresh out of college, just as Schwarzman was building the strategy. Gray quickly moved from the private equity division to the fledgling real estate group.
Gray became co-head of the group in 2005, then managing $4 billion. Two years later, he led the $39 billion acquisition of Sam Zell's Equity Office Properties Trust and Blackstone's investment in Hilton. By 2009, Blackstone was the largest landlord in the US.
He also added an Asia-specific strategy to the growing international portfolio and created real estate investment trusts designed to tap the growing retail market. When he rose to president in 2018, Blackstone gave Gray's real estate group credit for half the firm's earnings for several years.
In the post-Gray era, Ken
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: These Trump-backed chip stocks have seen steeper losses than the beleaguered sector
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
These Trump-backed chip stocks have seen steeper losses than the beleaguered sector
2026-11-09
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/these-4-trump-backed-chip-stocks-have-seen-steeper-losses-than-the-beleaguered-sector-193153591.html
Chipmaker Intel (INTC) is putting a notable drag on the burgeoning US government investment portfolio, shaving close to $20 billion off the government's stake in the chipmaker.
But it's not the only one. The Trump administration's other semiconductor investments have also incurred sharp losses that outpace the beleaguered sector.
Chipmaker GlobalFoundries (GFS), photonics company Aeluma (ALMU), and silicon carbide specialist Wolfspeed (WOLF) have all seen losses of at least 40% over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance data.
That's in excess of PHLX Semiconductor (^SOX), a capitalization-weighted index of the semiconductor sector, which is down about over 18% over the same span.
Read more: Intel's stock crash shares an uncanny resemblance to its 2000 bust
The government's portfolio, which spans 41 companies and includes industries from critical minerals to drones, according to a CATO Institute tracker, has taken investors on a wild ride since the Trump administration started buying up stakes last year.
Semiconductor stocks have proved especially volatile, with sharper ups and downs, including a bounceback in evidence Friday. All four were up more than 5% at midday, and some by double digits, as the sector as a whole jumped a more modest 4%.
The price action in these public chipmakers doesn't capture the private companies that have also negotiated equity stakes with the US government.
Trump and his team have placed extra focus on semiconductors, leveraging funds made available by the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act to acquire equity stakes in a host of private chipmakers, including Commonwealth Fusion Systems and xLight.
The Trump administration has also negotiated stakes in quantum computing companies using CHIPS Act money that have similarly struggled amid headwinds facing the tech sector as a whole.
The government portfolio of quantum computing companies includes publicly traded companies like D-Wave Quantum (QBTS), Infleqtion (INFQ), Quantinuum (QNT), and Rigetti Computing (RGTI).
The price oscillations could give ammunition to critics of the administration's investing approach. Economic research shows that full or partial government ownership in companies has historically led to worse outcomes for the companies and their stakeholders.
In a 2025 survey of economists, a large majority said that a government taking equity stakes tends to be detrimental to both a company's performance and its governance standards.
The mixed results of the government's investments at the moment also fly in the face of the outsized returns for taxpayers that Trump and his team often promise.

But it's not the only one. The Trump administration's other semiconductor investments have also incurred sharp losses that outpace the beleaguered sector.

Chipmaker GlobalFoundries (GFS), photonics company Aeluma (ALMU), and silicon carbide specialist Wolfspeed (WOLF) have all seen losses of at least 40% over the past six months, according to Yahoo Finance data.

That's in excess of PHLX Semiconductor (^SOX), a capitalization-weighted index of the semiconductor sector, which is down about over 18% over the same span.

Read more: Intel's stock crash shares an uncanny resemblance to its 2000 bust

The government's portfolio, which spans 41 companies and includes industries from critical minerals to drones, according to a CATO Institute tracker, has taken investors on a wild ride since the Trump administration started buying up stakes last year.

Semiconductor stocks have proved especially volatile, with sharper ups and downs, including a bounceback in evidence Friday. All four were up more than 5% at midday, and some by double digits, as the sector as a whole jumped a more modest 4%.

The price action in these public chipmakers doesn't capture the private companies that have also negotiated equity stakes with the US government.

Trump and his team have placed extra focus on semiconductors, leveraging funds made available by the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act to acquire equity stakes in a host of private chipmakers, including Commonwealth Fusion Systems and xLight.

The Trump administration has also negotiated stakes in quantum computing companies using CHIPS Act money that have similarly struggled amid headwinds facing the tech sector as a whole.

The government portfolio of quantum computing companies includes publicly traded companies like D-Wave Quantum (QBTS), Infleqtion (INFQ), Quantinuum (QNT), and Rigetti Computing (RGTI).

The price oscillations could give ammunition to critics of the administration's investing approach. Economic research shows that full or partial government ownership in companies has historically led to worse outcomes for the companies and their stakeholders.

In a 2025 survey of economists, a large majority said that a government taking equity stakes tends to be detrimental to both a company's performance and its governance standards.

The mixed results of the government's investments at the moment also fly in the face of the outsized returns for taxpayers that Trump and his team often promise.

item.title: Fed’s Daly Says More Rate Increases Likely Needed to Tame Prices
item.author: Catarina Saraiva
item.description:
Fed’s Daly Says More Rate Increases Likely Needed to Tame Prices
2026-11-09
Por Catarina Saraiva
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fed-daly-says-more-rate-182452168.html
(Bloomberg) -- Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said more interest rate increases are likely to be needed to tame inflation, but she said it was too soon to know how much higher rates will need to go.
Most Read from Bloomberg
"My expectation is we're going to have to tighten policy further," Daly said Friday in an interview on CNBC. "Exactly when and how much is still to be decided because we just have to take all the variables that are coming in."
Daly said she supported the decision last week to hold the Fed's benchmark rate steady amid uncertainty about the economy, and that she also backed the decision to raise interest rates in September for the first time since 2023. While two policymakers dissented from the decision to hold rates last month because they preferred to raise them instead, several officials have expressed support for moving them up gradually.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Microsoft Is Winding Down Oracle Deal to Rent AI Cloud Capacity
item.author: Brody Ford
item.description:
Microsoft Is Winding Down Oracle Deal to Rent AI Cloud Capacity
2026-11-09
Por Brody Ford
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/microsoft-winding-down-oracle-deal-173639264.html
(Bloomberg) -- Microsoft Corp. is winding down an arrangement to rent AI computing from Oracle Corp., part of a larger reassessment of billions of dollars in cloud partnerships.
Most Read from Bloomberg
In recent months, Microsoft has been turning off rented computing capacity from Oracle after declining to renew the contract, according to people familiar with the matter.
Over time, the computing Microsoft was renting became less useful because it no longer fit the company's specifications, said the people, who requested anonymity to discuss a private matter. The Oracle hardware used older-generation Nvidia Corp. chips, the people said.
An Oracle spokesperson said demand for the company's AI infrastructure remains strong, including for earlier-generation graphics processing units. Oracle said in September that it was renewing contracts for four-year-old GPUs at a 20% premium to the original deal price.
Microsoft declined to comment.
Under the arrangement, announced in 2023, Oracle agreed to sell Microsoft access to servers that would power a new AI-assisted version of the Bing search engine. The full size of the deal couldn't be determined.
The fact that Microsoft was prepared to rent servers from a major rival was seen as an early indication of the massive shortage of processing power that has come to define the AI era.
The world's largest software maker helped usher in a "neocloud" boom by signing massive contracts with upstart cloud businesses like CoreWeave, Nscale and Nebius. In all, Microsoft committed more than $80 billion to rent capacity from other cloud companies to bolster its own AI efforts.
But Microsoft has been re-thinking its strategy. Key leaders at the company have grown frustrated with the neocloud providers over high costs and delays. In recent months, the company has tightened oversight of data center projects, stepped away from ones it deems risky and debated internally whether to ink new neocloud deals, Bloomberg previously reported.
Oracle's cloud businesses has expanded rapidly since 2023, fueled by big AI contracts with companies like OpenAI and Meta Platforms Inc. For the year that ended in May 2026, Oracle's cloud business posted $18 billion in revenue.

item.title: OpenAI to press ahead with data-center expansion despite midterm sweep, CFO tells CNBC
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
OpenAI to press ahead with data-center expansion despite midterm sweep, CFO tells CNBC
2026-11-09
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/openai-press-ahead-data-center-180438617.html
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI will press ahead with its US data-center expansion plans despite a Democratic midterm sweep this week that has fueled fears of tighter scrutiny of the facilities, its Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar told CNBC in an interview on Friday.
"When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet customer demand," Friar said. "We are going to keep building out those relationships with communities so we can get the compute we need," she added.
One of the corporate faces of the AI boom, OpenAI has moved quickly to counter fears that a shift in congressional power could slow the industry's growth. It launched a charm offensive on Thursday to win over communities as opposition to data centers becomes a rallying point for anxieties about the technology.
As part of the efforts, OpenAI said, it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites. It will also give residents access to construction plans and their potential effects.
Growing data-center opposition was a crucial issue in the midterm elections. Democratic candidates, including Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, made tighter scrutiny of the facilities a central campaign pledge. The Lone Star State is one of the fastest-growing data-center regions in the world.
Fears the Democratic sweep may slow construction of the facilities critical to the AI boom wiped about $2.5 trillion off the US stock market on Thursday, as investors weighed the fallout for the chip, cloud and networking industries that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the spending frenzy.
Still, there are signs that tech giants remain committed to data-center expansion plans despite the growing backlash.
Alphabet-owned Google said on Thursday it would invest $17 billion to build its first data center in Wyoming.
Meanwhile, Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance is considering expanding a data center project in northeastern Brazil, a move that would strengthen its standing as Latin America's leading builder of computing facilities.
OPENAI'S FUNDRAISING PLANS
Friar also told CNBC that OpenAI was raising fresh capital, pushing back against suggestions the ChatGPT maker had scaled back its fundraising ambitions amid the sharp AI stocks selloff.
The company is seeking fresh capital after its business grew 70% quarter over quarter in the third quarter, with enterprise demand doubling over the same period, she said.

item.title: The VIX volatility index just spiked 70%. Here's what history suggests comes next.
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
The VIX volatility index just spiked 70%. Here's what history suggests comes next.
2026-11-09
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/the-vix-volatility-index-just-spiked-70-heres-what-history-suggests-comes-next-125333946.html
If you are looking for something positive after Thursday's shocking stock beatdown, you have come to the right place ahead of the weekend.
History suggests stocks tend to do well after the extreme volatility we saw two days removed from the Election Day blue wave.
The VIX volatility index (^VVIX) — better known as Wall Street's fear gauge — jumped as much as 70% on Thursday. A move this large has only happened eight times since 1991, according to data from CBOE.
Here's what happened to the S&P 500 on average after the eight prior extreme moves:
- 1 month later: +3.0% (7 of 8 times positive)
- 3 months later: +7.1% (6 of 8 times positive)
- 6 months later: +10.4% (8 of 8 times positive)
- 1 year later: +14.7% (7 of 8 times positive)
While somewhat comforting, it doesn't exactly erase from the minds what happened in the markets yesterday, as risk was repriced for a Democratic control of the House and Senate.
Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process. Looked at another way, the total market capitalization of the S&P 500 fell from $68.9 trillion to $65.9 trillion — the largest one-day dollar loss in the index's history.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,830 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).
"We are now seeing something of a buyers' strike in tech," said Truist chief markets strategist Keith Lerner.

- 6 months later: +10.4% (8 of 8 times positive)

- 1 year later: +14.7% (7 of 8 times positive)

While somewhat comforting, it doesn't exactly erase from the minds what happened in the markets yesterday, as risk was repriced for a Democratic control of the House and Senate.

Read more: How to protect your money during turmoil, stock market volatility

The S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4% of its market value, wiping out $3 trillion in the process. Looked at another way, the total market capitalization of the S&P 500 fell from $68.9 trillion to $65.9 trillion — the largest one-day dollar loss in the index's history.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged 1,830 points in its worst single-day rout since 2020. The tech-heavy Nasdaq cratered 5.5%, dragged down by semiconductor and cloud giants such as Micron (MU) and Sandisk (SNDK).

"We are now seeing something of a buyers' strike in tech," said Truist chief markets strategist Keith Lerner.

item.title: Supreme Court to Hear Goldman Sachs’ Bankruptcy Arbitration Bid
item.author: Angélica Serrano-Román
item.description:
Supreme Court to Hear Goldman Sachs’ Bankruptcy Arbitration Bid
2026-11-09
Por Angélica Serrano-Román
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/supreme-court-hear-goldman-sachs-191102310.html
(Bloomberg Law) -- The US Supreme Court agreed to review a request by Goldman Sachs on whether bankruptcy courts can override arbitration agreements, setting up a high-stakes test of the Federal Arbitration Act's reach.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The court on Friday approved the multinational investment bank's request that the high court clarify whether, and under what circumstances, a bankruptcy court can refuse to enforce an arbitration agreement for claims under Section 362(k) of US Bankruptcy Code if a creditor violates the automatic litigation stay protecting bankrupt people and companies.
Goldman Sachs said that because Section 362(k) issues arise frequently in bankruptcy, a circuit split on this issue reflected lower-court confusion about the FAA's intersection with bankruptcy law.
Goldman Sachs lost a bid in the US Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit to compel arbitration in a suit alleging it violated bankruptcy law by continuing debt collection efforts despite the stay. The majority of the three-judge Fourth Circuit panel found that arbitration inherently conflicts with the core purposes of the bankruptcy code. Judge Robert B. King, in a dissent, found that the debtors' claims belong in arbitration.
The FAA creates a national policy favoring arbitration when parties have agreed to it. But bankruptcy law is designed to provide a collective, centralized resolution of a debtor's financial affairs. Courts are generally divided over the use of a test that considers whether issues are "core" or "non-core" and whether arbitration creates an inherent conflict.
The Supreme Court hasn't tested the tension between the two statutory schemes. The debtors in this lawsuit, two holders of Apple Card accounts issued by Goldman Sachs, argued the Supreme Court shouldn't take the case because its specific facts — involving a Chapter 13 stay — make it an unsuitable fit to properly resolve the broader legal question.
The American Bankers Association filed an amicus brief in support of Goldman Sachs.
Latham & Watkins LLP represents Goldman Sachs. Kellett & Bartholow PLLC and Giles & Lambert PC represent the consumer borrowers.
The case is Goldman Sachs Bank USA v. Brown, U.S., No. 25-1408, cert denied/granted 11/6/26.

The majority of the three-judge Fourth Circuit panel found that arbitration inherently conflicts with the core purposes of the bankruptcy code. Judge Robert B. King, in a dissent, found that the debtors' claims belong in arbitration.

The FAA creates a national policy favoring arbitration when parties have agreed to it. But bankruptcy law is designed to provide a collective, centralized resolution of a debtor's financial affairs. Courts are generally divided over the use of a test that considers whether issues are "core" or "non-core" and whether arbitration creates an inherent conflict.

The Supreme Court hasn't tested the tension between the two statutory schemes. The debtors in this lawsuit, two holders of Apple Card accounts issued by Goldman Sachs, argued the Supreme Court shouldn't take the case because its specific facts — involving a Chapter 13 stay — make it an unsuitable fit to properly resolve the broader legal question.

The American Bankers Association filed an amicus brief in support of Goldman Sachs.

Latham & Watkins LLP represents Goldman Sachs. Kellett & Bartholow PLLC and Giles & Lambert PC represent the consumer borrowers.

The case is Goldman Sachs Bank USA v. Brown, U.S., No. 25-1408, cert denied/granted 11/6/26.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang admits to affair after allegations of romance with Chinese spy: Report
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia's Jensen Huang admits to affair after allegations of romance with Chinese spy: Report
2026-11-08
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidias-jensen-huang-admits-to-affair-after-allegations-of-romance-with-chinese-spy-report-205122263.html
Nvidia's (NVDA) board is launching an independent investigation into reports that a woman CEO Jensen Huang was having an affair with was allegedly spying on him for the Chinese government.
In a email to employees Sunday, Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair.
"I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Huang wrote.
"To my colleagues at Nvidia, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading Nvidia is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence," the CEO added.
In a statement Sunday, the board said it "a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation" into the matter.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," the board said statement.
The revelations come after reports of ties between Huang and a woman believed to be passing information to the Chinese government.
Last month, the New York Times reported the US intelligence service believed a Chinese national named Alice Huang, a former leader at Megaspeed, an Nvidia chip customer, and someone with a well-documented relationship with Huang himself, may have acted as an intelligence asset, sharing information with the ruling party in Beijing.
Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director Dan Ives wrote in a note to investors on Sunday that the investigation is a "black eye" for Huang and will likely spark multiple congressional investigations.
"The key question investors will be asking is: Will Jensen remain CEO of Nvidia?….The investigation will be key and we would expect Jensen to continue in his role as CEO with no interruption in the near-term," Ives wrote.
"There is clearly risk that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the Board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally. This will also increase major scrutiny regarding selling chips to China which remains a key battleground issue in DC," he added.
The US government banned the sale of Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China, though the company has lobbied to continue offering the hardware saying it is better if the world uses processors from a US business.

item.title: AI stocks like Nvidia, Micron, and Sandisk have been blown up, but keep this in mind
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AI stocks like Nvidia, Micron, and Sandisk have been blown up, but keep this in mind
2026-11-08
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/ai-stocks-like-nvidia-micron-and-sandisk-have-been-blown-up-but-keep-this-in-mind-110000652.html
I come to you today as a humble servant of the business and investing world with both good and bad news.
First, the sprinkles of good news, because I think we can agree we need something uplifting after watching the market get torched, blown up, and shredded to pieces in the aftermath of the blue wave.
Nothing changes in D.C. overnight, if at all. Companies' fundamentals are what will drive their stock prices in the long term. I don't think the fundamentals of companies have been destroyed this week, at least not to the extent that would warrant some of the sell-offs we witnessed.
A Hut 8 (HUT) data center build-out isn't getting a work order stoppage today that will derail the fourth quarter numbers. Dems aren't carting off AI data center C-suites to jail and sending their companies into bankruptcy.
Texas governor-elect Hinojosa isn't sending construction crews to data centers under an order to tear them all down and turn the land into parks. Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX) — based in Texas — is still operational this weekend, from what I can tell. Musk is still on pace to churn out Tesla (TSLA) robotaxis and robots in large numbers in 2027.
AMD (AMD) didn't offer a huge 2027 outlook this week on its earnings call because it fears a blue wave stopping its CPU momentum in its tracks.
In fact, AMD CEO Lisa Su told me the demand she is seeing is off the charts!
Hilton (HLT) CEO Chris Nassetta is so confident in his business trends that he told me this week he felt compelled to share directional guidance for 2027 with investors. Nassetta normally doesn't share these types of year-ahead specifics.
"Here's the reality. Our political system has been built pretty well," Nassetta said on Sozzi Unleashed. "Our founders did a pretty good job of creating a resilient system. We always figure it out. We'll figure it out this time. The reality is, in the next two or three years, I don't see any real dramatic impact as a result of the last couple days."
Nassetta is going on year 20 as CEO of Hilton, an almost unheard-of run in the C-suite. I don't think you get to log 20 years as Hilton CEO if you are wrong on a lot of stuff — and I think Chris makes a valid point on the political winds that are always blowing.
Now the bad news — and it's short and to the point.
We can no longer believe earnings estimates for 2027 and 2028. While in one breath I'm telling you corporate fundamentals haven't been destroyed this week, in the other breath I acknowledge they have taken a minor hit.
Data center projects won't come to a screeching halt in the US. It will just take a higher bar to get them built. And it will be costlier to get the deals done.

item.title: ¿Qué es la tarjeta flexible, uno de los cambios anunciados en Ecuador?
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
¿Qué es la tarjeta flexible, uno de los cambios anunciados en Ecuador?
2026-11-08
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/economia/tarjeta-flexible-credito-debito-ecuador-banco-central-136659/
¿Qué es la tarjeta flexible, uno de los cambios anunciados en Ecuador?
Las entidades emisoras de tarjetas de crédito y débito en Ecuador podrán entregar a sus clientes un sólo plástico que funcione para ambas modalidades. Además, los plásticos ya no tendrán datos personales, para elevar el nivel de seguridad.
Imagen referencial de una tarjeta.
- Foto
AFP
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
La Junta de Política y Regulación Financiera y Monetaria (JPRFM) emitió una nueva regulación con varios cambios al uso y emisión de tarjetas de débito y crédito en Ecuador. Una de ellas, por ejemplo, es la posibilidad de utilizar tarjetas "flexibles".
Se trata de las tarjetas de plástico o en formato virtual que combinan las funciones de débito y crédito en uno solo. Es decir, el usuario podrá elegir en cada pago si la compra se descuenta de su cuenta de ahorros o se carga a su línea de crédito.
Este es sólo uno de los cambios establecidos por la Junta. La medida incorpora normas de seguridad, determina requisitos para nuevos partícipes dentro del sistema auxiliar de pagos y unifica directrices sobre transparencia, costos y protección al consumidor. Entre los principales están:
- Inclusión de nuevos emisores
- Se autoriza formalmente como emisores de tarjetas a los neobancos, entidades de concesión digital de crédito, Sociedades Especializadas de Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (Sedpe) y a las cooperativas de ahorro y crédito.
- Tarjetas sin datos sensibles
- Las tarjetas físicas se emitirán sin número impreso, sin fecha de vencimiento y sin código CVV visible (salvo que el cliente lo pida expresamente y sin costo). Esto implica, por ejemplo, que si se pierde la tarjeta física, nadie podrá copiar los datos a simple vista para hacer compras en internet.
- Igualdad estricta entre pago en efectivo y con tarjeta
- Todos los comercios estarán obligados a mantener exactamente el mismo precio para pagos al contado y pagos con tarjeta, aplicando también las mismas ofertas, descuentos y promociones.
- Interoperabilidad obligatoria de datáfonos
- Los comercios deben garantizar que sus puntos de cobro (POS, terminales o aplicaciones) procesen tarjetas de cualquier marca y emisor. Además, se prohíben las cláusulas de exclusividad entre adquirentes y comercios
- Autenticación reforzada en compras por internet
- Para prevenir fraudes en compras electrónicas, es obligatorio el uso de Autenticación Multifactor (MFA), tokenización y CVV dinámico al registrar tarjetas en apps o realizar pagos en sitios web.
- Regulación de adquirencia no financiera y agregadores de pago
- Se formaliza el registro de adquirentes no financieros y agregadores de pago (plataformas intermediarias de cobro), exigiéndoles licencias vigentes con las marcas, solvencia con cuentas segregadas y certificación de ciberseguridad. Es decir, se protegen los fondos de los pequeños comercios.
- Protección en renovaciones, recompensas y emisión
- Cualquier cambio en programas de puntos, millas o dinero debe ser notificado al cliente con al menos 30 días de anticipación.
- La vigencia de las tarjetas será de 3 a 10 años.
- Se prohíbe la emisión automática de tarjetas de crédito no solicitadas y los mecanismos para forzar la migración masiva de clientes a nuevos plásticos o productos.
El plazo para adecuar las normativas e implementar la resolución es de seis meses, según lo determinado por la Superintendencia de Bancos, la Superintendencia de Economía Popular y Solidaria y el Banco Central del Ecuador (BCE).

https://www.primicias.ec/economia/tarjeta-flexible-credito-debito-ecuador-banco-central-136659/

¿Qué es la tarjeta flexible, uno de los cambios anunciados en Ecuador?

Las entidades emisoras de tarjetas de crédito y débito en Ecuador podrán entregar a sus clientes un sólo plástico que funcione para ambas modalidades. Además, los plásticos ya no tendrán datos personales, para elevar el nivel de seguridad.

Imagen referencial de una tarjeta.

- Foto

AFP

Autor:

Actualizada:

Compartir:

La Junta de Política y Regulación Financiera y Monetaria (JPRFM) emitió una nueva regulación con varios cambios al uso y emisión de tarjetas de débito y crédito en Ecuador. Una de ellas, por ejemplo, es la posibilidad de utilizar tarjetas "flexibles".

Se trata de las tarjetas de plástico o en formato virtual que combinan las funciones de débito y crédito en uno solo. Es decir, el usuario podrá elegir en cada pago si la compra se descuenta de su cuenta de ahorros o se carga a su línea de crédito.

Este es sólo uno de los cambios establecidos por la Junta. La medida incorpora normas de seguridad, determina requisitos para nuevos partícipes dentro del sistema auxiliar de pagos y unifica directrices sobre transparencia, costos y protección al consumidor. Entre los principales están:

- Inclusión de nuevos emisores

- Se autoriza formalmente como emisores de tarjetas a los neobancos, entidades de concesión digital de crédito, Sociedades Especializadas de Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos (Sedpe) y a las cooperativas de ahorro y crédito.

- Tarjetas sin datos sensibles

- Las tarjetas físicas se emitirán sin número impreso, sin fecha de vencimiento y sin código CVV visible (salvo que el cliente lo pida expresamente y sin costo). Esto implica, por ejemplo, que si se pierde la tarjeta física, nadie podrá copiar los datos a simple vista para hacer compras en internet.

- Igualdad estricta entre pago en efectivo y con tarjeta

- Todos los comercios estarán obligados a mantener exactamente el mismo precio para pagos al contado y pagos con tarjeta, aplicando también las mismas ofertas, descuentos y promociones.

- Interoperabilidad obligatoria de datáfonos

- Los comercios deben garantizar que sus puntos de cobro (POS, terminales o aplicaciones) procesen tarjetas de cualquier marca y emisor. Además, se prohíben las cláusulas de exclusividad entre adquirentes y comercios

- Autenticación reforzada en compras por internet

- Para prevenir fraudes en compras electrónicas, es obligatorio el uso de Autenticación Multifactor (MFA), tokenización y CVV dinámico al registrar tarjetas en apps o realizar pagos en sitios web.

- Regulación de adquirencia no financiera y agregadores de pago

- Se formaliza el registro de adquirentes no financieros y agregadores de pago (plataformas intermediarias de cobro), exigiéndoles licencias vigentes con las marcas, solvencia con cuentas segregadas y certificación de ciberseguridad. Es decir, se protegen los fondos de los pequeños comercios.

- Protección en renovaciones, recompensas y emisión

- Cualquier cambio en programas de puntos, millas o dinero debe ser notificado al cliente con al menos 30 días de anticipación.

- La vigencia de las tarjetas será de 3 a 10 años.

- Se prohíbe la emisión automática de tarjetas de crédito no solicitadas y los mecanismos para forzar la migración masiva de clientes a nuevos plásticos o productos.

El plazo para adecuar las normativas e implementar la resolución es de seis meses, según lo determinado por la Superintendencia de Bancos, la Superintendencia de Economía Popular y Solidaria y el Banco Central del Ecuador (BCE).

item.title: ¿Jacobito a la Yoni?
item.author: Felipe Rodríguez Moreno
item.description:
¿Jacobito a la Yoni?
2026-11-08
Por Felipe Rodríguez Moreno
https://www.primicias.ec/opinion/felipe-rodriguez-moreno/jacobo-bucaram-estrada-extradicion-estados-unidos-136567/
En sus Marcas Listos Fuego
¿Jacobito a la Yoni?
PhD en Derecho Penal; máster en Creación Literaria; máster en Argumentación Jurídica. Abogado litigante, escritor y catedrático universitario.
Actualizada:
Una vez más, explotaron las redes. ¿La razón? La misma de siempre en un país inundado por la criminalidad: célebres personajes de la política nacional son, una vez más, apresados por la Policía. Pero esta vez, los personajes son Jaime Estrada Bonilla -exalcalde de Manta y, otra vez, candidato a esa alcaldía- y su hijo, el ex asambleísta Jaime Estrada Medranda; y en Guayaquil, Jacobo Bucaram Pulley, junto a otros dos gatos.
¿Los cargos? Tráfico de armas y de drogas. ¿La jurisdicción? The Empire.
Las preguntas que quiero responder hoy, para que no se dejen obnubilar con las pendejadas que se leen todos los días en redes, son las siguientes: ¿qué es la extradición? ¿Cabe en este caso? ¿Qué debemos esperar en los próximos días? Vamos a ello.
¿Qué es la extradición?
Es el acto por el cual un Estado entrega a otro a una persona para que sea juzgada o cumpla una pena por delitos que le corresponde juzgar al Estado que la pide. Es cooperación judicial, no un secuestro.
El país que entrega a los sujetos requeridos no decide si el requerido es culpable o inocente. Verifica que la solicitud cumpla la ley y los tratados internacionales. Nada más, pero tampoco nada menos.
Hasta 2024 nuestra Constitución decía que “en ningún caso se concederá la extradición de un ecuatoriano”. La consulta popular de abril de 2024 rompió ese candado, y la reforma rige desde el 9 de mayo de 2024. Las reglas finas están en la nueva Ley Orgánica de Extradición.
Es decir: durante casi un siglo Ecuador fue una guarida perfecta para ecuatorianos que cometían delitos fuera del país, pero además, el lugar perfecto para cometerlos (gracias a la tan aclamada e institucionalizada impunidad).
¿Eso está cambiando? Sí. Duela a quien le duela.
¿Cuándo aplica?
Cuando concurren cuatro requisitos:
1. Base jurídica que incluya el narcotráfico.
2. Doble incriminación: la conducta debe ser delito aquí y allá.
3. Una pena privativa de libertad de al menos un año.
4. Una acción penal vigente.
¿Si se cumplen esos requisitos, se la puede negar? Sí. Solo cuando hay riesgo de pena de muerte, tortura o tratos crueles, inhumanos o degradantes; si el delito es político o conexo; si hay persecución por razones políticas, religiosas, étnicas o de género; o si el juicio sería ante tribunales de excepción.
Para los ecuatorianos hay un candado adicional: no se los puede extraditar por hechos anteriores al 9 de mayo de 2024. Ni un día antes. Es decir, si los personajes detenidos son acusados en EE. UU. de, por ejemplo, haber cometido un delito en el 2023, no cabe la extradición.
¿De qué los acusan exactamente?
Según lo que he podido investigar, la acusación de la Fiscalía Federal del Distrito Sur de Nueva York imputa a los cinco tres cargos: conspiración para importar cocaína a Estados; posesión de ametralladoras en relación con el narcotráfico; y, conspiración para poseer esas armas.
Según la Fiscalía de EE. UU., los Estrada habrían usado su exportadora de productos del mar en Manta para camuflar cocaína entre envíos de atún, en alianza con Los Choneros y Los Lobos y con droga proveniente de grupos armados colombianos.
Además, la Fiscalía sostiene que entre marzo y agosto de 2026 Fernández y Briones, como emisarios de los Estrada, se habrían reunido con Bucaram para negociar el envío de dos toneladas de cocaína a México, con destino final Estados Unidos.
¿Es todo esto real? ¿Existen pruebas? No tengo la menor idea. No soy abogado en Estados Unidos, no soy abogado de los personajes extraditables, y jamás me atrevería a emitir un juicio de valor sin haber accedido al expediente completo.
Todo
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Así era la estrecha relación entre Jaime Estrada Medranda y Luisa González, que se fortaleció en el correísmo
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
Así era la estrecha relación entre Jaime Estrada Medranda y Luisa González, que se fortaleció en el correísmo
2026-11-08
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/relacion-jaime-estrada-medranda-luisa-gonzalez-correismo-manabi-136581/
Así era la estrecha relación entre Jaime Estrada Medranda y Luisa González, que se fortaleció en el correísmo
El empresario Jaime Estrada Medranda pasó de ser un aliado cercano de Revolución Ciudadana, el movimiento correísta, a estar bajo la mira de la DEA por presunto narcotráfico. Con Luisa González, ahora detenida, compartió campañas electorales, actos políticos y actividades personales.
El 12 de abril de 2025, Jaime Estrada Medranda publicó en redes sociales una foto junto a Luisa González, en una visita al Faro de San Lorenzo en Manta.
- Foto
Cortesía
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
La relación de Jaime Estrada Medranda, detenido junto a su padre en Panamá por supuestos vínculos con el narcotráfico, y la excandidata presidencial Luisa González, tiene un antecedente que comenzó en 2022, cuando el líder del movimiento político Revolución Ciudadana, Rafael Correa, expresó su respaldo explícito a Estrada para la Alcaldía de Manta, en Manabí.
Durante esa campaña, Estrada Medranda viajó en reiteradas ocasiones a Bélgica para realizar grabaciones junto a Correa y promocionar su candidatura, compitiendo en alianza entre la RC y el movimiento provincial de su padre, Sí Podemos.
Aunque en los comicios seccionales de 2023 no logró ganar la Alcaldía —en la que fue su primera incursión política tras una trayectoria vinculada al sector empresarial y deportivo—, su vínculo político con el correísmo tiene su historia.
La relación de la familia Estrada con el movimiento data de la época en que su padre, Jaime Estrada Bonilla, mantuvo una alianza con Alianza PAIS (Lista 35) durante el gobierno de Correa. Estrada Bonilla, de larga trayectoria en la política, gobernó Manta entre 2009 y 2014, año en que buscó la reelección mediante la coalición Alianza PAIS - Unidad Primero (Listas 35-65).
A inicios de 2024, la constante cercanía entre Estrada Medranda y Luisa González comenzó a llamar la atención pública. El vínculo entre ambos no solo se reflejó en eventos proselitistas, sino también en actividades deportivas.
A lo largo de 2024, González lo respaldó activamente en su aspiración a una curul en la Asamblea Nacional para las elecciones extraordinarias legislativas de 2025, proceso en el que finalmente resultó electo. De manera recíproca, él impulsó la carrera de González hacia la Presidencia de la República.
El respaldo mutuo incluyó la asistencia conjunta a diversos actos de campaña; incluso el 14 de noviembre de 2024, siendo ambos candidatos, aparecieron en la transmisión oficial previa al partido entre Ecuador y Bolivia, donde fueron entrevistados en vivo.
En la política y el deporte
Pero ese no fue el único registro del apoyo mutuo o de las actividades que compartían. El 7 de febrero de 2025, Estrada publicó un video en compañía de varios allegados practicando 'snorkeling' en una playa de Manta.
Un día después, el 8 de febrero, se difundió otro material audiovisual donde se observa a ambos junto a la frase: "andamos con Jaimito a ver qué deporte nuevo probamos y hoy se nos ocurrió bucear". En las imágenes se ve a González al timón de una embarcación y nadando en las profundidades.
Otro de los momentos destacados ocurrió el 22 de febrero de 2025, durante un acto político en el cantón Jaramijó (Manabí), donde Medranda agradeció públicamente a la población por el respaldo brindado a González.
El nivel de colaboración era tal que, cuando la Intendencia de Policía de Manabí negó en un inicio la autorización para la Convención Nacional del 18 de enero de 2026 en Manta, Estrada acompañó a González a gestionar las acciones legales necesarias para revocar dicha decisión.

Cortesía

Autor:

Actualizada:

Compartir:

La relación de Jaime Estrada Medranda, detenido junto a su padre en Panamá por supuestos vínculos con el narcotráfico, y la excandidata presidencial Luisa González, tiene un antecedente que comenzó en 2022, cuando el líder del movimiento político Revolución Ciudadana, Rafael Correa, expresó su respaldo explícito a Estrada para la Alcaldía de Manta, en Manabí.

Durante esa campaña, Estrada Medranda viajó en reiteradas ocasiones a Bélgica para realizar grabaciones junto a Correa y promocionar su candidatura, compitiendo en alianza entre la RC y el movimiento provincial de su padre, Sí Podemos.

Aunque en los comicios seccionales de 2023 no logró ganar la Alcaldía —en la que fue su primera incursión política tras una trayectoria vinculada al sector empresarial y deportivo—, su vínculo político con el correísmo tiene su historia.

La relación de la familia Estrada con el movimiento data de la época en que su padre, Jaime Estrada Bonilla, mantuvo una alianza con Alianza PAIS (Lista 35) durante el gobierno de Correa. Estrada Bonilla, de larga trayectoria en la política, gobernó Manta entre 2009 y 2014, año en que buscó la reelección mediante la coalición Alianza PAIS - Unidad Primero (Listas 35-65).

A inicios de 2024, la constante cercanía entre Estrada Medranda y Luisa González comenzó a llamar la atención pública. El vínculo entre ambos no solo se reflejó en eventos proselitistas, sino también en actividades deportivas.

A lo largo de 2024, González lo respaldó activamente en su aspiración a una curul en la Asamblea Nacional para las elecciones extraordinarias legislativas de 2025, proceso en el que finalmente resultó electo. De manera recíproca, él impulsó la carrera de González hacia la Presidencia de la República.

El respaldo mutuo incluyó la asistencia conjunta a diversos actos de campaña; incluso el 14 de noviembre de 2024, siendo ambos candidatos, aparecieron en la transmisión oficial previa al partido entre Ecuador y Bolivia, donde fueron entrevistados en vivo.

En la política y el deporte

Pero ese no fue el único registro del apoyo mutuo o de las actividades que compartían. El 7 de febrero de 2025, Estrada publicó un video en compañía de varios allegados practicando 'snorkeling' en una playa de Manta.

Un día después, el 8 de febrero, se difundió otro material audiovisual donde se observa a ambos junto a la frase: "andamos con Jaimito a ver qué deporte nuevo probamos y hoy se nos ocurrió bucear". En las imágenes se ve a González al timón de una embarcación y nadando en las profundidades.

Otro de los momentos destacados ocurrió el 22 de febrero de 2025, durante un acto político en el cantón Jaramijó (Manabí), donde Medranda agradeció públicamente a la población por el respaldo brindado a González.

El nivel de colaboración era tal que, cuando la Intendencia de Policía de Manabí negó en un inicio la autorización para la Convención Nacional del 18 de enero de 2026 en Manta, Estrada acompañó a González a gestionar las acciones legales necesarias para revocar dicha decisión.

item.title: Así Estados Unidos descifró la participación de los Estrada y de Bucaram en la red de Los Choneros y ‘Patucho Celso'
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
Así Estados Unidos descifró la participación de los Estrada y de Bucaram en la red de Los Choneros y ‘Patucho Celso'
2026-11-08
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/estados-unidos-choneros-patucho-celso-jaime-estrada-jacobo-bucaram-caso-136610/
Así Estados Unidos descifró la participación de los Estrada y de Bucaram en la red de Los Choneros y ‘Patucho Celso'
Un expediente penal desclasificado en Nueva York revela cómo la DEA unió las pistas tras Celso Moreira, alias 'Patucho Celso'; la cúpula empresarial y política de los Estrada, y Jacobo Bucaram Pulley. Ahora, forman parte de un caso por narcotráfico y tráfico de armas en Estados Unidos.
Alias 'Patucho Celso', Jaime Estrada Bonilla, Jaime Estrada Medranda y Jacobo Bucaram Pulley comparten una misma acusación de narcotráfico en Estados Unidos.
- Foto
PRIMICIAS
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
La desclasificación de una acusación sustitutiva en el Distrito Sur de Nueva York cambió el enfoque de un caso que inicialmente apuntaba a ‘Patucho Celso’, cabecilla de Los Choneros. Por primera vez, una acusación federal por narcotráfico en Estados Unidos incluyó a figuras empresariales y políticas de Ecuador.
El documento presentado por el fiscal James M. McDonald sumó al proceso penal de Celso Moreira Heredia, alias 'Patucho Celso', al exalcalde de Manta y candidato al mismo cargo, Jaime Estrada Bonilla, a su hijo, el exasambleísta Jaime Estrada Medranda, y a Jacobo Bucaram Pulley, hijo del expresidente Abdalá Bucaram Ortiz.
Las detenciones ejecutadas entre el 2 y el 4 de noviembre de 2026 en Panamá y Guayaquil expusieron la trama. La operación regional fue coordinada por la Policía Nacional del Ecuador, la Policía de Panamá, la DEA e Interpol con notificaciones rojas reservadas.
Las autoridades estadounidenses sostienen que la red tuvo un rol clave en el tráfico del 70% de la cocaína hacia su territorio. El director de la DEA, Terrance Cole, afirmó que ningún poder político pone a los acusados por fuera del alcance de la justicia.
Los nexos de ‘Patucho Celso’ con Manabí y Los Choneros
Celso Miguel Moreira Heredia, alias 'Patucho Celso', fue identificado por inteligencia policial y autoridades como cabecilla de Los Choneros y sucesor de alias 'Fito', quien fue el primer narco ecuatoriano extraditado directamente a Estados Unidos. Todos parte de la cúpula chonera.
Su primer arresto registrado ocurrió en 2009 en Manta con 24,8 kg de cocaína en un pesquero. Justamente la ciudad identificada por la Fiscalía de Estados Unidos como el centro de operaciones de los Estrada.
El 7 de octubre de 2010 fue absuelto por el Sexto Tribunal Penal de Manta, integrado por Marcos Zambrano, George Moreira y Carlos Flores. En octubre de 2014 volvió a ingresar a prisión por el Caso Pacífico, nuevamente por narcotráfico en Manabí. Pero recuperó su libertad en mayo de 2015.
Las acusaciones de Estados Unidos señalan que fue a partir de esos años cuando esta red empezó a tomar fuerza en el narcotráfico.
En 2018, Moreira resultó aprehendido en Portoviejo como el más buscado de Manabí. Pese a ello, recibió una pena de 18 meses por asociación ilícita, firmada por el juez José Tamayo Arana, el mismo magistrado que excarceló a alias 'Rasquiña', cabecilla histórico de Los Choneros asesinado en 2020.
A partir de ahí, ‘Patucho Celso’ tuvo un perfil bajo, lo que le significó el membrete estatal de ‘narco invisible’, actuando tras las sombras como un financista de Los Choneros, pero teniendo un alto nivel de influencia junto a delincuentes de mayor perfil como ‘Fito’ y ‘Rasquiña’.
Su regreso a la palestra pública ocurrió el 10 de mayo de 2024, cuando se ejecutó el allanamiento a la finca San Andrés, en el km 36 de la Vía a la Costa en Guayaquil. La intervención policial interrumpió la celebración de su cumpleaños 41, un ostentoso festejo estimado en USD 500.000.
En el evento catalogado como ‘narcofiesta’ participaron 203 invitados exclusivos y artistas internacionales. Moreira
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Stocks had their worst day in 18 months — here’s why your portfolio probably held up
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Stocks had their worst day in 18 months — here’s why your portfolio probably held up
2026-11-07
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/stocks-had-their-worst-day-in-18-months--heres-what-that-means-for-your-portfolio-164024037.html
The AI trade ran off a cliff Thursday. Most of the stock market was nowhere near the edge.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) fell more than 4% Thursday, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash. About $3 trillion in stock market value disappeared in a single session.
Chipmakers took the hardest hit. The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) dropped 12%, its worst day since March 2020, and Nvidia (NVDA) fell 9%, its worst day since the DeepSeek scare in January 2025.
The trigger was Washington. Democrats won control of Congress this week, and candidates in both parties campaigned against AI data centers, the giant buildings those chips go into. Investors worry that new rules could slow the building boom that sent chip stocks to records.
But look past the AI stocks, and the picture gets a lot calmer.
The S&P 500 is only about 5% below its October record and is still up about 8% this year. The typical stock in the index is about 3% off its high, and more than half of S&P 500 stocks are up for the week.
How can both be true? The S&P 500 gives the biggest companies the biggest say. Chipmakers alone make up about 14% of the index, by Yahoo Finance's count, so when they crash, they drag the whole index down even when most other companies are holding steady.
For an average portfolio, the damage so far is modest. For every $1,000 in an S&P 500 index fund at the market's Oct. 6 peak, you'd have about $950 left, and the index is still up about 8% this year. Savers in target-date funds, which mix stocks with bonds, fared even better Thursday. Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund (VTTHX) lost less than 3%, compared with more than 4% for the S&P 500.
Stocks are bouncing Friday, with chip stocks leading the way, after a strong jobs report showed employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the roughly 70,000 economists expected.
The AI risk hiding in your index fund
One good day doesn't mean the danger has passed.
The same setup that cushioned investors this week cuts both ways. AI-linked companies are a big piece of the S&P 500, and they've powered much of the market's gains in recent years. If the AI slide deepens, index funds like those based on the S&P 500 will feel it a lot more.
Rich Bernstein, global head of macro and customized investing at Janus Henderson Investors, compared the AI run to Wile E. Coyote, the cartoon character forever chasing the Road Runner off cliffs.
"You're running full speed, and then you realize that there's nothing anymore, and you fall to the bottom of the canyon," Bernstein said on Yahoo Finance's "Market Domination" on Thursday. "That's momentum investing."
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com.

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/stocks-had-their-worst-day-in-18-months--heres-what-that-means-for-your-portfolio-164024037.html
The AI trade ran off a cliff Thursday. Most of the stock market was nowhere near the edge.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) fell more than 4% Thursday, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash. About $3 trillion in stock market value disappeared in a single session.
Chipmakers took the hardest hit. The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) dropped 12%, its worst day since March 2020, and Nvidia (NVDA) fell 9%, its worst day since the DeepSeek scare in January 2025.
The trigger was Washington. Democrats won control of Congress this week, and candidates in both parties campaigned against AI data centers, the giant buildings those chips go into. Investors worry that new rules could slow the building boom that sent chip stocks to records.
But look past the AI stocks, and the picture gets a lot calmer.
The S&P 500 is only about 5% below its October record and is still up about 8% this year. The typical stock in the index is about 3% off its high, and more than half of S&P 500 stocks are up for the week.
How can both be true? The S&P 500 gives the biggest companies the biggest say. Chipmakers alone make up about 14% of the index, by Yahoo Finance's count, so when they crash, they drag the whole index down even when most other companies are holding steady.
For an average portfolio, the damage so far is modest. For every $1,000 in an S&P 500 index fund at the market's Oct. 6 peak, you'd have about $950 left, and the index is still up about 8% this year. Savers in target-date funds, which mix stocks with bonds, fared even better Thursday. Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund (VTTHX) lost less than 3%, compared with more than 4% for the S&P 500.
Stocks are bouncing Friday, with chip stocks leading the way, after a strong jobs report showed employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the roughly 70,000 economists expected.
The AI risk hiding in your index fund
One good day doesn't mean the danger has passed.
The same setup that cushioned investors this week cuts both ways. AI-linked companies are a big piece of the S&P 500, and they've powered much of the market's gains in recent years. If the AI slide deepens, index funds like those based on the S&P 500 will feel it a lot more.
Rich Bernstein, global head of macro and customized investing at Janus Henderson Investors, compared the AI run to Wile E. Coyote, the cartoon character forever chasing the Road Runner off cliffs.
"You're running full speed, and then you realize that there's nothing anymore, and you fall to the bottom of the canyon," Bernstein said on Yahoo Finance's "Market Domination" on Thursday. "That's momentum investing."
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com.

item.title: Hassett Says No Economic Policy Shift Even After Election Rout
item.author: Michael Sasso
item.description:
Hassett Says No Economic Policy Shift Even After Election Rout
2026-11-07
Por Michael Sasso
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/hassett-says-no-economic-policy-153704724.html
(Bloomberg) -- President Donald Trump's chief economic adviser said the administration won't be revamping its economic policies in the wake of Republicans' sweeping defeat in the midterm congressional elections.
Most Read from Bloomberg
"I don't think we have a policy change we need to plan," Kevin Hassett, director of the White House National Economic Council, said in an interview on Bloomberg TV Friday. "The policies are working."
Hassett argued the Democratic victory in the elections wasn't a rebuttal of the president's supply-side policies, and reiterated Trump's threat to use vetoes to keep his agenda in place. Among other benefits, those measures have led to 120,000 people involved in building new factories, Hassett said, following an October employment report showing the nation added 165,000 jobs last month.
Trump "is concerned that the positive momentum that we've built could be upended by Democrats now that they've taken more power," Hassett said. "But I think they're going to have a really hard time repealing all the great policies which created the strong job market, because the president will veto it."
Hassett attributed recent stickiness in inflation to the Iran war and its effects on gasoline prices, rather than the administration's economic policies, which he suggested are having a downward effect on inflation. He contrasted that with what he called the inflationary impact of former President Joe Biden's agenda, "where they basically helicopter-dropped money down to people after the Covid crisis was over."
Joking that he had gotten a "veto hat" from the president, Hassett said the administration also has a "huge amount" of executive authority to keep pressing ahead with its program, including taking on over-regulation.
--With assistance from Dani Burger and Michael McKee.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Goldman’s US Stock Panic Gauge Hits Extreme, Signaling Rebound
item.author: Natalia Kniazhevich
item.description:
Goldman’s US Stock Panic Gauge Hits Extreme, Signaling Rebound
2026-11-07
Por Natalia Kniazhevich
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-us-stock-panic-gauge-152807575.html
(Bloomberg) -- Goldman Sachs Group Inc. traders said the violent selloff in US equities has pushed market panic to an extreme level that historically signals a strong rebound over the medium term.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The bank's Vol Panic Index surged to 9.57 out of 10 on Thursday, crossing the 9.5 threshold that marks the panic zone. The roughly five-point increase was the third-largest daily jump on record. Coming on the heels of a huge decline Wednesday, the fourth largest, it resulted in the biggest ever two-day swing, traders including Lee Coppersmith wrote.
"The combined two-day swing was the largest on record, which I think shows how quickly the market went from relief to outright panic," Coppersmith said.
The sharp reversal followed an aggressive wave of demand for downside protection ahead of Wednesday's US midterm vote. Clients had sold hedges into the post-election relief rally, leaving portfolios materially under-protected when equities turned lower. As stocks tumbled and forced liquidations spread across hedge funds, investors scrambled to buy back the protection they had just shed, according to the traders.
The rush for hedges was reflected in options activity. More than 11 million puts traded on Cboe on Thursday, the highest daily volume on record, surpassing the previous peak in April 2025. Index puts accounted for much of the activity, while single-stock put volume ranked fourth-highest ever, highlighting the concentration of demand in broad-market protection.
Still, Goldman's historical analysis suggests the medium-term outlook becomes more constructive when panic reaches such extremes. Following the 15 previous signals in which its Vol Panic Index exceeded 9.5, the S&P 500 gained an average 4.6% over the subsequent three months, with an 80% hit rate. Over six months, the average gain was 9%, with stocks rising in 73% of cases.
"Yesterday was as much about an exceptionally poor technical setup and forced re-hedging as it was about a deterioration in fundamentals," Coppersmith wrote.
While there is still more positioning to work through as markets continue to search for a bottom, the historical pattern suggests that extreme volatility and forced selling can eventually create opportunities for investors willing to look beyond the near-term turbulence, according to Goldman's traders.

item.title: Q-Day may arrive by 2030. AI’s power problem isn’t going anywhere
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
Q-Day may arrive by 2030. AI’s power problem isn’t going anywhere
2026-11-07
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/ai-powered-hacking-risk-is-getting-worse--and-thats-before-q-day-110000397.html
The Binance hack was a harsh reminder: Nothing online is truly safe.
After the largest cryptocurrency theft on record — initiated through classic phishing but executed through AI tools — corporate America and security analysts are warning of the fresh dangers posed by sophisticated AI technology, which can find and exploit software flaws much faster than people can.
The risks, it seems, are on the rise for everyone.
"This is every crypto platform, every wallet service, every bank, every financial institution that you use," Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said in an interview with Yahoo Finance. "Especially now with AI improving so quickly, I think we're going to see a lot more of this."
While the hack underscored the weaknesses of centralized financial intermediaries, rather than the underlying blockchain technology, "its effects could spread to other market participants," Moody's analysts wrote in a note this week.
Circle's (CRCL) Jeremy Allaire told us this week that the acceleration of agentic AI means risk is accelerating dramatically in tandem.
"Any critical infrastructure, any major industry, hospital systems, energy systems, utilities, financial industry participants — everyone has risk here," he said. "I think the threat vectors are some of the most intense vectors we have ever seen in the history of the world. I think we are in a hot environment right now, and everyone needs to be operating from the assumption that they are under attack."
It's truly wild to think that bank robberies, a phenomenon that seems almost archaic, are a risk that has somehow boomeranged back.
And just like AI's turbocharged hacking worries, a new tech specter sits on the horizon, without a kill switch: "Q-day."
Quantum computing presents an enticing idea: the ability to tackle calculations that would be impractical for legacy computers, while using far less energy.
As early as 2030, computer scientists project that quantum computers can break the traditional encryption that safeguards pillars of the economy, such as the financial system and global communications, a moment the industry calls "Q-day."
It's something we've been seeing in Wall Street analyst research that's mostly been absent from broader headlines, because it's more long-term. But in September, Bank of America's thematic research team noted that a key security algorithm could be broken with far fewer quantum bits (qubits) than previously thought. In just 10 months, researchers saw progress to the tune of a 99% (not a typo) decrease.

item.title: Market Impacts of Midterm Results
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Market Impacts of Midterm Results
2026-11-07
Por Texto propio
Market Impacts of Midterm Results
Key Takeaways
Democratic victories in state elections, particularly in Texas, could lead to tighter data center restrictions and project delays, although the broader AI investment cycle is expected to stay the same.
Change in control of Congress could delay or soften planned Medicaid and SNAP spending reductions, potentially supporting consumer spending and economic growth.
Morgan Stanley Research maintains its overweight position in global equities, supported by expectations for resilient growth, corporate earnings and continued AI investment.
The presidential administration’s trade and geopolitical policies are likely to continue, while potential changes to healthcare policy and AI regulation could influence sector performance.
Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, while also winning gubernatorial races in traditionally Republican states. The results raise questions about potential policy changes and their implications for economic growth, financial markets and asset classes.
For investors, one of the most significant developments is the prospect of tighter restrictions on data center development, which could weigh on sentiment toward artificial intelligence (AI) investment. At the same time, Democratic control of Congress could benefit the healthcare sector and consumer spending with opportunities to revisit planned reductions in federal healthcare and food assistance spending.
We think there are three key policy developments to watch over the short term and as potential foundational themes for the 2028 election, along with their potential implications for markets.
1. Fiscal Policy: Potential Changes to Medicaid and SNAP Cuts
The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) includes approximately $900 billion in Medicaid spending reductions and $200 billion in cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) over the next decade.
With Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress, some of these reductions could be delayed, softened or reversed as part of negotiations around upcoming fiscal deadlines.
The size of the Democratic majority could also help lawmakers overcome disagreements within their party and unite around a limited set of policy priorities.
Despite the potential changes, we think federal fiscal deficits will remain around 6% of GDP, even if the spending cuts remain in place.
2. Executive-Led Policy: Uncertainty Likely to Persist
Much of the policy uncertainty that has marked President Donald Trump's second term has stemmed from executive actions rather than legislation.
Democratic control of Congress is unlikely to materially change the administration's approach to geopolitics, export controls, deregulation and trade, including the upcoming review of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).
As a result, investors should expect continued policy uncertainty, particularly in areas where the administration retains substantial executive authority.
3. AI Infrastructure: Greater Risk of Data Center Restrictions
The election results could introduce additional challenges for AI infrastructure investment, especially as newly elected state officials consider restrictions on data center development.
Decisions governing data center projects—including grid interconnection, electricity rate structures for large users, site selection and tax abatements—are largely determined by state utility commissions, legislatures and county boards.
Additional state-level regulations could create a more fragmented environment, with some jurisdictions remaining receptive to new data centers while others impose tighter restrictions.
The Texas gubernatorial election is particularly significant for the industry. Democrat Gina Hinojosa's victory increases the likelihood of substantial project delays, given that her campaign platform included a moratorium on new dat
