item.title: A New Investment Case for Europe
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
A New Investment Case for Europe
2026-11-07
Por Texto propio
A New Investment Case for Europe
Key Takeaways
European governments are placing greater emphasis on economic security, strategic autonomy and industrial resilience, redirecting capital toward strategically important industries.
Defense, energy, digital infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and critical technologies could benefit from increased spending after years of underinvestment.
Investors should look across borders as rearmament, electrification, automation and AI infrastructure span multiple European markets and may be better approached as continental themes than individual country allocations.
Europe’s capital cycle creates potential opportunities across sovereign and corporate credit, infrastructure and private markets, making the investment case inherently multi-asset.
Europe is undergoing its most significant economic policy shift since the creation of the euro. After decades in which fiscal restraint, globalization and market efficiency shaped policy, governments across the region are increasingly focused on economic security, strategic autonomy and industrial resilience.
The shift is redirecting capital toward defense, energy, digital infrastructure, advanced manufacturing and critical technologies—areas that received systematic underinvestment for much of the post-Cold War era.
Europe still faces longstanding challenges, including weak productivity, unfavorable demographics, expensive energy and institutional fragmentation. But for investors with a long-term horizon, the change in policy direction and an emerging multiyear capital expenditure cycle may create an opportunity set with a different return profile from that of the past decade.
A Cross-Region Transformation
Across Europe, countries are adapting to a changing geopolitical and economic environment. Conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have exposed insufficient investment in energy, the region’s structural dependence on Russian gas and the need for greater defense spending.
China’s evolution from customer to competitor has added pressure on Europe to upgrade its manufacturing base and accelerate technological innovation. Industrialization is increasingly shifting toward Eastern Europe, which offers competitive energy costs, skilled engineering labor, available factory capacity and geographic proximity to the defense supply chains that NATO is urgently rebuilding.
Meanwhile, the countries at the center of the eurozone debt crisis in the 2010s, including Portugal, Ireland, Italy, Greece and Spain, spent much of the past decade reducing private debt, rebuilding external balances and recapitalizing banks. As a result, they entered the current expansion with greater fiscal and financial flexibility than some of their core European counterparts.
The geopolitical shocks of the past four years have created a coalition broad enough to act, contributing to a looser fiscal framework and greater willingness to direct investment toward strategic priorities.
A Regime Change, Not a Renaissance
Europe is mobilizing and changing its trajectory, but it hasn’t resolved some of its structural problems. This distinction is critical to the region’s investment case.
The European Union has not produced a global-scale platform company in a generation, while venture funding remains at a fraction of U.S. levels. Fragmented capital markets also constrain the ability to fund companies at scale.
Demographics present another challenge. A shrinking working-age population, rising pension costs and a hardening political consensus against non-EU migration are contributing to labor supply constraints that industrial policy cannot directly address.
What has changed is the political environment. The geopolitical shocks of the past four years have created a coalition broad enough to act, contributing to a looser fiscal framework and greater willingness to direct investment toward strategic priorities.
From G

item.title: Cloudflare shares leap after blowout Q3 results, strong forecast
item.author: Luke Juricic
item.description:
Cloudflare shares leap after blowout Q3 results, strong forecast
2026-11-06
Por Luke Juricic
https://finance.yahoo.com/news/cloudflare-shares-soar-hours-blowout-215805051.html
Investing.com -- Cloudflare Inc (NYSE:NET) shares surged more than 14% in premarket trading Friday after the connectivity and cloud security provider delivered third-quarter results that surpassed Wall Street expectations across all primary metrics and issued an aggressive full-year outlook.
The robust performance was underpinned by accelerating enterprise adoption and surging demand for the company's developer platform amid broader artificial intelligence workloads.
Revenue for the quarter ended September 30 climbed 39% year-over-year to $782.5 million, topping the consensus estimate of $736.8 million and marking the company's fastest pace of top-line expansion in nearly four years. On an adjusted basis, net income reached $0.38 per diluted share, beating analyst projections of $0.34 and improving from $0.27 per share in the prior-year period.
Operational indicators underscored broad-based commercial momentum, highlighted by a 37% year-over-year increase in current remaining performance obligations (cRPO). Adjusted operating income expanded to $137.1 million, or 17.5% of total revenue, up from $85.9 million, or 15.3% of revenue, a year earlier.
On a GAAP basis, operating loss widened to $67.9 million from $37.5 million in the third quarter of 2025, driven in part by $174.1 million in stock-based compensation and $11.0 million in restructuring charges. GAAP net loss totaled $34.1 million, or $0.10 per share, compared to a net loss of $1.3 million in the prior-year period.
Cash generation remained steady despite heightened infrastructure investments, with operating cash flow rising to $215.4 million from $167.1 million a year ago. Free cash flow came in at $82.1 million, representing a 10% margin, while total cash, cash equivalents, and available-for-sale securities stood at $5.13 billion at quarter-end.
Management highlighted structural tailwinds tied to security and AI infrastructure as primary growth catalysts. "We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue with revenue of $782 million, up 39% year over year," co-founder and chief executive Matthew Prince said in the release, adding that the company has "built the development platform for the AI-powered Internet."

item.title: Apple, Microsoft hit all-time highs as Nasdaq surges 2% in post-election rally: AlphaCheck
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Apple, Microsoft hit all-time highs as Nasdaq surges 2% in post-election rally: AlphaCheck
2026-11-06
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/apple-microsoft-hit-all-time-highs-as-nasdaq-surges-2-in-post-election-rally-alphacheck-152548814.html
Good morning. Stocks surged on Wednesday, with most sectors green across the board after a Democratic mid-term election sweep. Tech (XLK) bounced as Apple (AAPL) shares hit all-time highs, sending the iPhone maker's market cap above $5 trillion. Microsoft (MSFT) also surged 6% to hit a new record. The Nasdaq (^IXIC) Composite rallied more than 2%, while the Dow (^DJI) surged about 1,100 points, or about 2%.
Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) initially fell over worries of regulatory hurdles in the AI data center build-out as Democrats took control of the House and Senate. However, those stocks trimmed losses as the overall markets surged higher.
Oil prices extended their decline amid growing hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the war in the Middle East. Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) tumbled more than 2% to around $100 per barrel, while WTI (CL=F) also dropped, hovering above $93 per barrel.
Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Here are some other notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: CVS Health (CVS), McDonald's (MCD), and Uber (UBER).

item.title: Friday’s jobs report is expected to show the labor market chugging along
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Friday’s jobs report is expected to show the labor market chugging along
2026-11-06
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/a-blowout-us-added-165000-jobs-in-october-trouncing-expectations-135651705.html
The US added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past economists' expectations, as the labor market showed strength despite the Federal Reserve's recent rate hikes.
The unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1% even amid a slight increase in labor force participation. September's underwhelming jobs report of 29,000 additions was also revised upward to a gain of 60,000 jobs.
Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, deemed the results "a blowout" in a post on X.
Economists surveyed by Bloomberg projected a gain of about 70,000 jobs in October and saw the unemployment rate holding steady.
Wage growth increased 0.4% from September, better than expectations for 0.3% month-over-month growth. Annual earnings rose 3.1%, beating expectations but likely still below the current inflation rate.
Employers added jobs in a number of sectors of the economy. Professional and business services, which had been seen as more vulnerable to AI-related disruptions, added 70,000 roles. Healthcare, long a strong spot for job growth, added a higher-than-average 42,000 positions.
Transportation and warehousing jobs rose by 25,000, and manufacturing continued to show strength with 19,000 additions.
"This is still a low-hire, low-fire market overall, but we could be seeing some green shoots on the hiring side," Jake Krimmel, senior economist at Realtor.com, said in a statement.
Other job market measures released earlier this week telegraphed steady hiring — though not to the extent of Friday's report blowout number. Job openings and hiring edged higher, the Labor Department's monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey showed; private employers added 86,000 jobs, according to ADP; and layoff plans dropped to a three-year low while seasonal hiring ramped up.
"Consistent with prior, more partial indicators of the US labor market, the October Jobs Report came in very strong, across the board," Wharton economist Mohamed El-Erian posted on X.
The solid report will likely give the Federal Reserve more confidence to move forward with another rate hike in December. The central bank will also consider November jobs data and October's inflation figures before its Dec. 9 rate decision. Traders currently see a 77% chance of a 25 basis point rate hike next month, up from 67% on Thursday, according to CME FedWatch.
"Today's jobs report is a strong rebuttal to fears that the economy is heading into a meaningful slowdown," Seema Shah, chief global strategist at Principal Asset Management, said in a statement. "With wage growth also picking up, a December Fed hike remains firmly on the table despite the recent tightening in financial conditions."
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Why SoftBank stock is sinking under the weight of its AI bets
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why SoftBank stock is sinking under the weight of its AI bets
2026-11-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-softbank-stock-is-sinking-under-the-weight-of-its-ai-bets-134912183.html
The over-the-top tech house Masayoshi Son has spent billions to build at SoftBank (SFTBY) is getting torched, looking at the stock price action.
SoftBank shares crashed 10.83% in early trading on Friday after losing 14.4% on Thursday as the AI-heavy company was swept into the broader AI stock rout. Sentiment was also dinged by an FT report that China would not allow SoftBank to go ahead with the $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics division.
Shares are down 45% in the past month.
The company's credit risk climbed to its highest level in four years today, as measured by its five-year credit default swap (CDS) spread. The spread widened to as much as 466 basis points, its highest since Oct. 22, Reuters reported.
The level indicated a default probability of 30.6%.
SoftBank's primary asset anchor remains its roughly 90% ownership stake in Arm Holdings (ARM), whose chip architectures power the vast majority of mobile and enterprise AI workloads. With concerns about a "blue wave" on Election Day stunting AI demand, a company like Arm is caught in the crosshairs — and by extension so is SoftBank.
Meanwhile, the company also has a $64.6 billion stake in OpenAI, which had decided to push its IPO out to 2027. But OpenAI's valuation is at risk in light of the blue wave, as seen in chatter that the upcoming Anthropic IPO won't deliver it a $2 trillion valuation as many expected.
item.content:encoded:
Why SoftBank stock is sinking under the weight of its AI bets

2026-11-06

Por Brian Sozzi

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-softbank-stock-is-sinking-under-the-weight-of-its-ai-bets-134912183.html

The over-the-top tech house Masayoshi Son has spent billions to build at SoftBank (SFTBY) is getting torched, looking at the stock price action.

SoftBank shares crashed 10.83% in early trading on Friday after losing 14.4% on Thursday as the AI-heavy company was swept into the broader AI stock rout. Sentiment was also dinged by an FT report that China would not allow SoftBank to go ahead with the $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics division.

Shares are down 45% in the past month.

The company's credit risk climbed to its highest level in four years today, as measured by its five-year credit default swap (CDS) spread. The spread widened to as much as 466 basis points, its highest since Oct. 22, Reuters reported.

The level indicated a default probability of 30.6%.

SoftBank's primary asset anchor remains its roughly 90% ownership stake in Arm Holdings (ARM), whose chip architectures power the vast majority of mobile and enterprise AI workloads. With concerns about a "blue wave" on Election Day stunting AI demand, a company like Arm is caught in the crosshairs — and by extension so is SoftBank.

Meanwhile, the company also has a $64.6 billion stake in OpenAI, which had decided to push its IPO out to 2027. But OpenAI's valuation is at risk in light of the blue wave, as seen in chatter that the upcoming Anthropic IPO won't deliver it a $2 trillion valuation as many expected.

item.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su sees AI becoming 'essential to every aspect of our lives'
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AMD CEO Lisa Su sees AI becoming 'essential to every aspect of our lives'
2026-11-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/amd-ceo-lisa-su-sees-ai-becoming-essential-to-every-aspect-of-our-lives-172825495.html
AMD (AMD) CEO Lisa Su appreciates the market's increasing jitters about the health and sustainability of AI demand.
She doesn't see any signs of caution in her red-hot chips business, which is helping power the AI boom.
"I think the market can sometimes be a little bit short-sighted. It is what it is," AMD CEO Lisa Su said on Sozzi Unleashed.
"What I look at is in the long term, if you believe, which I do, I believe very deeply that computing, in many ways, equates to intelligence," Su added. "So the more compute you have, the more intelligent your company is, the more problems you're going to be able to solve, the more you're going to accelerate your business. If you believe that foundation, then investing ahead of the curve is the right thing to do because we're always investing for the long term — long term being three to five years and beyond. And that means you have to make the investments now. So I think from our standpoint, I've always operated that way. We're always looking at what do we see over the horizon? And over the horizon, I see AI and super intelligence becoming more and more essential to every aspect of our lives and every aspect of our business. So I believe in this demand, and I very much believe that many of the investments that are being made throughout the ecosystem are also seeing some of these same trends."
AMD delivered a strong double beat in its third quarter earnings report on Tuesday evening.
Third quarter sales jumped 45% year over year to a record $13.38 billion, comfortably surpassing Wall Street consensus estimates of roughly $13.06 billion.
Adjusted earnings climbed 74% to $2.09 per share, easily topping analyst projections of $1.94 per share.
The blowout performance was anchored by AMD's Data Center segment, where revenue surged 97% to a record $8.5 billion on robust demand for EPYC server processors and the production ramp of Instinct MI450 AI accelerators.
For the fourth quarter, AMD said it sees 50% sequential growth in data centers. In 2027, Su guided to revenue growing more than 80%, with server revenue doubling and data center AI more than doubling.
AMD stock finished Wednesday's session up 1% but fell 17% on Thursday. The stock has gained a sizzling 88% year to date.
"With AI business reaching escape velocity, investor focus shifts from proving AI competitiveness to executing a multiyear ramp centered on MI450/MI455, Helios, and Venice with significant operating leverage as the business scales," Citi analyst Atif Malik said.
Malik gave AMD a top pick call.

item.title: Amazon partners with Uber Eats to bring restaurant delivery to Prime members
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Amazon partners with Uber Eats to bring restaurant delivery to Prime members
2026-11-06
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/amazon-partners-with-uber-eats-to-bring-restaurant-delivery-to-prime-members-110100295.html
Amazon (AMZN) is teaming up with Uber Eats (UBER), allowing Prime members to order from restaurants through Amazon.com and the Amazon app, as third-party delivery gets more competitive.
Prime members who order via Amazon will get free delivery on orders of $25 or more. Customers will also get $20 off their first two Uber Eats orders of $25 or more through the first 14 days.
"This is what Prime is all about: unlimited free, fast delivery on a wide selection of products, big savings, fantastic entertainment, and now even more value on restaurant delivery with Uber Eats, all in a single membership," Jamil Ghani, worldwide vice president of Amazon Prime, said in a statement.
Uber also offers its Uber One service, which includes no delivery fees on food and groceries, as well as other benefits, for $9.99 a month, or $96 per year. Amazon Prime, which includes access to Prime Video and Amazon Music, as well as free shipping options, costs $140 a year.
Amazon has been taking share in the grocery delivery market, especially on same-day and one-hour deliveries. Earlier this week, Amazon announced that it added more than 6,000 items to its grocery options over the last six months.
But the company faces stiff competition from Walmart (WMT), which has created a bundle for Walmart+ and its wholesale retailer, Sam's Club Plus, for $120 a year, plus tax.
Amazon's partnership with Uber Eats also came after DoorDash (DASH) announced plans to acquire hyperlocal grocery-delivery provider Instacart (CART) in a $17 billion deal to compete in the online grocery market.

item.title: Record share of first-time homebuyers paying in cash as Great Wealth Transfer picks up steam
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Record share of first-time homebuyers paying in cash as Great Wealth Transfer picks up steam
2026-11-06
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/record-share-of-first-time-homebuyers-paying-in-cash-as-great-wealth-transfer-picks-up-steam-155110254.html
The Great Wealth Transfer is starting to impact the housing market.
A record share of first-time homebuyers are paying for their properties in cash, a sign that more buyers are likely using money they inherited from older generations to help fund their purchases.
Last year, 1 in 10 first-time buyers did an all-cash transaction, according to a new report from the National Association of Realtors, the fourth straight year with an increase, and the largest share since the trade group began collecting data on those transactions in 2003. Among first-time all-cash buyers, 28% reported using an inheritance to help fund their deal, compared with just 9% of first-time buyers who financed.
As home prices hover near all-time highs and mortgage rates stay north of 7%, pricing out many prospective buyers, some portion of those buyers may simply be waiting for an inheritance or other significant help from wealthy baby boomers or members of the Silent Generation.
"It is critical when analyzing first-time buyers to understand there is a growing divide among those who are saving independently and priced out of homeownership, versus those who are waiting on the sidelines but then given a generational transfer of wealth," the report said.
Buyers reliant on wealth transfers look different from those who finance and use their own savings. As modern life expectancy increases, delaying inheritances, first-time all-cash buyers are typically deep into middle age. The median first-time buyer paying all cash is 54 years old, according to the report, significantly older than the median age of 38 for first-time buyers financing their homes.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher following worst sell-off since 2020
item.author: Ines Ferré
item.description:
Nvidia, AMD, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher following worst sell-off since 2020
2026-11-06
Por Ines Ferré
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/nvidia-amd-micron-sandsik-lead-chip-sector-higher-134336542.html
Chip stocks rebounded on Friday after suffering their worst sell-off since 2020. The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) bounced 4% following a 12% plunge on Thursday.
Shares of US chipmaker Intel (INTC) jumped about 7%, erasing part of their 10% slide in the prior session. AMD (AMD) also rebounded 11% after suffering a 17% fall. Nvidia (NVDA), which declined 9% in the prior session, jumped more than 2%.
Semiconductors bounced back after much of the AI trade was hammered on Thursday as investors digested what a Democratic win in Congress means for the data center build-out in the US.
Memory and storage names Sandisk (SNDK), Micron Technology (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) also rebounded.
Other notable movers rebounding on Friday include processor maker Qualcomm (QCOM) and chip designer Arm Holdings (ARM).

item.title: US worker productivity surges in third quarter
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
US worker productivity surges in third quarter
2026-11-06
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/us-worker-productivity-surges-third-140218233.html
WASHINGTON, Nov 5 (Reuters) - US worker productivity grew faster than expected in the third quarter, depressing labor costs and supporting views that the labor market was not a source of inflation.
Nonfarm productivity, which measures hourly output per worker, increased at a 3.6% annualized rate last quarter after advancing by an upwardly revised 2.1% pace in the April-June quarter, the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast productivity increasing at a 2.8% rate after a previously reported 1.4% growth pace in the second quarter.
Productivity is volatile on a quarter-on-quarter basis. It grew at a 2.1% rate from a year ago. Economists and policymakers are hoping that an artificial intelligence spending blitz will translate into significant productivity gains.
Unit labor costs — the price of labor per single unit of output — fell at a 0.7% rate last quarter. That was the first decline since the second quarter of 2025 and followed an upwardly revised 1.9% growth pace in the second quarter.
Economists had forecast labor costs rising at a 0.6% pace after growing at a previously reported 1.2% rate. Labor costs grew at a 2.4% rate from a year ago.
They followed on the heels of data last week showing a moderate increase in the Employment Cost Index, the broadest measure of labor costs, in the third quarter.
Policymakers and economists have argued that the jobs market was not a source of inflation. Benign wage inflation gives the Federal Reserve more latitude to focus on rising price pressures stemming from the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran.
The US central bank last week left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated." Economists expect the Fed to raise borrowing costs in December.
(Reporting by Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

Unit labor costs — the price of labor per single unit of output — fell at a 0.7% rate last quarter. That was the first decline since the second quarter of 2025 and followed an upwardly revised 1.9% growth pace in the second quarter.
Economists had forecast labor costs rising at a 0.6% pace after growing at a previously reported 1.2% rate. Labor costs grew at a 2.4% rate from a year ago.
They followed on the heels of data last week showing a moderate increase in the Employment Cost Index, the broadest measure of labor costs, in the third quarter.
Policymakers and economists have argued that the jobs market was not a source of inflation. Benign wage inflation gives the Federal Reserve more latitude to focus on rising price pressures stemming from the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran.
The US central bank last week left its benchmark overnight interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated." Economists expect the Fed to raise borrowing costs in December.
(Reporting by Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

item.title: JPMorgan says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh needs to spend more time with Congress to keep his gig
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
JPMorgan says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh needs to spend more time with Congress to keep his gig
2026-11-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/jpmorgan-says-fed-chair-kevin-warsh-needs-to-spend-more-time-with-congress-to-keep-his-gig-131703650.html
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh may want to restructure his calendar for 2027 to schedule one fewer call with the president and spend less time on executive-level thinking about which committee he wants to create next.
In place of all this, Warsh should spend more time walking the halls of Congress chatting up newly elected Democratic members of Congress if he doesn't want to be a one-term Fed chair, the team at JPMorgan said in a spicy new hot take.
"Chair Warsh's term as Fed chair ends in May 2030," JPMorgan strategist Michael Feroli said. "While there's another election between now and then, last night [Election Day] increased the odds his term will end with Democratic control of the Senate. Unless he wants to be a one-term chair, Warsh will need to spend less time looking out the window and more time walking the halls of Congress."
"In fact," Feroli added, "this was one of the few pieces of advice Powell publicly gave to his successor: 'Our window into democratic accountability is Congress. And it's not a passive burden for us to go to Congress and talk to people. It's an affirmative, regular obligation.'"
Warsh — appointed by President Trump — assumed the Fed chair position in May, and brought with him a grand plan to overhaul Fed policy.
He quickly made waves at his inaugural June FOMC meeting by slashing forward guidance and shortening the Fed's rate decision statement.
His first signature policy move came in September, when he orchestrated a 25 basis point interest rate hike to take the federal funds target range to 3.75% to 4%.
Read more: What experts say about the possibility of additional rate cuts
Following the Fed's October hold on interest rates, Warsh delivered a resolute message to global markets, vowing that the Fed will achieve its 2% price stability mandate with "no ifs, ands, or buts."

item.title: Mortgage rates dropped again, helped by the tech stock rout and post-election trades
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
Mortgage rates dropped again, helped by the tech stock rout and post-election trades
2026-11-06
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/mortgage-rates-dropped-again-helped-by-the-tech-stock-rout-and-post-election-trades-170000027.html
Mortgage rates drifted down for the third consecutive week, following Treasury yields lower as investors sought safe-haven assets and began assessing the market implications of the Democratic Party's overwhelming victories in the midterm elections.
The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage was 7.18% this week through Wednesday, according to Freddie Mac data, down from 7.24% a week earlier.
The ongoing rout in technology stocks helped push the 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates closely track, lower this week as investors fled into a traditional safe-haven asset. Yields dropped again on Wednesday, alongside oil prices, as investors grew hopeful that the Democrats' strong midterm showing may usher in a faster resolution to the Iran War, new restrictions on data center spending and development, and lower inflation.
A number of factors, from oil prices to AI spending to US fiscal policy, have helped push mortgage rates above 7% this year. It's unclear if, or when, those pressures will ease.
"Whether the forces keeping bond yields elevated — government deficits, geopolitical impacts on prices, and corporate borrowing to fund AI spending — could sustainably fade remains an open question," Kara Ng, senior economist at Zillow, said in a statement. The listings giant sees mortgage rates staying above 7% for the rest of this year and through mid-2027.
There are few signs that slightly lower rates are bringing buyers off the sidelines. Mortgage applications for home purchases declined 2% in the week through Friday from a week earlier, according to Mortgage Bankers Association data, while refinancing applications were nearly flat.
"Prospective borrowers may be holding off decisions until rates and economic and political conditions settle," MBA president and CEO Bob Broeksmit said in a statement.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Voters this week ‘showed their support for taxing the rich’ in spite of the likely failure of a billionaire's wealth tax in California
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Voters this week ‘showed their support for taxing the rich’ in spite of the likely failure of a billionaire's wealth tax in California
2026-11-06
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/tax-the-rich-won-in-ballot-measures-across-the-us-153106669.html
Voters weighed in on tax ballot initiatives across at least 10 states in the midterm elections, returning verdicts that reflected a strong "tax the rich" sentiment despite the likely failure of California's high-profile plan for a wealth tax.
Other successful measures sought to limit taxes on Americans of more modest means either through new caps on state income taxes or lower property taxes.
Voters' affordability worries ran, "at least in part, through the tax code," as the Tax Foundation summarized the results in a wrap-up of the races.
In California, a billionaire tax imposing a one-time 5% wealth tax on state residents and trusts with assets over $1 billion appeared on track to fail, after voters cooled on the effort as the campaign wound down.
But proponents of other taxes on the rich counted plenty of wins, including elsewhere on California's ballot.
The state's voters approved permanently higher tax rates on incomes starting at $250,000 in a separate measure that solidified rates first approved in 2012 to fund education.
Elsewhere in the US, a "millionaires tax" in Washington state survived, with 58% of voters rejecting a proposal to repeal a new 9.9% tax on individual and household wage income above $1 million per year to fund education, healthcare, and other priorities beginning in 2028.
Colorado is on track to narrowly pass a measure to raise taxes on its richest residents. That initiative aims to raise rates on incomes above $500,000 and tops out at 8.4% for incomes over $1 million.
"In three of four cases, voters showed their support for taxing the rich," the left-leaning Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy said in an analysis of state tax ballot measures, calling it a win for tax fairness.
(The California wealth tax initiative and the Colorado measures had not been formally called by the Associated Press as of Friday, so the results could change.)
A range of measures to limit taxes
Elsewhere in the nation, voters put a cap on future tax increases.
North Carolina voted to permanently cap state income taxes at 3.5% and approved a second measure to limit property taxes imposed at the local level.
Iowa approved its own measure that sets a higher threshold for lawmakers to approve future tax hikes. Utah approved a similar measure making it harder for future voters in the state to raise taxes through ballot initiatives.
Florida voters moved on housing costs and approved a phased-in $250,000 homestead exemption to limit property taxes except those used to fund public schools.

item.title: Oil bounces after its worst 3-day drop since 2021, but energy stocks aren't joining in
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Oil bounces after its worst 3-day drop since 2021, but energy stocks aren't joining in
2026-11-06
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-bounces-after-its-worst-3-day-drop-since-2021-but-energy-stocks-arent-joining-in-184905541.html
Almost everything on Wall Street was in the red Thursday, but oil was one of the few exceptions. WTI crude (CL=F) rose about 3% after its worst three-day drop since late 2021, and energy stocks didn't join the bounce.
WTI futures fell 15% from their Oct. 30 settle above $104 to a Nov. 4 settle near $88, the lowest since Aug. 31. The steepest leg came Nov. 4, after Democrats won control of Congress and Vice President JD Vance posted on X, "The reason we lost is the war."
It's been the pattern all year.
Oil and the S&P 500 (^GSPC) have moved in opposite directions more often in 2026 than in any year since at least 2001, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. The correlation between their daily moves is -0.44, where -1 would mean they always move in opposite directions. The previous low was -0.25 in 2003, the year the US invaded Iraq.
With the Iran war driving crude, rising oil has been bad news for stocks, and falling oil good news. On Nov. 4, the S&P 500 rose more than 1.5% as crude fell more than 8%. Thursday ran in reverse.
Energy stocks didn't play along. The Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) fell 3% to its lowest close since Sept. 30, as Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX) slipped about 2% and Baker Hughes (BKR) and Williams (WMB) fell with the market.
XLE is still 2026's best-performing sector, up about 40% this year, but it has fallen 12% from its Oct. 30 high in four sessions.
Crude still carries plenty of war premium. WTI is up more than 50% this year, and Iran's crude exports "have fallen from roughly 1.8 million barrels per day to essentially zero," Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote in a Nov. 4 note. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)
Washington's appetite for the war may count for more than any level.
"The vice president probably is speaking for at least a good portion of the Republican caucus," Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, said on Yahoo Finance's morning show Thursday. "JD Vance said the quiet part out loud."
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

item.title: Chip stocks slaughtered as Wall Street suffers worst post-midterm day since 1896
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Chip stocks slaughtered as Wall Street suffers worst post-midterm day since 1896
2026-11-06
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/chip-stocks-slaughtered-as-wall-street-suffers-worst-post-midterm-day-since-1896-213204256.html
Wall Street's midterm celebration lasted one day. Chip stocks got taken to the woodshed Thursday, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 3.4%, its worst second session after a midterm election in data going back to its start in 1896.
It took the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) six minutes to erase its entire post-election rally. Then the selling got worse.
The tech-heavy index closed down 5.5%, and the S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4%. It was the worst day for both since the April 2025 tariff crash.
Investors bought stocks Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, helped by falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields. Thursday, the focus shifted to what a Democratic Congress could mean for the AI build-out, and in particular for the data centers driving it.
It was also the S&P 500's worst second day after a midterm in data going back nearly a century. The previous low came in 2002, when the index fell about 2.3%.
This week has an echo from 1896. The day after William McKinley won the White House that November, the Dow jumped about 4.5%, then gave back about 2% the next session. On Wednesday, the Dow jumped 3%, its best day after a midterm since 1982.
The Nasdaq-100 (^NDX), in correction territory since Monday, fell 6.4% for its worst day since March 2020. The broader Nasdaq Composite joined it, closing nearly 12% below its Oct. 6 record. Both indexes also closed below their 200-day moving averages for the first time since April. Many traders treat that line as the boundary between an uptrend and a downtrend.
The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) sank 12%, its worst day since March 2020, leaving it about 38% below its June record.
The S&P 500 shed about $3 trillion in market value. Nvidia (NVDA) alone lost about $450 billion, and chipmakers as a group gave up more than $1.5 trillion.

item.content:encoded:
Chip stocks slaughtered as Wall Street suffers worst post-midterm day since 1896

2026-11-06

Por Jared Blikre

https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/chip-stocks-slaughtered-as-wall-street-suffers-worst-post-midterm-day-since-1896-213204256.html

Wall Street's midterm celebration lasted one day. Chip stocks got taken to the woodshed Thursday, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) fell 3.4%, its worst second session after a midterm election in data going back to its start in 1896.

It took the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) six minutes to erase its entire post-election rally. Then the selling got worse.

The tech-heavy index closed down 5.5%, and the S&P 500 (^GSPC) lost 4.4%. It was the worst day for both since the April 2025 tariff crash.

Investors bought stocks Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, helped by falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields. Thursday, the focus shifted to what a Democratic Congress could mean for the AI build-out, and in particular for the data centers driving it.

It was also the S&P 500's worst second day after a midterm in data going back nearly a century. The previous low came in 2002, when the index fell about 2.3%.

This week has an echo from 1896. The day after William McKinley won the White House that November, the Dow jumped about 4.5%, then gave back about 2% the next session. On Wednesday, the Dow jumped 3%, its best day after a midterm since 1982.

The Nasdaq-100 (^NDX), in correction territory since Monday, fell 6.4% for its worst day since March 2020. The broader Nasdaq Composite joined it, closing nearly 12% below its Oct. 6 record. Both indexes also closed below their 200-day moving averages for the first time since April. Many traders treat that line as the boundary between an uptrend and a downtrend.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) sank 12%, its worst day since March 2020, leaving it about 38% below its June record.

The S&P 500 shed about $3 trillion in market value. Nvidia (NVDA) alone lost about $450 billion, and chipmakers as a group gave up more than $1.5 trillion.

Memory and storage stocks took the worst of it, with SanDisk (SNDK), Western Digital (WDC), Seagate (STX), and Micron (MU) all suffering steep double-digit losses. AMD (AMD), Marvell (MRVL), Arm (ARM), and Lam Research (LRCX) fell sharply too. Even the biggest names, Nvidia, Broadcom (AVGO), and Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM), fell 9% or more.

The damage spread across the AI supply chain. Cloud provider Nebius (NBIS) fell double digits and CoreWeave (CRWV) nearly 10%, along with networking and optical names Astera Labs (ALAB), Lumentum (LITE), Coherent (COHR), Dell (DELL), Corning (GLW), and Quanta Services (PWR).

Speculative favorites went down with them. Tesla (TSLA), SpaceX (SPCX), Robinhood (HOOD), Coinbase (COIN), and Strategy (MSTR) each fell 9% or more. (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)

item.title: 'Pretty solid job growth:' Private US employers added 86,000 jobs in October
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
'Pretty solid job growth:' Private US employers added 86,000 jobs in October
2026-11-06
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/pretty-solid-job-growth-private-us-employers-added-86000-jobs-in-october-140029435.html
Hiring in the private sector showed continued strength in October, according to payroll processor ADP, as employers across a variety of industries added roles.
Private companies added 86,000 jobs this month, matching a revised 86,000 in September, data released Wednesday showed. Economists had been expecting a gain of 67,000 jobs.
Base wages for private-sector workers rose 3.2%, a figure that still trails inflation, while gross pay, which includes additional compensation such as overtime and bonuses, was up 4.7%.
"You have back-to-back, two consecutive straight months of pretty solid job growth," ADP chief economist Nela Richardson said.
Gains in healthcare and education continue to be major drivers of hiring, with the sectors adding 28,000 jobs last month. Showing even more strength was the category of trade, transportation, and utilities, with 39,000 additions.
But there are still spots of weakness within the job market. Business services shed 27,000 roles, and information lost 2,000 jobs, a sign of ongoing challenges in certain white-collar industries.
The ADP report covers private-sector hiring and comes out ahead of the Labor Department's broader survey data on public and private employers on Friday. Economists expect the economy added 65,000 jobs in October by that measure.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: AI’s circular financing is a ‘feature,’ not a bug, Wall Street’s elite bond committee tells Treasury
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
AI’s circular financing is a ‘feature,’ not a bug, Wall Street’s elite bond committee tells Treasury
2026-11-06
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/ais-circular-financing-is-a-feature-not-a-bug-wall-streets-elite-bond-committee-tells-treasury-155811224.html
AI's circular financing is a 'feature,' not a bug, Wall Street's elite bond committee tells Treasury
The cost of insuring AI borrowers' debt has jumped as much as 80% since August.
The government's top bond advisers say the money sloshing around the AI boom is built that way on purpose, and that it's mostly fine — at least for now.
The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee, a panel of big-bank and investor executives that advises Treasury on how the US borrows, made AI debt one of its two research topics this quarter. Its presentation, out Wednesday, sums up the view in one slide title: "Circular Financing is a feature."
That's the loop of chipmakers, cloud companies and their biggest customers funding one another. The committee's bet is that the hardware outlasts some of its buyers. "While some individual compute operators might not remain viable, the physical infrastructure will continue to find demand," the presentation said.
The bill is enormous. Tech's capital spending is headed for $1 trillion this year and $1.7 trillion in 2027, by the committee's count, far more than those businesses bring in. That leaves a hole of more than $600 billion next year, and about $735 billion of new tech debt to help fill it.
"The face of AI financing has just changed," Defiance ETFs CEO Sylvia Jablonski told Yahoo Finance on Wednesday. "It used to come from the balance sheet. And it can't do that anymore."
The weak links are paying up
The committee's fine print carries a warning: "The strength of the overall cohort should not obscure the vulnerabilities of individual borrowers."
Lenders seem to agree. Insuring Amazon's (AMZN) debt costs nearly 80% more than in early August, as its cash burn hits a record. Oracle (ORCL) and CoreWeave (CRWV) are up about 50%, against roughly 20% to 25% for the broader bond market.
Oracle's insurance now costs more than at any point in the 2008 financial crisis, after it borrowed another $10 billion. CoreWeave's price implies about a 60% chance of default within five years, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Washington isn't feeling the squeeze yet. "Treasury auction results show no evidence that 2026 technology-related issuance has crowded out long-end Treasury demand," the committee told Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.
But the two are fishing in the same pond. Treasury is borrowing short-term, so insurers and pensions hunting for long-term bonds are buying corporate debt. "When the government issues short and companies issue long, the investors who need duration most will go where the duration is," Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote last week. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

That's the loop of chipmakers, cloud companies and their biggest customers funding one another. The committee's bet is that the hardware outlasts some of its buyers. item.title: SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
SpaceX inks Qualcomm deal, putting Starlink closer to becoming the fourth major US wireless carrier
2026-11-06
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/spacex-inks-qualcomm-deal-putting-starlink-closer-to-becoming-the-fourth-major-us-wireless-carrier-133000731.html
SpaceX's (SPCX) goal of turning its Starlink service into a major US mobile carrier is one step closer to becoming a reality.
On Wednesday, Qualcomm (QCOM) announced that SpaceX has selected its Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure platforms to power Starlink Mobile's nationwide terrestrial 5G cellular network.
Starlink already has the largest satellite-based network, and the ground-based stations will allow it to better compete with AT&T (T), T-Mobile (TMUS), and Verizon (VZ).
Last month, the company announced an agreement to purchase licenses for 800 MHz spectrum.
"While Starlink Mobile's global 2 GHz mid-band spectrum will provide high-bandwidth capacity in the United States, this new low-band spectrum will provide a coverage layer that ensures Starlink Mobile's signal penetrates through obstacles, such as walls, and can provide service to customers' devices even when they are in buildings," the company said at the time.
According to Qualcomm, the new deal will allow both companies to begin deploying advanced 5G service and provide "an opportunity to lay the foundation for AI-native 6G in the years ahead."
The company says the effort will require SpaceX to deploy its chip technology across tens of thousands of cellular towers nationwide.
"Our agreement with SpaceX is structured in such a way that as the deployment begins, starting from next year, it's going to ramp up pretty rapidly from there onwards," said Durga Malladi, EVP and GM for technology planning, edge solutions, and data center at Qualcomm.
"So it's a multi-year agreement that we have with them in terms of the deployment capability as we ramp up all the way to nationwide coverage," he added.
Earlier this month, The Washington Post reported that SpaceX was in talks with EchoStar (ECHO) to operate its own carrier through EchoStar's Boost Mobile brand.
The company made the move after AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon reportedly rejected its requests to use their network capacity through a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) deal.
An MVNO rents capacity from existing carriers and sells it under its own branding. But an operator like Starlink Mobile could prove a particularly potent challenger to the Big Three network carriers, leaving them little incentive to work with Elon Musk's firm.

item.title: ‘The money has to come from somewhere’: Florida voters approve sweeping property tax cut, while tax revolts in Wyoming and Oklahoma fall short
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
‘The money has to come from somewhere’: Florida voters approve sweeping property tax cut, while tax revolts in Wyoming and Oklahoma fall short
2026-11-06
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/the-money-has-to-come-from-somewhere-florida-voters-approve-sweeping-property-tax-cut-while-tax-revolts-in-wyoming-and-oklahoma-fall-short-184002359.html
'The money has to come from somewhere': Florida voters approve sweeping property tax cut, while tax revolts in Wyoming and Oklahoma fall short
Voters in seven states weighed in on property tax relief measures on Tuesday, part of an ongoing property tax revolt that has developed in recent years as home prices and assessed values soared while incomes have largely failed to keep up. The outcomes were mixed, with voters in Florida and North Carolina overwhelmingly approving amendments designed to cut or cap taxes, while Wyoming and Oklahoma voters rejected tax-limiting measures.
The split results reflect the complicated trade-offs between limiting unpopular and fast-rising taxes and funding public services.
"Property tax bills are rising far faster than inflation and even home valuations," said Nicole Fox, a policy analyst at the Tax Foundation. "People are noticing."
Read more: Democrats win Congress, eye healthcare, tariffs, and Trump's allies
The most sweeping effort to lower taxes came in Florida, where 62% of voters approved a major property tax cut that will increase the amount of a home's value that can be exempted from non-school homestead property taxes, effectively eliminating those taxes entirely in some parts of the state.
"What happened last night was a really big deal," said Danielle Blake, chief of residential and advocacy at Miami Realtors, which supported the Florida initiative, known as Amendment 3. "That is the voters speaking loud and clear that they want relief."
In North Carolina, an amendment requiring the General Assembly to pass legislation limiting how much local governments can raise property tax revenues from year to year passed with over 60% of the vote. And Louisiana voters approved ballot initiatives designed to provide property tax relief to select groups, including seniors.
But in Oklahoma, voters rejected a ballot question that sought to limit the growth in property tax assessment limits. A Wyoming amendment that would have cut property taxes by 50% for most homes also failed after critics, including the state's governor, argued that the cuts would decimate local services.
Municipalities across the country rely heavily on property taxes, which account for 70% or more of local revenues. Those taxes frequently fund popular services like infrastructure, parks, and public safety. Cutting them can mean municipalities must find another way to cover the shortfall or reduce services.
"If you eliminate [property taxes], the money has to come from somewhere else, or the service gets eliminated," said Bill Healey, 2026 president of the International Association of Assessing Officers.

https://finance.yahoo.com/real-estate/article/the-money-has-to-come-from-somewhere-florida-voters-approve-sweeping-property-tax-cut-while-tax-revolts-in-wyoming-and-oklahoma-fall-short-184002359.html

'The money has to come from somewhere': Florida voters approve sweeping property tax cut, while tax revolts in Wyoming and Oklahoma fall short

Voters in seven states weighed in on property tax relief measures on Tuesday, part of an ongoing property tax revolt that has developed in recent years as home prices and assessed values soared while incomes have largely failed to keep up. The outcomes were mixed, with voters in Florida and North Carolina overwhelmingly approving amendments designed to cut or cap taxes, while Wyoming and Oklahoma voters rejected tax-limiting measures.

The split results reflect the complicated trade-offs between limiting unpopular and fast-rising taxes and funding public services.

"Property tax bills are rising far faster than inflation and even home valuations," said Nicole Fox, a policy analyst at the Tax Foundation. "People are noticing."

Read more: Democrats win Congress, eye healthcare, tariffs, and Trump's allies

The most sweeping effort to lower taxes came in Florida, where 62% of voters approved a major property tax cut that will increase the amount of a home's value that can be exempted from non-school homestead property taxes, effectively eliminating those taxes entirely in some parts of the state.

"What happened last night was a really big deal," said Danielle Blake, chief of residential and advocacy at Miami Realtors, which supported the Florida initiative, known as Amendment 3. "That is the voters speaking loud and clear that they want relief."

In North Carolina, an amendment requiring the General Assembly to pass legislation limiting how much local governments can raise property tax revenues from year to year passed with over 60% of the vote. And Louisiana voters approved ballot initiatives designed to provide property tax relief to select groups, including seniors.

But in Oklahoma, voters rejected a ballot question that sought to limit the growth in property tax assessment limits. A Wyoming amendment that would have cut property taxes by 50% for most homes also failed after critics, including the state's governor, argued that the cuts would decimate local services.

Municipalities across the country rely heavily on property taxes, which account for 70% or more of local revenues. Those taxes frequently fund popular services like infrastructure, parks, and public safety. Cutting them can mean municipalities must find another way to cover the shortfall or reduce services.

"If you eliminate [property taxes], the money has to come from somewhere else, or the service gets eliminated," said Bill Healey, 2026 president of the International Association of Assessing Officers.

item.author: Ivana Pino
item.description:
I bonds now pay 5.51%: What to know before you buy
2026-11-06
Por Ivana Pino
https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/investing/article/i-bonds-now-pay-551-what-to-know-before-you-buy-161812462.html

Government-backed Series I bonds now pay higher interest, 5.51% annual interest through April 30, up from 4.26% — is now the time to lock in?
With everyday costs trending upward, many savers may be looking for ways to inflation-proof their wallets — including their savings.
The latest Consumer Price Index showed prices climbed in September, up 3.7% from a year earlier, with gasoline driving more than half of the increase.
One way to hedge against inflation: explore alternative savings options.
Read more: 6 ways investors and savers can stay ahead of inflation
What is a Series I bond?
Series I bonds are government-backed savings bonds tied to inflation. Each bond is issued at face value with a 30-year final maturity, consisting of a 20-year original maturity period immediately followed by a 10-year extended maturity period.
The bond's composite rate, or earnings rate, has a two-part structure: a fixed rate and an inflation rate. The fixed rate stays the same for the duration of your bond's term, while the inflation rate can change every six months.
I savings bonds earn interest monthly, and that interest is compounded semiannually.
Read more: I bonds are back: Why the new 5.51% rate is so attractive
Another benefit of these bonds is that, while they are subject to federal income tax, they are exempt from state and local income tax. Savers can choose whether to report each year's earnings or report their earnings all at once when they cash out their bond. Additionally, if you choose to use your money for qualified higher education expenses, you may not have to shell out any tax on those earnings.
Series I savings bonds issued between Nov. 1, 2026, and April 30, 2027, are currently offering a composite rate of 5.51%, with a 1.40% fixed rate.
Savers can buy I bonds electronically for as little as $25, up to $10,000 per calendar year, through a TreasuryDirect account.
Read more: How to protect your savings against inflation
The case for buying now
Series I bonds can be an attractive savings vehicle during periods of rising inflation because the combined rate increases alongside inflation, giving savers a built-in hedge against rising prices.
These bonds are also currently offering yields that are well above national averages for other savings vehicles. The national average rate for a traditional savings account is only 0.38%. Money market accounts and certificates of deposit (CDs) offer slightly higher national average rates at 0.63% for money market accounts and 1.76% for a 12-month CD, but this is still significantly less than the going rate for a Series I bond.
If the inflation rate continues to rise, that could translate to even higher returns for bondholders. In 2022, Series I bonds reached rates as high as 9.62%. Unlike your average savings account or CD, investing in this kind of bond can offset the cost of rising inflation. However, this can be a double-edged sword. Because a portion of the rate is variable and tied to current inflation, the rate can fall significantly — sometimes to near zero — meaning your returns could end up being lower than other investments.
See also: Best high-yield savings accounts and Best CD rates
The downsides of Series I bonds
These bonds are not without drawbacks, and it's worth understanding the rules and limitations before committing.
These bonds come with a mandatory lockup period. This means that you cannot redeem an I bond for at least 12 months after the purchase date. If there's a chance you'll need to tap into those funds earlier, I bonds aren't the right fit.

item.title: Democrats won control of Congress. Their economic agenda is set to target healthcare, tariffs, and Trump's allies.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Democrats won control of Congress. Their economic agenda is set to target healthcare, tariffs, and Trump's allies.
2026-11-06
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/democrats-won-control-of-congress-their-economic-agenda-is-set-to-target-healthcare-tariffs-and-trumps-allies-052305694.html
Democrats retook power in Washington on Tuesday, flipping key House and Senate seats to command majorities in both chambers of Congress.
The power shift creates a new platform for Democrats to launch investigations of President Trump's economic allies — Elon Musk, to name one — and pass bills that may be unlikely to become law but will mark a sharp change in the political climate for business leaders and economic issues after two years of unified Republican control.
The change also appears set to elevate figures like Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren and others to prominent positions with oversight over economic policy.
Democrats are planning "a shock-and-awe legislative sprint," the New York Times reported, on issues like healthcare subsidies and Trump's tariffs, which could prompt a wave of bills to pass the House but stall against the 60-vote threshold in the Senate. Even in the minority, Senate rules mean Republicans retain the power to stop legislation.
Democrats are also likely to seek areas of bipartisan agreement on pharmaceuticals, the housing market, and AI data centers, all sectors that both Republicans and Democrats have spotlighted on the campaign trail.
Divided government, of course, may also set the stage for political clashes that could destabilize markets and the broader economy.
"While conventional wisdom suggests equities tend to rally following midterm elections, particularly when the outcome produces divided government, we caution that the post-election environment may look considerably different this cycle," Raymond James Washington Policy Analyst Ed Mills warned in a pre-election note.
He added that much of the recent volatility has been driven by unexpected moves from the White House. "We believe Trump will increasingly test the limits of executive authority during the remainder of his term," Mills wrote.
'Lawyer up': An expected focus on Elon Musk and Trump's economic team
He met with Democratic volunteers as Election Day wound down and told reporters, "We're relentlessly focused on driving down the high cost of living and fighting for an affordable America."
Going by early signals, Democrats intend to aim their new powers at an array of high-profile targets, with Musk chief among them, as part of a far-reaching effort to impose new checks on the Trump administration.
"Lawyer up," said Rep. Robert Garcia, who is poised to become chair of the House Oversight Committee, in one particularly pithy signal of the Democrats' plans.
Recent developments involving Elon Musk and Starlink in Ukraine are just the latest topic that Democrats say they will investigate around the world's richest man. The Wall Street Journal has reported that Musk ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of Starlink relied on by Ukraine and discussed the decision on a call with Trump in October.
A group of Silicon Valley lawmakers said in a letter the issue raises broader concerns and could lead them to "closely scrutinize federal funding awarded to Mr. Musk's businesses" in the next Congress.
Musk could also face questions about his role in the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) and SpaceX's other government contracts.
Trump this week said he would consider preemptively pardoning officials like Musk who face legal scrutiny from Democrats, saying in an interview, "I would if I needed to, sure. I wouldn't even think about it."
Capitol Hill observers are also expecting economic-themed clashes, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent potentially facing new scrutiny.
Politico recently reported that Democrats are planning to investigate the Treasury Department and the IRS, as well as Trump's actions to

item.title: Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
2026-11-06
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/democrats-victories-in-texas-laid-bare-voter-unease-over-data-centers--and-signal-new-hurdles-for-the-industry-142918051.html
Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
A strong showing by Democrats in Texas swept Gina Hinojosa into office as the state's first Democratic governor since 1990 in a contest closely watched by Big Tech companies.
Texas is considered a bellwether for government restrictions on AI data centers and was just one place where deep voter unease over the build-out was on display. Voters across the country passed a series of local ballot measures aimed at restricting construction in the years ahead.
Hinojosa, Texas's first Latina governor, has pledged to impose a moratorium on data center construction in Texas, which accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030.
"I want to say something to the powerful people who have gotten very comfortable running this state," she told supporters in her victory speech. "The voters have delivered a mandate for change, and it is change they will get."
Her victory was one of a series of wins for Democrats in Texas. The party is also on track to take control of the Texas House, which would give Hinojosa more power to follow through on restrictions even as the state Senate appears set to remain under Republican control.
"We view the Texas gubernatorial race as particularly important for the next leg of the AI trade," wrote Raymond James's Ed Mills in a pre-election note saying that a strong Democratic showing there "could signal a broader electoral wave while increasing concerns about data center moratoriums and more restrictive AI regulation in the nation's largest planned data center development."
Bank of America called the race "one of the highest impact elections for the entire utility sector."
A race that 'could make a real difference'
Hinojosa made opposition to data center construction a central part of her campaign, charging in one ad that Gov. Greg Abbott "works for" Elon Musk.
She staked out plans for a moratorium on new data center construction, stricter regulations on water and power usage, and an end to tax breaks.
Abbott was seeking his fourth term as governor and said last year he wanted Texas to be the "epicenter of AI development."
More recently, he announced a moratorium of his own and said he would support more stringent requirements on power and water usage. Hinojosa immediately charged that Abbott's new proposals amounted to an "election year pause."
Tobin Marcus of Wolfe Research said Texas "is the one state with enough scale and enough difference between the candidates that it could make a real difference."

item.itunes:summary:
Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
2026-11-06
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/democrats-victories-in-texas-laid-bare-voter-unease-over-data-centers--and-signal-new-hurdles-for-the-industry-142918051.html
Democrats' victories in Texas laid bare voter unease over data centers — and signal new hurdles for the industry
A strong showing by Democrats in Texas swept Gina Hinojosa into office as the state's first Democratic governor since 1990 in a contest closely watched by Big Tech companies.
Texas is considered a bellwether for government restrictions on AI data centers and was just one place where deep voter unease over the build-out was on display. Voters across the country passed a series of local ballot measures aimed at restricting construction in the years ahead.
Hinojosa, Texas's first Latina governor, has pledged to impose a moratorium on data center construction in Texas, which accounts for more than 25% of planned US capacity by 2030.
"I want to say something to the powerful people who have gotten very comfortable running this state," she told supporters in her victory speech. "The voters have delivered a mandate for change, and it is change they will get."
Her victory was one of a series of wins for Democrats in Texas. The party is also on track to take control of the Texas House, which would give Hinojosa more power to follow through on restrictions even as the state Senate appears set to remain under Republican control.
"We view the Texas gubernatorial race as particularly important for the next leg of the AI trade," wrote Raymond James's Ed Mills in a pre-election note saying that a strong Democratic showing there "could signal a broader electoral wave while increasing concerns about data center moratoriums and more restrictive AI regulation in the nation's largest planned data center development."
Bank of America called the race "one of the highest impact elections for the entire utility sector."
A race that 'could make a real difference'
Hinojosa made opposition to data center construction a central part of her campaign, charging in one ad that Gov. Greg Abbott "works for" Elon Musk.
She staked out plans for a moratorium on new data center construction, stricter regulations on water and power usage, and an end to tax breaks.
Abbott was seeking his fourth term as governor and said last year he wanted Texas to be the "epicenter of AI development."
More recently, he announced a moratorium of his own and said he would support more stringent requirements on power and water usage. Hinojosa immediately charged that Abbott's new proposals amounted to an "election year pause."
Tobin Marcus of Wolfe Research said Texas "is the one state with enough scale and enough difference between the candidates that it could make a real difference."

item.title: Oil’s war premium is leaking out fast — and the midterms just sped it up
item.author: Jared Blikre
item.description:
Oil’s war premium is leaking out fast — and the midterms just sped it up
2026-11-06
Por Jared Blikre
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/oil-prices-fall-below-90-as-traders-bet-on-iran-war-ending-after-democrats-sweep-midterms-192105228.html
Wall Street's post-midterm party has two no-shows: AI and chip stocks, and oil. Crude is having the far worse time, on track for its worst week since April 2020.
West Texas Intermediate crude (CL=F) settled at $88.12 a barrel on Wednesday, down more than 8% on the day and $16 below Friday's close of $104. Its three-day drop of about 15% is its steepest since November 2021.
Brent (BZ=F), the global benchmark, is near a two-month low. The sell-off came as traders bet on an end to the Iran war after Democrats swept Tuesday's elections.
"The election results may pressure the president to seek to end the war more quickly," the Wells Fargo Investment Institute wrote Wednesday.
Read more: How oil price shocks ripple through your wallet, from gas to groceries
The damage is spreading beyond crude. Gasoline futures (RB=F) are on track for their lowest close since March 10, which is good news for anyone driving to Thanksgiving dinner. The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) is down more than 5%. Refiners Marathon Petroleum (MPC) and Valero (VLO) are down about 8% to 10%.
Even after the slide, oil hasn't given back the whole war. WTI started 2026 near $57 and peaked near $113 on April 7, and it's still roughly 50% above where the year began.
The election angle adds some history. Oil hasn't followed a single script after Trump's elections. Crude rose about 10% from Election Day through the end of November after his 2016 win and about 20% after his 2020 loss, and it fell about 6% after his 2024 win.
The closest echo is 2018, Trump's first midterm, when Democrats took the House. Crude fell about 18% from Election Day through the end of that November, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Supply hasn't caught up with the peace trade. US diesel stockpiles are at their lowest since 2003, and Wells Fargo noted that gasoline and diesel supplies "remain constrained by the war."
That leaves crude priced for a deal that hasn't happened. Nationwide's chief market strategist, Mark Hackett, says oil is retreating "on hopes for a deescalation in the Iran conflict, even as the diplomatic signals remain ambiguous."

item.title: Big Tech Stocks Soar as Traders Bet Democrats Will Slow AI Spend
item.author: Jeran Wittenstein; Ryan Vlastelica
item.description:
Big Tech Stocks Soar as Traders Bet Democrats Will Slow AI Spend
2026-11-06
Por Jeran Wittenstein; Ryan Vlastelica
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/big-tech-stocks-soar-traders-170754816.html
(Bloomberg) -- The shares of US technology giants led the market higher on Wednesday as investors bet that a Democrat-controlled Congress will slow the massive spending on artificial intelligence that's eating up free cash flow.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Amazon.com Inc. was up as much as 8.3%, Microsoft Corp. gained 7%, Alphabet Inc. jumped 5.9% and Meta Platforms Inc. advanced 3.6%. Together with Apple Inc., which has avoided heavy AI spending and leaped more than 6%, the five tech behemoths are on pace to add nearly $1 trillion in market value on Wednesday.
Democrats secured majorities in both the House and Senate in Tuesday's election, flipping seats in Republican bastions including South Carolina, Texas and Kansas, and winning down-ballot votes as well to secure control of numerous statehouses and governors' mansions. The party's candidates ran heavily on slowing down AI development, in particular checking the mass construction of data centers required to run the burgeoning technology.
"The market is acting like this represents the end of the AI buildout," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth Management. "If that means the hyperscalers aren't spending ridiculous amounts of money to build out compute, that means they could become cash-flow positive again."
Exit polls showed that voters strongly oppose new data centers in their communities, Keith Parker, UBS's head of global macro equity strategy and US equity strategy research, wrote in a note to clients on Wednesday. "The blue wave will have implications for equities, with the biggest impact likely coming from an increase in data center regulation at the state level near-term," he wrote.
Shares of Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta have been under pressure recently as investors grow increasingly concerned that the hundreds of billions of dollars they're spending on computing infrastructure won't generate sufficient returns. Meanwhile, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta have all seen their free cash flows turn negative, meaning they're spending more on capital expenditures than they're generating from their operations. As a result, the firms are being forced to use the debt and equity markets to fund their spending.

item.title: Why the stock market is unexpectedly rallying in the wake of the Democratic blue wave
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
Why the stock market is unexpectedly rallying in the wake of the Democratic blue wave
2026-11-06
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/why-the-stock-market-is-unexpectedly-rallying-in-the-wake-of-the-democratic-blue-wave-152956959.html
Call it a contrarian move. It has been a riveting 12 hours or so in the markets as investors slice and dice the midterm election outcomes.
Initially, stocks got hammered as the results trickled in. The thinking was that Democrats are less pro-business than Republicans, and since they will control the House and the Senate, there goes the corporate profit miracle that has driven the markets over the past two years.
But something very interesting has emerged after that initial knee-jerk reaction. Stocks are rallying on Wednesday — big-time!
Here are three reasons I think we're seeing this play out.
The AI readthrough
First, the midterm election results threaten to significantly disrupt AI data center expansion as voter backlash over soaring utility bills, grid instability, and water usage drive a sharp political pivot toward tighter regulatory oversight. That is being viewed as a positive for hyperscalers such as Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) in that they will be forced to pull back on spending, which would boost free cash flow.
Free cash flow declines have been at the heart of the latest AI stock sell-off, so if cash flow outlooks brighten up at the biggest companies driving the market, all the better.
Bye-bye uncertainty
Second, with the elections over, the cloud of uncertainty that had begun to seep into markets in recent weeks has been lifted. Now investors can better place their chips where they see fit.
As the team at the Stocktrader's Almanac pointed out, six months after the past 19 midterm elections, the S&P 500 (^GSPC) has been higher 100% of the time, with an average gain of 14.18%.
Eyes on corporate profits
Third, there is this callout by Goldman Sachs strategist Jan Hatzius today that also gets to the heart of this day-after rally.
Hatzius wrote: "The larger-than-expected majorities could give them slightly greater leverage in negotiations with the White House, but will also dilute the influence of small factions within the Democratic caucus. We expect Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to seek to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs, and reverse spending cuts enacted last year."
I read that as a pro-corporate bottom line.

item.title: US Treasury Borrows Record $839 Billion in Single Week
item.author: Elizabeth Stanton
item.description:
US Treasury Borrows Record $839 Billion in Single Week
2026-11-06
Por Elizabeth Stanton
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/us-treasury-borrows-record-839-201757901.html
(Bloomberg) -- The US government borrowed a record $839 billion in a single week via its sales of Treasury bills and notes — both to repay holders of maturing debt and to raise the additional capital needed to finance the federal deficit.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Auctions of bills, floating-rate notes and Treasuries due in two, five and seven years conducted from Oct. 26-30 eclipsed the previous weekly record of $795 billion, set in the same period a year ago, according to Tony Farren, managing director in rates sales and trading at Mischler Financial Group.
The $839 billion is the sum of the 11 auction sizes, and the majority of it went to repay holders of maturing bills. Only $68 billion represented new borrowing by the US government, and it's not close to record levels. Those were set in March and April 2020, when auction sizes surged to finance pandemic response measures, and weekly net new cash peaked at levels around $350 billion.
Gross weekly debt totals vary widely depending mainly on how much debt is slated to mature. This week's record total underscores how the accumulated debt — and the rising cost of financing it — is driving the US government toward ever-larger auction sizes.
"Nothing good is coming from Treasury gross weekly issuance at a record high," Farren said. "The No. 1 risk is that people are going to demand higher yields."
Over the past two years, the Treasury Department has met growth in its borrowing need by increasing the size of its weekly bill auctions, while maintaining the sizes of its seven monthly auctions of notes and bonds with maturities ranging from two to 30 years.
That will have to change eventually — or else risk bills growing as a share of the total debt, which exposes US taxpayers to rising interest rates because bills mature more frequently. Since early 2024, the Treasury's quarterly policy statements have said it expects to keep auction sizes steady "for at least the next several quarters." Bond market strategists expect that guidance to change when the next statement is made on Nov. 4.
(Corrects amount of previous record in second paragraph and new borrowing amount in third paragraph of story originally published on Oct. 30, before the release of the Treasury quarterly policy statement.)
